screening_results.reason: This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=30, mean age 26) that uses a social-related body perception task probing perception and understanding of self and others. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation analyses (FEAT/FLAME) with thresholded Z-statistic maps and coordinate results for contrasts (e.g., own body > scrambled; same-sex and opposite-sex other bodies) clearly from the healthy/control sample. Analyses include within-group and between-sex comparisons and parametric whole-brain results. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, and fits the review’s constructs (Perception/Understanding of Self and Others). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (understanding others’ regret) involving healthy adult participants (two samples of N=24, ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM5; contrasts IP−IF and OP−OF; parametric and conjunction analyses; thresholding and reported activation foci/coordinates), not limited to ROI, connectivity-only, or clinical groups. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described in the text and figures/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Although the study includes a healthy adult control group (N=24, ages 19–36) and uses task fMRI of social processing, the reported results are primarily between-group contrasts and ROI analyses. The paper does not present a clear, unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map or contrast explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Whole-brain figures and tables focus on group interactions and BPD>HC or HC>BPD contrasts; the amygdala result is an ROI finding. Because the review requires at least one healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (reported as HC task effect or within-group contrast), this study does not meet that inclusion criterion.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) Uses task-based fMRI to investigate perception of social interactions (social communication / perception of others). (2) Sample = 21 healthy adults (ages 18–35) with results reported for the healthy group. (3) Whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (whole-brain beta maps, group-level t-tests, and whole-brain searchlight analyses are described), providing voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy sample. The study is empirical and not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: N=50, ages 19–34; Experiment 2: N=23, ages 18–30). The task probes perception/understanding of others (observed social interactions), satisfying the social-related construct. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., social interaction > independent actions) with FDR-corrected clusters and surface-based group analyses, clearly from the healthy/control sample. It is empirical fMRI work (not ROI-only, not resting-state), and reports whole-brain results; therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=25, mean age 25.1) investigating social-related processing (learning about others’ preference similarity to self—affiliation/social cognition). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected activations, peak MNI coordinates, conjunction analyses) rather than only ROI or connectivity analyses. Healthy participants’ whole-brain task contrasts and parametric modulators are clearly described and reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state, participants are within 18–65). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

While this is an fMRI study of social processing (Cyberball) in adult participants (mean age ~19.8) and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps (EX–IN and SUP–EX), the reported whole-brain results are for the entire sample (46 participants), which includes 9 participants meeting criteria for social anxiety disorder. The paper does not present a clearly identified whole-brain group-level task activation map coming specifically from a healthy/control-only group. The review’s eligibility rules require that if clinical participants are included, results for the healthy group must be reported separately (or a whole-brain healthy/control map must be clearly identified). Because that criterion is not met, the study must be excluded.

Although the study uses task fMRI with healthy adult controls and addresses social-affective processing, it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. Analyses are based on predefined network nodes and sliding-window network cohesion indices (ROI/network-level connectivity) and comparisons of these NCI time series; no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation maps or voxelwise contrasts are presented. This falls under the exclusion criterion for studies reporting only ROI/network or connectivity analyses without whole-brain task activation results. Therefore it fails the ‘whole-brain evidence’ inclusion criterion.

The study used task-based fMRI of a social-related paradigm (peer-oriented social judgment assessing acceptance/rejection), meeting the construct of social reward/processing. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=20; mean age ~28) and reports within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts for the control group (acceptance>control and rejection>control). Analyses were whole-brain (SPM8) with cluster-based correction and results for the healthy/control group are described in the text and figures. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only, resting-state, or connectivity-only, and reports unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activations. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of action observation and weight-discrimination (perception/understanding of others’ actions), which falls under 'Perception and Understanding of Others' (a social-related construct). Multiple experiments include healthy adult participants (n=79 across Experiments 1–3; separate healthy control group n=31 reported for the clinical comparison), with results for healthy groups reported separately from the SCA6 patients. The manuscript presents group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve contrasts) and statistical maps/analyses (thresholds, conjunctions, ROI and whole-brain comparisons) clearly attributed to the healthy/control groups. Thus it meets the review’s fMRI, sample, and whole-brain evidence inclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI task study of social processes in healthy adult physicians (n=18) and the task/behavioral measures map onto social constructs (empathic concern/compassion), the reported neuroimaging results are from an a priori ROI-restricted analysis (5mm spheres) with FWE correction performed within those ROIs. The paper does not present an unmasked, whole‑brain group-level task-evoked statistical map (voxelwise whole‑brain results) for the healthy group. Because the review’s inclusion criteria require at least one group-level whole‑brain (voxelwise) task activation map, this study must be excluded despite meeting other criteria.

Although this is an fMRI study of social-related processing (biological motion) that includes a healthy adult control group, it does not report a clear group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper relies on individual-level ROI localizers (STSp and MT), ROI-based event-related analyses, and reports ROI peak activations and Talairach coordinates. Whole-brain analyses described were directed at patients (searching for clusters) and no unmasked, group-level healthy-control whole-brain contrast or coordinate table of healthy-group task activations is provided. Thus it fails the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked results and must be excluded.

Although the study uses a social task (interactive Domino) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=30, ages 18–34), the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, whole‑brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map (voxelwise GLM contrast) explicitly identified for the healthy/control group. The analyses center on ICA-derived component spatial maps and between-group comparisons of component beta-weights (temporal-sorting), with component maps reportedly created from back-reconstructed ICs across all participants rather than a TD-only whole-brain task activation map or coordinate table for the healthy group. Because the inclusion criteria require at least one clearly identified whole-brain (voxelwise) task effect for the healthy/control group, this study does not meet criterion #3 and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20; mean age ~20.6) that investigates event simulation and explicitly addresses social-cognition constructs (theory of mind, trait inference) and uses stimuli that include social situations (~42% social). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects one-sample t-tests) with cluster-corrected thresholds (p<0.001 height, p<0.05 cluster) and coordinates for activation peaks (and additional reported uncorrected peaks). Tasks involved explicit/implicit situational understanding and future prediction, producing contrasts (e.g., Exp–Imp, Ftr–Exp) that identify canonical social brain regions (MPFC, TPJ, TP, PCC). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of action observation/execution in healthy adults (final N=12, mean age 26), directly addressing perception/understanding of others’ actions (inferring others’ applied force). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (SPM12 GLM, polynomial parametric modulation), whole-brain statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and conjunction/second-level results for the healthy sample. It is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and reports unmasked healthy-group task effects. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (social-related fMRI task; healthy adult sample; whole-brain group-level task results) and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an fMRI hyperscanning experiment of real-time mutual eye contact—a clearly social communication task. Participants are healthy adults (n≈30, mean age ~21.7), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts LIVE > REPLAY) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides regional results (tables/figures), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Although additional connectivity and interbrain synchronization analyses are included, the study also presents univariate whole-brain activation maps for the healthy sample, and results are not restricted to ROIs or to only connectivity/resting analyses. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this fMRI study includes a healthy adult control group and probes a social-related process (irony comprehension—social communication/perception of others), the full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported neuroimaging results focus on between-group contrasts (controls > schizophrenia and reverse) and combined/previously published control results; main effects are described for “study participants” without providing a standalone whole-brain healthy-group map (coordinate table or figure) in this paper. Because the review requires at least one clearly reported healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map, this manuscript does not meet the whole-brain evidence inclusion criterion and must be excluded.

This is a task-based dual‑fMRI (hyperscanning) study of social interaction (cooperation vs competition), conducted in healthy adults (n=38; mean age 22.4). The analyses produce group-level whole-brain spatial components from gICA (voxelwise maps shown/used) and report task-related effects via back-reconstructed component time‑courses and group statistical tests (paired t-tests, ISC comparisons). The paper is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and reports healthy-group whole‑brain results tied to task conditions. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria.

The study uses fMRI during social-related tasks (self-reflection and other-reflection — constructs of Perception/Understanding of Self and Others). It includes a healthy adult control group (21 HCs) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task effects for the healthy control group (main effects in HCs: VMPFC, DMPFC, ACC, PCC, precuneus, etc.), with thresholds and results summarized (including Supplementary Table S1), i.e., whole-brain voxelwise activations rather than ROI-only analyses. No exclusion criteria are met (not resting-state/seed-only, not ROI-only, includes healthy adult group). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task is an fMRI task involving observation of others’ actions with risk—relevant to social perception/understanding; sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 18–22 (within 18–65); group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (risk-taking vs safe) were computed and reported using SPM (maps, coordinates and figures are provided); the paper is empirical and not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or resting-state only, and results for the healthy group are reported. No exclusion criteria are violated. The study therefore qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy toward humans and animals) in healthy adult participants (n=60, ages 18–60). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (human negative > neutral; animal negative > neutral) with second-level random-effects analyses and coordinates with FWE-corrected thresholds and conjunction/within-group maps. Healthy groups’ whole-brain results are clearly reported separately (within-group and between-group contrasts). The study is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state or connectivity-only, and participants fall within the 18–65 range. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of narrative comprehension that explicitly probes social-related processing (mentalizing/Theory-of-Mind). Sample: healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (Mentalizing vs Action; Action vs Mentalizing) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction and reported cluster coordinates/locations, not limited to ROI-only results. The task evokes social cognition (perception/understanding of others) during story listening. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, healthy adult group reported separately). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study of social/affiliative processing (maternal attachment and owner-dog bond) using a passive viewing paradigm clearly targeting affiliation/attachment. Sample consists of healthy adult women (ages 22–45). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM8 analyses and multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., own child vs. fixation, own dog vs. fixation, own child vs. own dog, own vs. unfamiliar) with activation maps and MNI coordinates provided. Although significance was assessed with ROI-based small-volume correction, the analyses were conducted voxelwise across normalized whole-brain data and results for the healthy adult group are reported and illustrated, meeting the review’s requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI results, only connectivity/resting-state, non-adult sample) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=18, ages 18–24) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Popular>Notes, Artistic>Notes, Popular>Artistic, Artistic>Popular) with voxelwise and cluster-level correction and coordinate tables. Although the task is aesthetic music appreciation rather than an explicit ToM task, the authors frame and demonstrate involvement of social-related processing (default mode/ToM and cognitive-empathy regions such as arMFC, PCC/PC, TPJ, hippocampus) and present whole-brain results for those contrasts in the healthy sample. Therefore it meets the sample, whole-brain reporting, and social-related processing relevance criteria (perception/understanding of others; cognitive empathy) for inclusion.

This is an fMRI task study of empathy for pain, a social/other-focused process (perception/understanding of others). The sample includes healthy adult participants in the 20–30 age range (meets 18–65 criterion) and reports results separately by age group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps/contrasts (e.g., pain>no pain and pain>baseline) with voxelwise statistics (FWE-corrected maps and tables of coordinates) for the healthy participants; NeuroVault and coordinate tables are provided. Analyses are not limited to ROIs or connectivity only. Although an older group (65–75) is included, the younger healthy adult subgroup is analyzed and reported separately, satisfying the age-range requirement. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (perception of others’ dynamic vs. static facial expressions). It includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (n=13, age M=24.3) with results reported separately from the ASD group. Group-level whole-brain task contrasts for the control group (dynamic > static; and interaction contrasts) are presented with voxelwise statistics, corrected thresholds, and MNI coordinates (i.e., whole-brain random-effects maps), not limited to ROIs. Although the paper also reports connectivity/DCM and patient vs. control comparisons, it provides unmasked whole-brain activation maps for the healthy control group, satisfying all inclusion criteria and violating none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (approachability judgments), including a healthy adult control group. The paper reports within-group and between-group whole-brain task contrasts (social > gender and gender > baseline) and describes whole-brain voxelwise results for groups, with within-group analyses and statistical maps reported in the main text and supplementary materials (supplementary tables/figures). Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity analyses, and healthy-control group results are reported separately (within-group analyses and comparisons). Participants are adults and healthy controls are clearly defined. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related processing with whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=23, ages 19–32) examining neural correlates of suspense during reading. The task involves social-cognitive processing (mentalizing/theory-of-mind about story characters), a construct within ‘Perception and Understanding of Others.’ The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects GLM) with cluster-level FWE correction and lists peak coordinates and tables of activations (medial frontal cortex, TPJ, IFG, etc.), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Although an amygdala ROI was also tested, whole-brain results are clearly reported for the healthy sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy adult sample within 18–65). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI assessing social-related processing (participants thought about 16 social interaction items); includes a healthy adult control group (17 age- and IQ-matched adults, ages within adult range); reports group-level whole-brain within-group task contrasts for the control group (Social interactions – fixation contrasts reported and described in text/figures, thresholded at p=0.001 uncorrected). Not limited to ROI or resting-state/seed-connectivity analyses. Although the study also includes a clinical autism group, the healthy control whole-brain task results are reported separately. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study’s participant sample comprises adolescents (ages 12–18) with mean ages ~14.6–15.1; there is no healthy adult (age 18–65) group or separately reported adult subgroup. Although the paper uses an fMRI social-emotion face-processing task and reports whole-brain, voxelwise control-group activation maps, it fails the review’s required sample criterion (at least one healthy adult group aged 18–65). Therefore it does not meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (directional head turns) in healthy adults (final sample within age range 22–38). The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others’ attention), and group-level voxelwise results are reported: both ROI-based and whole-brain (gray matter–masked) group analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values are provided for univariate and MVPA effects (e.g., early visual cortex, STS peaks). Healthy-group results are reported separately and are not limited to ROIs only. No exclusion criteria (only ROI/ connectivity/ non-healthy groups) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=35, mean age 29) using a social-related task (memory for faces with emotional expressions — perception/understanding of others). The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (ANCOVA) with voxelwise results (FDR-corrected), provide Talairach coordinates and cluster sizes for emotion and load contrasts, and report correlations between behavior and whole-brain-derived ROIs. All inclusion criteria are met (task is social, sample is healthy adults within 18–65, and whole-brain task-evoked maps are reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (n=51, ages within 18–65) using the Ultimatum Game, a social/economic exchange task probing social decision-making (perception/understanding of others, affiliation/prosocial behavior). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (conjunction, ANOVA, parametric regressions, whole-brain coordinates and FDR-corrected results) for the healthy participant groups (MT and CT), not limited to ROIs or connectivity only. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain, task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (agency/intentionality attribution using Heider–Simmel–style animations). Sample includes healthy adult participants (n=12, mean age 25.2, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (High>Low and Low>High) analyzed with SPM2 and thresholded at p<0.001 (uncorrected), with reported activation loci (STS, IFG, occipital regions, etc.). The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and reports unmasked healthy-group task activation maps/contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met, so the study should be included.

The study's participants are adolescents (scanned at age ~16–17; samples: CFP N=156 and PGS‑E N=119). The meta-analysis requires at least one group of healthy adults aged 18–65 or a separately reported healthy adult subgroup. No adult sample or adult subgroup is reported; all participants are under 18. Although the paper reports whole‑brain task-evoked fMRI maps for a social cognition/emotion introspection task, the age criterion is not met, so the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (approachability and intelligence judgements from faces) in healthy adults (n=47; ages mean ~32, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (social vs gender) for the healthy control group, with coordinates, statistical thresholds, figures, and cluster-corrected results. A clinical ASD group is also included but healthy-control results are reported separately. Analyses are not limited to ROI-only, nor to resting-state or connectivity-only methods. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is a methods/tutorial paper describing intersubject correlation (ISC) methodology (review/tutorial), not an original empirical fMRI study reporting new whole-brain task-evoked results in a healthy adult sample. The full text provides conceptual framework, extensions, and practical considerations but does not report group-level voxelwise activation maps from healthy adults. Per exclusion criteria, non-empirical/methods-only papers without original fMRI data in healthy adults should be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20 scanned; mean age 25.7). The task probes social-emotional processing (guilt memories vs hypothetical social scenarios), clearly mapping onto social cognition / perception-understanding constructs. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., guilt memories vs neutral memories; guilt memories vs guilt hypotheticals) with whole-brain thresholding (p<0.001, cluster extent) and reports activated regions and coordinates; SPM8 second-level analyses are described. The study is not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-healthy samples. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This study reports an fMRI task involving social touch (self- vs other-touch), addressing social-related processing (perception/understanding of self and others). It includes a healthy adult control group (NC; mean age 23.7 ± 3.6 years) analyzed and reported separately. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activations for the control group are presented (self-touch and other-touch effects, FWE-corrected whole-brain results and coordinates are reported/illustrated). Although an ADHD clinical group is also studied, the healthy-control whole-brain task results are clearly reported, satisfying inclusion criteria. Therefore the paper qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked whole-brain fMRI of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing using an altruism (dictator-style) task probing consideration of others’ payoffs and fairness (perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (altruism N=55, subset N=37 also did the food task), ages within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight SVR maps, SPM second-level tests, conjunctions, and reported cluster coordinates) clearly identified as healthy/control group results; whole-brain results and statistical maps are available on OSF. No clinical groups confound the reported healthy-group maps, and the study is empirical with original fMRI data. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (final N=23, mean age 26.4) that examines social perception (animacy, action observation, theory-of-mind related processes) during a task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (main effects of agent form and belief, interactions) with voxelwise thresholding (p<0.005, cluster reported) and tables/figures of peak coordinates and activations. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (fMRI task in healthy adults; whole-brain group-level results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates social-related processing (perception of fearful faces with direct vs. averted gaze) and includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=22, mean age 23.7 yrs, within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked analyses for the control group (e.g., within-group AVERTED>DIRECT and AVERTED>FIXATION contrasts), using mixed-effects FLAME and permutation testing with FWE correction and cluster thresholds; results for controls are described in the text and shown as statistical maps. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria (social task, healthy adult group reported separately, and whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps). It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, includes suitable age range).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (attentional orienting to social gaze vs. arrow cues; social communication/perception constructs). Sample: 22 healthy adult participants (mean age ~23), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (2×2×2 factorial ANOVA) with voxelwise thresholds and peak coordinates; whole-brain results (incongruent>congruent, invalid>valid, cue contrasts) are described and reported, with additional small-volume corrections—i.e., not ROI-only. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for healthy adult whole-brain task fMRI of social processing.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants addressing social-related audiovisual non-verbal face processing and reports group-level, voxelwise activation contrasts, the functional acquisition used a split-sagittal, limited-slice coverage that explicitly excluded medial regions and other parts of the brain. The review’s inclusion criterion requires at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (i.e., whole-brain coverage). Because the reported voxelwise analyses are based on partial-brain coverage rather than whole-brain imaging, the study does not meet the ’whole-brain evidence’ requirement and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of healthy adults using social tasks (theory-of-mind; social attribution-of-attention) and participants are within the 18–65 range. However, the primary task analyses are performed using localized ICA restricted to a TPJ-region-of-interest and mixed-effects regression on IC time courses. The paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (GLM main effect or within-group contrast) for the healthy group. Although seed-to-voxel functional connectivity maps (whole-brain) are reported, these are connectivity results rather than task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Because the study lacks the required whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group map, it fails the inclusion criteria and should be excluded.

This is an fMRI task study of social-related processing (self- and other-reflection). It includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=33) within the 18–65 age range and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts for the control group (e.g., Self>Facts, Other>Facts, Other>Self) with voxelwise cluster-level inference (z-threshold and cluster-correction) and coordinate tables/figures. Although a clinical (schizophrenia) group is also included, healthy-group results are reported separately. The study does not limit results to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria for the review.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=31, ages 18–35) that examines neural responses to viewing faces with vs. without facial disfigurement—an instance of social perception/Perception and Understanding of Others. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (contrasts of pre- vs. post-surgery faces) with familywise-error cluster correction and describes significant clusters (fusiform/occipital increases; medial anterior cingulate decreases). The sample is within the 18–65 range and results are reported for the healthy group (no clinical subgroup-only reporting). The analysis is whole-brain (not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study reports task-based fMRI of prosodic (social-communication) speech processing, which falls under social-related processing. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=8, mean age 23.05) within the 18–65 range and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task results for controls (one-sample t-tests, conjunctions, and deactivation maps with thresholding and anatomical localization). Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Although sample size is small, all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (fMRI sample n=29, mean age 25.6) investigating social-related processing (learning about others’ inter-temporal preferences, social influence, perception/understanding of others). The task required evaluating choices for self and others during fMRI and interleaved probe trials. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and cluster-level FWE-corrected results (including coordinates and whole-brain contrasts testing repetition suppression and surprise signals in mPFC, striatum, pMFC), not limited to ROI-only analyses. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion requirements for the review.

This study uses task-based fMRI with the HCP social cognition (Animated Triangles/social motion) paradigm, directly addressing social-related processing. It includes a healthy adult control group (N=25) reported separately. The paper provides whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy controls (voxelwise t-maps, peak MNI coordinates, FWE-corrected statistics), not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Although a clinical (first-episode schizophrenia) group is also included, healthy-group results are explicitly reported. Participant ages are adults within the target range. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=12, ages 20–32) that directly probes social-related processing (learning facts about people vs buildings vs hammers) and interprets person-selective anterior temporal lobe responses as social cognition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (conjunction analyses, thresholding and cluster-size correction across ROIs and whole-brain) and presents domain-specific and domain-general whole-brain results (figures and cluster tables described). Results are reported for the healthy/control sample (no separate patient-only reporting). The study is empirical, not ROI-only, and includes task-evoked activation maps meeting the review’s whole-brain requirement. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts for healthy adult participants, the task does not target social-related processing as defined by the review (affiliation/attachment, social communication, perception/understanding of self or others). The paradigms present erotic pictures and videos to probe sexual arousal and orientation (ventral striatum reward/incentive responses). While some brain regions related to perception or mentalizing are reported incidentally, the primary experimental manipulation and aims are sexual incentive/orientation, not social cognition. Therefore it fails the requirement that the study use fMRI during a social-related task and should be excluded.

Although this fMRI study tests self-related processing in healthy adult participants (ages 18–35) using a task probing perception/understanding of self, the reported neuroimaging results are based on ROI / small-volume analyses. The manuscript does not clearly present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for the healthy sample; reported coordinates and statistics appear to come from restricted ROI/SVC analyses. Therefore it fails the review’s required criterion of documented whole-brain group-level task activation and must be excluded.

Although the study uses task fMRI probing personal familiarity (a social-cognition construct) and reports whole-brain, within-group activation maps for the healthy control group, the control participants are elderly (older adults) rather than healthy adults aged 18–65. No healthy adult subgroup in the 18–65 age range is reported separately. This violates the sample age inclusion criterion (studies must include a healthy adult group age 18–65 or report such a subgroup), therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion discrimination, a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). Sample includes healthy adult control group (ages 19–35) reported separately from the excessive smartphone group. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster tables with FWE-corrected p-values and >100 voxels) including within-group contrasts for the normal control (NC) group (e.g., NC activations for AH vs HH), not limited to ROI-only analyses. Imaging methods and whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates are described. Age range and healthy control reporting meet inclusion criteria; the study is empirical with original task-based fMRI data. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of emotional prosody, which is a social-communication/social-perception task relevant to the review. It includes a healthy adult control group (behavioral: n=22, fMRI: n=21; age ranges 20–46), within the 18–65 criterion. The paper presents group-level whole-brain task activation results for controls (emotional vs neutral prosody, complexity and condition contrasts), including conjunction maps and FWE cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses reported in the text/figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Although a clinical ASD group is included, healthy-group results are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, and reports unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (moral dilemma/kinship and a moral-decision task). Participants: healthy adult sample (N=30; females aged 19–39), meeting the 18–65 requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses: inter-subject correlation (ISC) maps across the whole brain with FDR correction and cluster reporting, and a separate GLM whole-brain analysis of the moral-dilemma decision task (group-level contrasts, corrected, with tables of clusters/coordinates and neurovault link). Results are reported for the healthy sample (no mixed clinical groups). The study is neither ROI-only nor resting-state/connectivity-only and provides unmasked whole-brain task effects for the healthy group. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social evaluation (social cognition/perception) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–29). The task is a social judgment task (forced-choice evaluations of target persons) and analyses report group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (multilevel whole-brain MLM, reported clusters with MNI coordinates, DLPFC and dACC activations). It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and healthy-group whole-brain effects are clearly described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

While the study is an fMRI investigation of social evaluation in healthy adult participants (N=36) using an appropriate social task, the reported neuroimaging results are confined to a priori small-volume–corrected analyses within a bilateral vACC ROI. The manuscript describes group-level analyses and ROI-based SVC results but does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map for the healthy group (nor whole-brain coordinates/tables) that would meet the review’s whole-brain evidence requirement. Therefore it fails the inclusion criterion requiring at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for healthy adults.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results (FWE-corrected) relevant to social processing, the participant sample is adolescent/young adults with ages ranging 17–20 (mean 18). The paper does not report a separate healthy adult (age 18–65) subgroup analyzed independently; the sample is treated as an adolescent/young adult group and authors note limited generalizability to adults. Because the inclusion criterion requires at least one group of healthy adult participants (18–65) reported separately or clearly meeting the age range, this study fails the sample-age criterion and must be excluded despite meeting the imaging and task criteria.

This is an fMRI task study of face perception (passive face/object/texture viewing), which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=51, ages 18–42) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts for the adult/control group (e.g., Face>Object, Face>Fixation; FLAME mixed-effects group analyses with cluster correction) presented in figures and tables. The study is empirical, not connectivity-only, and provides unmasked whole-brain activation results for the healthy adults. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in a sample of healthy adult participants (N=74) using a social-related task (neutral face processing, emotion recognition, affective ToM). The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (one-sample t-tests and contrasts) with FWE-corrected thresholds and presents whole-brain results (figures and supplementary tables). While ROI and connectivity analyses are also reported, whole-brain healthy-group task effects are clearly described and meet the review’s requirement for unmasked, within-group activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and healthy adults are analyzed separately). Age range is not explicitly stated in the excerpt, but participants are described as healthy adults; there is no indication they fall outside 18–65. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The healthy sample comprises adolescent males (age range 13–19); no healthy adult (18–65) subgroup is reported separately. Thus the study fails the sample inclusion criterion requiring at least one healthy adult group. Although the study used task fMRI and reports whole-brain analyses (exploratory across groups), it does not clearly present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy adult group. Therefore it does not meet the review’s age-based inclusion criterion (and likely the healthy-group whole-brain reporting requirement).

This is an fMRI study of prosody perception and production, a form of social communication relevant to perception/understanding of others and empathy. Participants are healthy adults (n=19; ages 18–58). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., “happy‑neutral”, “question‑neutral”) analyzed with random-effects models and FDR/FWE thresholding and provides whole-brain results and coordinate lists and figures. The design is task-based (production and perception) rather than resting-state or connectivity-only. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for healthy adult whole‑brain task fMRI of social-related processing.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (imitate/observe emotional faces) in healthy adults (initial N=28; final imaging N=20; ages 18–55). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses: a task PLS and a GLM in SPM8 with voxelwise maps and bootstrap-thresholded voxel patterns (rendered on the brain and described in the text). Results are reported for the healthy/control sample (no patient-only or ROI-only restrictions). The methods and results clearly present whole-brain, voxelwise task activation patterns related to social cognitive processing, satisfying all inclusion criteria and violating none of the exclusion criteria.

Multiple inclusion criteria are not met. Participants are adolescents (age 12–18), not healthy adults aged 18–65, so the sample is outside the required age range. The task is the Embedded Figures Task, a visual search/perceptual task, not a social-related paradigm (e.g., affiliation, social communication, perception/understanding of self/others). Although whole-brain group-level fMRI contrasts are reported, they pertain to adolescent case/sibling/control groups and not to a healthy adult group. Therefore the study does not provide a whole-brain task activation map from healthy adults and does not address social processing in adults.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (anticipation of touching an animate vs inanimate target). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=32, ages 21–33; task data in 21 participants but healthy adult group reported). The paper presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (paired-sample t-test: anticipation animate vs inanimate; whole-brain analyses with PNI covariates) with FDR-corrected statistical maps and reported coordinates/clusters. Although additional resting-state analyses (PLE, DFA) are included, the study provides unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation results rather than only ROI or connectivity analyses. Age range and healthy-group reporting meet inclusion criteria. Therefore it qualifies for inclusion.

This study uses task-based fMRI (Cyberball social exclusion) addressing social-related processing. It includes a healthy adult control group (HC; n=28) reported separately. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results for the healthy controls (main effect of condition: left anterior insula/inferior frontal gyrus) with voxelwise FWE correction and reported coordinates/figures. The task contrasts (ESE vs INC, ISE vs INC) and statistical maps are clearly described for HC. Not ROI-only, not resting-state or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of empathy-for-pain, a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=18 males, ages 22–63) reported separately alongside an ASD group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (see whole-brain analyses and Supplementary Table 1; contrasts of High Pain–Low Pain in Other, masked by Self, with reported coordinates and between-group whole-brain contrasts). Results for the control/healthy group and subgroup contrasts are clearly described. The study is empirical, uses task-evoked BOLD activation, and does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social processing (empathy/mentalising) in healthy adults (final sample n=34, ages 20–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., emotional > neutral) and voxelwise correlations (EA modulation, time-series correlations with intensity), analyzed with SPM12/FSL and TFCE FWE correction, with peak activations and cluster tables. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and healthy-group whole-brain results are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are violated.

The study uses fMRI during social-related tasks (action observation/understanding; theory-of-mind measures) and includes a healthy control (HC) group. However, the full text describes primarily between-group contrasts (ALS > HC, HC > ALS), conjunction analyses, and ROI/small-volume results. The paper does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map or main-effect/within-group contrast explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., a standalone HC whole-brain activation map reported in text/tables). Because the review requires at least one clearly described healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map, this criterion is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study uses task fMRI with healthy adult controls and addresses social-related processing (emotion word comprehension). However, the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. Key whole-brain results are presented either pooled across all participants or as between-group (control > ASC) contrasts, and ROI analyses and within-group ROI statistics for controls are reported, but a clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task effect (main effect or within-group voxelwise map) is not provided in the full text. Because the review requires at least one clearly reported healthy-group whole-brain task map, this study fails that criterion and must be excluded.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) Uses task-based fMRI during a social-related impression-formation task (perception/understanding of others, varying race and status). (2) Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8). (3) Reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM contrasts used for PLS; whole-brain PLS results with voxelwise bootstrap ratios, cluster reporting, and figures), not limited to ROI or resting-state or seed connectivity. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore include.

Meets all inclusion criteria: fMRI task explicitly probes social processing (direct vs averted gaze; social cognition/action control). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=30, ages 19–41). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; direct vs averted gaze) with cluster- and FWE-thresholding and coordinates described, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirement. Although psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity is reported, this is supplementary to whole-brain task results (not the sole analysis). No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study examines social perception (gaze processing/theory-of-mind), using a task involving direct vs. averted gaze. It includes a healthy adult control group (initial n=25; adults) with group-level, within-group contrasts reported (controls: direct > averted gaze) derived from a second-level voxelwise GLM. Coordinates and P-values for group and within-group contrasts are presented (tables/figures), and voxelwise results are described (visualized at P<0.001 uncorrected and small-volume corrected ROIs). Although some ROI-based small-volume correction was used, the paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation for the healthy/control group separately, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI-only analyses, only connectivity/resting-state, or no healthy adult data) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI of social contingency and includes a healthy adult control group (TD adults, mean age ~29), it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy/control group. The authors explicitly state they focused on an a priori arMPFC ROI and that whole-brain/functional connectivity analyses could not be conducted due to signal loss around the paranasal sinus (including striatum and mOFC). Results are presented as ROI analyses and between-group contrasts rather than unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effects. This violates the inclusion criterion requiring at least one whole-brain task-evoked map for the healthy group.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) Uses task-based fMRI probing social-related face perception/emotional/mentalizing processes (Thatcher Illusion, attention to eyes/mouth). (2) Includes a healthy adult control group (neurotypical adults, mean age ~25.8) with results reported separately. (3) Reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise within-group task contrasts for the healthy/control group (statistical maps and thresholds described for NT). No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, healthy adults within 18–65). Therefore it should be included.

While this is an fMRI study of social appraisal (trustworthiness) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=17), the paper does not clearly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map specifically for the healthy/control group. The whole-brain analyses described are reported across all participants or as between-group contrasts, and control-specific results are presented primarily as ROI analyses and summary statistics rather than an unmasked, voxelwise healthy-group map. Because the inclusion criteria require at least one explicitly reported healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map (or equivalent coordinate table/figure clearly identified as from the healthy group), this study does not meet that criterion and must be excluded.

This fMRI study includes a healthy adult control group (n=25) and reports whole-brain, second-level random-effects task activation analyses for gesture planning and execution. The task probes social-communication relevant processes (pantomime/gesture planning and production), fitting the review’s social-related constructs. Within-group (healthy controls) whole-brain results are described (Analyses S2/S3, figure S2, table S2) and thresholding/cluster criteria are reported, so maps/coordinates for the healthy group are available. The study is task-based (not resting-state or seed-only) and not limited to ROI analyses. Participant ages are described as adult and matched to patients; no exclusion criteria (e.g., only connectivity or ROI-only reporting, non-adult sample) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

While the study uses task fMRI of social processing (emotional face perception) and includes healthy adult participants (and an independent healthy replication sample), it does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The primary whole-brain analyses were conducted on a combined sample (patients + controls) and the independent healthy replication used an anatomical ROI approach (fusiform ROI) rather than an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group contrast. Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (eye gaze perception) in healthy adults (N=18, ages 18–30). The task is social (perception/understanding of others’ gaze), and analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (second-level SPM-t maps, whole-brain FDR p<0.05) and coordinate tables showing effects in social attention regions. Results for the healthy/typical group are reported explicitly (including whole-brain correlations with AQ). The study does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity, or resting-state analyses and includes clearly described whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy participants. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusions.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (nulliparous women, N=17, ages 19–29) examining social-related processing (perception of infant cries and faces—affiliation/attachment and perception of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., cries vs pink noise; happy/sad vs neutral faces) with fully described preprocessing, second-level random-effects analyses, cluster correction and thresholding, and figures/tables of whole-brain results. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and participants fall within the 18–65 age range. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (social-media 'likes') with whole-brain group analyses reported, but the sample consists of adolescents aged 13–18 and does not include or report a separate healthy adult (18–65) group. Therefore it fails the age/sample inclusion criterion (I4) and meets exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social task), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used functional MRI during a social-related task (listening to film excerpts requiring inference of characters' mental states/language conveying social information), satisfying I3. A healthy adult group (n=28; age range 18–65) is reported separately, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrast maps for the healthy control group (INT>HIN) with voxelwise results and FWE-corrected maps and tables of coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical article) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study uses task fMRI of social processing (SID, EFP) and includes a healthy control group of adults aged 50–60 (I3, I4). The paper reports whole-brain analyses (Tables S1–S2) and ROI results, but the provided full text does not show an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map reported specifically for the healthy/control group alone. Main reported whole-brain maps are for the combined sample or ROI-focused, and primary between-group contrasts (cocaine > control) are reported. Therefore the paper fails to meet I5 (no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task map), triggering exclusion per E4. Full text appears complete.

This article is a non-empirical review (in Japanese) summarizing fMRI approaches and findings; it does not present original fMRI data or report group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from healthy adult participants. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no original fMRI task data reported), I4 (no healthy adult sample data presented), I5 (no group-level whole-brain maps), I6 (not applicable). Full text appears incomplete in the provided materials (only abstract/metadata available).

This fMRI study investigates neural responses to dynamic facial expressions (a social-communication/perception task) in a sample of healthy adults (n=51; mean age 22.5 years), meeting the review’s population requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (dynamic expression vs dynamic mosaic) analyzed with random-effects models and whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds; results are presented in tables/figures and described in the text. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample; I5: whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps; I6: whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only/resting-state-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical work).

This article is a narrative review of fMRI research on social brain development rather than an empirical fMRI study reporting original whole-brain task-evoked group maps for a healthy adult sample. It does not present original fMRI methods, participant samples, or group-level voxelwise statistical maps attributable to the paper itself. Therefore it meets exclusion E6 (non-empirical/review) and does not satisfy required inclusion criteria I3–I6 (no original fMRI task data, no healthy adult sample analyzed as a group, and no whole-brain group-level activation maps reported as original results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of imitation, a social-related construct (imitation/perception of others). It uses a healthy adult sample (N=37; ages 18–25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation and random-effects one-sample t-tests) with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activations; PPI connectivity is reported in addition to task activations. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=31–45 across analyses; ages 19–28) that uses social-related tasks (eye-gaze shifts, self-propelling motion, and an implicit mental-inference role-playing task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., E–O, S–X, Investigation–Control) analyzed with SPM5 and reports voxelwise and cluster-corrected results (figures and tables of activation peaks). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study addressing social-related processing (empathy/intimacy/relationship perspective-taking). Sample: 36 healthy adult participants (mean age 23), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM2 results, voxel-level FDR threshold, coordinate tables and figures) for contrasts of interest (Pain vs. Neutral across perspectives), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating attractiveness comparisons (social perception of others) using a task that requires judging the beauty of other people (and dogs). The sample comprises 25 healthy adult women (mean age 23.5), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses, conjunctions, and ROI analyses, with voxelwise thresholds and tables/coordinates. Thus it meets the social-related task requirement, healthy adult sample criterion, and whole-brain reporting requirement. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the reported voxelwise task analyses are restricted to a bilateral STS mask (region-focused reporting) and the manuscript does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map or whole-brain voxelwise task results for the healthy group. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I5/I6 not met) and falls under the exclusion for studies reporting only ROI-restricted results (E2).

The provided "full text" is not the article but a website privacy/cookie notice; core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing. Although the title indicates an fMRI study of self-knowledge (which would map onto I3: perception/understanding of self), there is no information to confirm participant sample (I4) or that the paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps (I5/I6). Therefore the review cannot verify required criteria. Inclusion criteria confirmed: none. Inclusion criteria not met/unknown: I4, I5, I6. No exclusion criteria from the list can be confidently applied because of missing content. Marking fulltext_incomplete=true and excluding due to inability to assess eligibility from incomplete/full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (Animated Triangles Task) that probes theory-of-mind/mentalizing (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (17 adults, ages within 18–65) with results reported separately from the patient group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activations for the control group (describes control-group activations, group-level FLAME analysis, cluster-corrected Z maps, and references individual group activations in supplementary material), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (meets I5). The reporting format (text, figures, supplementary material) is acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs, not only connectivity/resting-state, and not only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making that collected whole-brain task-evoked BOLD data in healthy adult participants. The neuroimaging cohort includes healthy adults aged 18–53 (n=62 after exclusions), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM results (voxelwise threshold p<.001, extent threshold; tables referenced in Supplementary S5 and NeuroVault collection) and describes activations in dACC, bilateral dlPFC, parietal cortex, insula, etc. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps), and I6 (results reported via text/tables/NeuroVault). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (perception of person dyads/interactions) in healthy adult participants (n=12; ages 21–31), meeting the reviewer’s sample requirements. The study used task-based fMRI during a social-related sex-categorization of person dyads (I3). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and contrasts are reported (e.g., incongruent > congruent; non-interaction contrasts) with tables of peak coordinates and figures (Table 3, Figs. 6–7), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/connectivity-only, between-group only, out-of-range participants, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=34, ages 19–31 and 22–29) that uses task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (observing others' social-integrity threats and rating schadenfreude or fremdscham). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (SIT>NEUT) with family-wise error (FWE) correction for whole-brain analyses and presents voxelwise activation results and coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are fully reported in the provided full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Meets inclusion criteria: (I3) study used task-based fMRI probing social cognition (affective ToM, emotion recognition, face processing); (I4) includes a healthy adult control group (n=18) reported separately; (I5) reports within-group (healthy controls) task-evoked whole-brain activation results (e.g., task-associated activation in controls, full-factorial analyses, whole-brain thresholding P<0.001 uncorrected, with supplementary tables referenced); (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text and supplementary materials. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria applied: ["I3","I4","I5","I6"]. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task: participants regulated emotional reactivity to participant-generated, socially salient autobiographical situations and negative self-beliefs (perception/understanding of self in social contexts). Sample: 35 healthy adults aged 22.6–55.4 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (whole-brain results shown in tables and figures; random-effects group maps and cluster-correction details are provided). Reporting includes whole-brain coordinate tables, figures, and an a priori amygdala ROI analysis; whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly identified. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within the required age range). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and should be included.

This empirical fMRI study reports a faces-versus-houses task (socially-relevant face perception) using task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample. The fMRI subset (N=22) comprises healthy undergraduate adults (mean age 18.87), meeting the age and health requirements. Authors conducted whole-brain SPM8 second-level group analyses, report significant clusters/activation maps (Table 2, group-level figures, FWE-corrected maps) and also describe suprathreshold voxel counts in bilateral fusiform gyri; these constitute group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results from the healthy/control group. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-communicative processing (speech act comprehension: Naming vs. Requesting) in healthy adults (N=18, ages 18–41). It reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (whole-brain contrasts “Request > Naming” and “Words > Faces”) with FDR-corrected results, provides ROI SVC and coordinate tables/figures, and describes methods, results, and discussion in full. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported via tables/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes direct healthy-group task effects, empirical original fMRI data). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants performed a valence classification task on agentic and communal trait words (social content). Sample: 42 healthy adult Chinese undergraduates (age 18–25), healthy group reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 contrasts: agency vs. fixation, communion vs. fixation, conjunctions, and pairwise t-tests) with AlphaSim correction; results are presented in tables and figures and described in the text. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This empirical study used fMRI to measure brain activation during a social communication task (communication vs description), meeting the review’s focus on social-related processing. The sample comprised 29 healthy adult participants aged 18–24 (results reported for healthy group). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses and contrasts (e.g., communication vs description; familiar vs unfamiliar) with results presented in figures and tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy task maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study uses a social appraisal task (Socio-emotional Preferential Task) probing face-related socio-emotional processing (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) reported separately alongside patients (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical results (e.g., task effect like>gender in dmPFC/ACC and corrected whole-brain Drug×Group interaction in medial occipital cortex with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values), and refers to figures/tables (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (free online reciprocal imitation) in healthy adults (N=23 females, ages 18–30), satisfying the review population criterion. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and contrasts are reported (GLM contrasts for imitating, being imitated, observation vs rest; FWE-corrected p<0.05) with tables of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Although the study also reports PPI connectivity analyses, it provides unmasked, whole-brain task activation results for the healthy adult group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete.

This study uses task fMRI during a social interaction (iterated Prisoner's Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Analyses are restricted to ROI-based activation summaries and task-based connectivity (gPPI) within a predefined network with small-volume corrections. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. This matches exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Accordingly the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based functional MRI using social stimuli (faces) embedded in an oddball target-detection task, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=19; ages 19.3–47.5), meeting the age and healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., shape targets vs. novels, face targets vs. novels, and direct comparisons), with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected thresholds described, satisfying whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (complete core content). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study of social interaction (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 22.3). The task probes social/affective processing related to provocation and retaliation (social interaction, perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with statistical maps and Talairach coordinate tables (figures and tables of voxelwise results) for the healthy sample. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of eligibility.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball ball-toss) that probes social interaction/reward, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=31; mean age ~21), meeting the age and health sample criterion. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (task contrasts, voxel-level threshold and cluster-level FWE correction) with tables of significant clusters and coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of neural processing of social hierarchy (social-related task), with healthy adult participants (72 adults, ages within 18–65) and detailed methods. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ‘superior player > inferior player’) with thresholded statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures (FDR-corrected thresholds), clearly attributable to the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants viewed virtual characters whose gaze and facial expressions manipulated self-involvement and social relevance (SOC vs ARB; ME vs OTHER). Sample: 18 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 25.9), satisfying healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with random-effects inference, whole-brain contrasts (e.g., SOC>ARB, ME>OTHER), SPM{z} maps, coordinates and tables of activations (Table 4; Figs. 3–4). Results for the healthy group are reported directly. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social stimuli (traffic awareness campaign videos) to probe socio-cognitive processes (mentalizing/empathy), meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (ages 19–30 and 20–29 ranges reported), meeting I4.
