The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (CV vs NV) for each group, with whole-brain analyses and figures/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original task-based fMRI study of self–other processing (a social-cognition/ self and other understanding task), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports within-group whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts for the typically developing (healthy control) group (e.g., self vs. letter contrasts with tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The sample includes a healthy control group of adults (TD group mean age 27.3, within 18–65). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, and includes healthy adult within-group whole-brain task effects). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used resting-state fMRI and graph-theory connectivity analyses; no task-based fMRI paradigm was administered during scanning and no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from the healthy/control group are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes a healthy adult control group). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (no task fMRI/social-related task during scan) and I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group map). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (resting-state analyses only without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social working memory (SWM) in healthy adults (N=25, mean age 21.6). The task explicitly probes social cognition (ranking friends on traits) during fMRI and includes a comparator cognitive working memory task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (parametric modulation, conjunctions, contrasts) with cluster thresholds and tables/figures of activated regions; results are reported for the healthy participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only metadata/header provided). Cannot verify that study meets inclusion criteria: no available methods or results to confirm (I3) that functional MRI during a social-related task was used for a healthy adult group, (I4) that a healthy adult (18–65) group was included and reported separately, (I5) that a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported, or (I6) that whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on provided content. Because the full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing, inclusion cannot be confirmed and the record must be excluded pending full text.

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making (iterated prisoner's dilemma) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 23–38). The task probes perception/understanding of others’ intentions, meeting the social-related construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunction and COMP>COOP contrasts) with cluster-level correction and coordinates/figures/tables of activations (rTPJ, mPFC, PCC, hippocampus, etc.). Full methods, results, and discussion are provided, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are clearly identified. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical work) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses task fMRI of social inference (Why/How) (I3 satisfied) and includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (I4 satisfied). However, it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The whole-brain analyses presented focus on Group×Stimulus interactions and between-group/post-hoc group differences rather than an independent, clearly identified control-group whole-brain task map. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (explicit mental simulation of others' actions/feelings), meeting the review objective. Sample: 20 healthy adults aged 21–47 (within 18–65) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked BOLD contrasts (GLM second-level SPM-t maps; thresholded at p<0.05 FDR corrected) and corresponding figures and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and illustrated. Although the study also includes connectivity/ISPS analyses, it additionally provides conventional whole-brain activation maps and contrasts (e.g., simulate > watch, simulate losing > simulate winning), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task effects. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI data including multiple social-related tasks (false belief/Theory of Mind, animacy/intentional triangles, human vocalizations, trustworthiness, eyes intention/face tasks), collected in a sample of 78 healthy adults (age range 18–40). It presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects (RFX) analyses with voxelwise correction (p<0.05 FWE), figures, and peak tables, and also provides individual-level whole-brain contrast maps and supplementary materials. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps), and I6 (results clearly reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are violated. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social perception (affiliation vs. isolation) using BOLD fMRI during a social-related pleasantness-rating task, satisfying I3. The sample includes a younger healthy adult group (mean age 20.75), meeting the required adult age range (18–65) for inclusion (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise group analyses with reported coordinates, tables, and figures of group-level task-evoked activation maps for the healthy groups (I5), and these whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, includes within-group whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the review’s core content requirement: the fMRI task is a low-contrast moving vs. stationary visual motion paradigm (motion perception), not a social-related task. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (the paper includes healthy adult control groups with results reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not use fMRI during a social-related task or measure social constructs such as affiliation, social communication, or perception/understanding of others), I5 (the paper does not clearly report a whole-brain, group-level task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; results are reported primarily as ROI and group-difference analyses). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball social exclusion) addressing social-related processing (affiliation/attachment and perception of others). The sample comprises healthy adult university students (final N=42; ages within adult range). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (exclusion vs inclusion) with voxelwise analyses and FWE-corrected thresholds, and provides coordinate tables and whole-brain interaction analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study of face encoding (social cognition) including a healthy control group of typically-developing adults (mean age ~18.7, within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps and contrasts for the control group (e.g., Table 2 and within-group Dm effect analyses using whole-brain Monte Carlo cluster correction). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results for the healthy group), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy maps, participants in age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study is excluded because the sample is adolescents (mean age 17.0, range 15.47–18.72) and does not report a separate healthy adult (age 18–65) group; thus it meets exclusion criterion E5. It does meet several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses task-based fMRI probing social processing — viewing/rating parents), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/cluster-corrected results), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures and described in text). However it fails I4 (sample of healthy adults 18–65). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical dual-fMRI (task-based) hyperscanning study using an interactive social task (pattern game) — i.e., a social-related task. Participants were healthy adults (N=44; mean age 22.4), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses (FEAT/FLAME) with non-parametric permutation correction and presents thresholded whole-brain statistical maps and cluster tables (Figures and Tables referenced). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no resting-state/connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants in age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social evaluation (trustworthiness judgments) using a social-related task and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for healthy control adults. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task: trustworthiness/age judgments—social processing), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately; controls mean age 32.2, within 18–65), I5 (within-group, whole-brain voxelwise analyses for the control group are reported; Tables and T-maps described), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effects. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study investigates voice identity recognition (social communication / perception of others) using task-based fMRI paradigms (vocal vs non-vocal sounds; speaker vs speech tasks), fulfilling the review’s social-related processing scope. It reports healthy control groups (n=32; ages ~29–34) and presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses for controls (within-group contrasts, figures, and coordinate tables; supplementary whole-brain results are referenced). Results include voxelwise contrasts (e.g., vocal>non-vocal; speaker>speech) for controls and reported coordinates/thresholds, satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (social vs. non-social context in episodic memory) using a task involving social interaction and word recognition. Participants were 24 healthy adults (ages 18–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with contrasts, tables of activations, coordinates, and thresholding procedures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, whole-brain group results reported, and acceptable reporting of coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

This empirical fMRI study uses a deception paradigm that engages social-cognitive processes (deception/theory-of-mind aspects), includes a healthy adult sample (24 males aged 19–60), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (lie vs truth) with tables/figures describing activations. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind (social-related processing) using a validated moving-triangles ToM paradigm (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adults with ages 24–64 (mean 45.6), within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (ToM > R, ToM > Baseline, R > Baseline) and provides thresholding and cluster results (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within the eligible age range, and the paper is empirical. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study examines vocal emotional processing with task-evoked fMRI in healthy adults (N=36, ages 20–35) and therefore addresses a social communication construct (I3) and has an eligible healthy adult sample (I4). However, the reported results are atlas-based ROI functional connectivity and graph-theoretical network metrics (Power-264 ROI analyses) rather than voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate-based activation tables/figures from a standard GLM. No unmasked, group-level voxelwise activation maps or coordinate tables for task activation are reported, and the paper focuses on connectivity/ROI-network analyses. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (I5) and falls under exclusions for studies reporting only ROI/connectivity-type analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map (E2, E3). Full text appears complete.

The study includes a healthy control group and reports whole-brain, within-group fMRI activation maps for that control group (meeting I3, I5, I6). However, the healthy/control sample spans ages 12–23 and is not exclusively adults aged 18–65; no subgroup analysis limited to adults (18+) is reported. Therefore it does not meet the sample criterion I4 requiring a healthy adult (18–65) group. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly met. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (affective/CT-targeted touch) in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (arm>baseline, palm>baseline, and arm>pal m contrasts) with corrected thresholds and cluster information; connectivity (PPI) is supplemental. Methods, results, and discussion are present, and healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps are clearly reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self, friend, celebrity role judgments) that probes Perception and Understanding of Self/Others. The sample is healthy adult participants (N=37 males, mean age 22.9) within 18–65. The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (self vs. celebrity; friend vs. celebrity) with thresholding (p<.05 FDR corrected with voxelwise p<.001) and provide activation coordinates/tables and figures. Whole-brain gPPI connectivity analyses are also reported, but task activation maps for the healthy group are clearly presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI task study of social processing (approachability judgments from faces) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=24) with ages within 18–65 and reports healthy-group results separately. The paper provides group-level whole-brain task activation results for the healthy control group (detailed cluster-level results and peak coordinates; figures and text describe BOLD activations and maps), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain evidence. Whole-brain results are reported in tables/coordinates and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task map, only between-group contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

Exclusion criteria met: E2 (study reports ROI-based results with small-volume correction in predefined ROIs and does not present unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy/control group) and E4 (results focus on group differences and differential connectivity without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related/attachment task: baby-cry with self/other/own-child perspectives) and I4 (contains a healthy adult control group, results reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked voxelwise statistical map is reported). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, but the reported analyses are ROI- and seed-based rather than whole-brain healthy-group activations, so the study must be excluded under E2/E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (dynamic social gestures) using a task manipulating sociability, actor-orientation, and face-visibility (meets I3). The sample is a healthy adult group (N=20; mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7) reported as healthy young adults and the group-level results are presented for this healthy/control sample (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected) with coordinates and figures/tables (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not incomplete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment probing social interaction (perceived live vs. recorded speech) in a sample of healthy adult participants (final N=29, ages 18–27). The task is social-communication relevant and the manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Live > Social; Social > Standard) thresholded and cluster-corrected, with figures/tables describing the results. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial (social-related) learning using a task where participants learned to obtain rewards for self, another person, or no one, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 31 healthy adult participants (males, ages 19–32), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses and statistics (main effects, conjunctions, contrasts) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables/figures (e.g., Tables S1–S4, voxel-wise results described), meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is therefore complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and this is original empirical work).

This study reports an fMRI social-cognition task in adolescents (ages 10–18) with clinical (KS, ASD) and non-clinical control groups. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (participants only outside the 18–65 adult range; no healthy adult subgroup reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — face processing/affect labeling), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for controls using voxelwise analysis and cluster correction), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures described in text). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no healthy adult participants aged 18–65 reported separately). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the adult healthy fMRI meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults: 17 healthy adult participants (mean age 26). The task involved observing social versus individual actions with gaze manipulated (a social-related task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level random-effects ANOVA), thresholding details, SPM maps, coordinates, and figures showing main effects and interactions (dMPFC, IFG, pSTS, amygdala, etc.). The full text provided includes introduction/background, methods, results, and discussion, so full-text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical work) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) that includes a matched healthy adult control group (n=22, ages within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results (ToM > Emo > neutral; Table 3) and describes additional group-specific whole-brain contrasts reported in the supplementary materials (separate within-group contrasts). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps for the healthy group reported/available in supplement), and I6 (allowing coordinates/supplement) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly examines social stimulus processing (implicit social content via pictures of humans) within an fMRI task, reported in healthy adult participants (N=28, ages 30–50). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM ANOVA, contrasts, conjunctions) with thresholding and cluster reporting, and provides figures and coordinate tables. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

The study reports an fMRI task probing social-related processing (recall of autobiographical relationship episodes; self- and other-referencing), meeting the review’s construct scope. The sample comprises 35 healthy participants with diagnostic screening and no reported mental disorders (healthy adult group reported). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (self-relevant>control, other>control) with FDR correction, tables of results, and figures—fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; not between-group-only; participants are healthy adults; empirical fMRI data present). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in 'normal subjects' performing social-cognition tasks (attentional and attributional judgements), which fits social-related processing (I3). The results list group-level activations across multiple brain regions (BAs, caudate, cingulate), consistent with whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked findings reported for the healthy group (I5). A healthy adult sample is indicated ('normal subjects') satisfying I4, and reporting of coordinates/regions meets I6. However, only an abstract-like full text is provided here (background, method summary, results, conclusion) rather than the complete article; I cannot verify participant ages, exact sample size, or that whole-brain voxelwise maps (vs. ROI) were used from the full methods/analyses. Therefore inclusion is provisionally supported but fulltext_incomplete=true; recommend obtaining the complete article to confirm details.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test). Participants were healthy adults (n=18 males, mean age 26), and the paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results: one-sample t-test within the placebo (healthy) condition and exploratory whole-brain analyses (P<0.001 uncorrected) with tables/coordinates. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (empathy/social cognition) in healthy adults (n=16 analyzed, mean age ~27.8), using a social-related task (passive viewing of emotional/neutral scenes; social relation manipulation). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task contrasts with voxelwise results (FDR-thresholded maps and peak coordinates in tables) for main effects (emotional content; social relation), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present and complete for screening purposes.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social-related processing (attribution of emotions/mental states to humans and non-human animals) using task-based fMRI (Explicit mentalizing task and Implicit viewing task), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 21–46 with analyses reported for the healthy group, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (conjunctions, whole-brain t-statistic images, cluster-level FWE correction) and provides coordinates and whole-brain maps, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This report presents task-based fMRI of social cognition (Theory of Mind and empathy comic-strip task) in a healthy nonclinical sample (college students, ages 17–21) and explicitly reports group-level, whole-brain SPM activation maps (including pooled-condition analyses and coordinates in supplementary Data S1). Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample; majority within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported for the healthy group), and I6 (maps/coordinates clearly described). No exclusion criteria are triggered (whole-brain results are provided; not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI probing empathy (a social cognition/Perception and Understanding of Others task); (I4) includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, ages 22–47) with results reported separately; (I5) reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps for the healthy/control group (one-sample t-tests, SPM8, cluster tables and figures); (I6) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-group healthy-task effects, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures/tables, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using social-related tasks (self- and mother-referential processing; a social attribution/task) that probe perception/understanding of self and others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (composite t-maps), coordinates, tables of peaks, and statistical thresholds (FDR and uncorrected contrasts), clearly from the healthy/control group. The full-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within adult range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social-cognition tasks (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) satisfying the review topic. It includes a healthy adult control group (13 healthy matched controls) with behavioral and imaging results reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain analyses and group comparisons; within-group results for single groups are indicated as reported in Supplementary Tables S1–S4, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (coordinates/tables acceptable per I6). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, age outside range, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory-of-mind) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants. The fMRI experiment (N=17, mean age 22) used whole-brain SPM analyses with second-level random-effects contrasts (e.g., mentalising > factual; parametric modulation) and reports whole-brain-corrected results (figures and Table 1 with coordinates). Neuroimaging data are also archived (DOI provided). Thus the paper provides group-level, voxelwise task activation maps for a healthy adult sample, addressing social-related processing. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical).

This full text reports an fMRI task investigating reappraisal of angry faces (socially relevant facial-emotion processing), with a healthy adult sample (N=60, age range 18–57) and a separate resting-state subset (N=48). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Decrease vs Observe-angry, Observe-angry > Observe-neutral) with coordinate tables and statistical thresholds (FWE cluster correction), clearly reported for the healthy/control sample. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present and complete. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review and violates no exclusion criteria.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examines social-cognitive processing (evaluation of political beliefs, involving self/other and social judgment). The sample comprises healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (MDS N=24; fMRI N=26; ages 22–45). Group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked analyses are reported (second-level random effects parametric contrasts, whole-brain thresholding and ROI-corrected results; tables/figures present activations). The task (political judgment vs font) indexes social-related processing (perception/understanding of self and others). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This fMRI study (healthy adults N=16, ages 18–26) directly investigates emotion evaluation from vocal and musical stimuli, a form of social-cognitive processing (perception/understanding of others’ emotional states). The task contrasts explicit emotion tracking with an implicit pitch task, meeting the review’s social-related task criterion (I3). The sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65 (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain surface-based analyses (second-level random effects), conjunctions and contrasts with multiple-comparison correction and presents statistical maps/tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, empirical data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-affiliative processing (hand-holding/attachment-like regulation) in healthy adults (mean age ~23.6, n=22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-wise tests via FSL/FEAT) and presents ROI and coordinate results from those multisubject whole-brain contrasts (threat vs safe), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. The study methods, results, and discussion are provided in full. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, not non-empirical).

Exclusion criterion E4 met: the paper reports whole-brain exploratory analyses only for between-group contrasts (healthy>manic, manic>healthy) and does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task: social vs. non-social pictures), I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with results reported), I6 (results and coordinates reported in text/figures/supplement). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map reported specifically for the healthy/control group; within-group healthy results are reported as ROI/SVC analyses only). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social processing (observation of cooperative vs affective social interactions) in healthy adults, meeting the review objective. Sample: 36 healthy right-handed adults (ages ~24–25) reported separately — satisfies I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with statistical maps, corrected thresholds, tables of activations/coordinates and figures (parametric and categorical contrasts) — satisfies I5 and I6. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self- and other-evaluation of personality traits), includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results for the healthy controls (one-sample analyses, flexible factorial, whole-brain Monte Carlo-corrected results reported in tables/figures). Whole-brain contrasts for controls (SELF vs baseline, OTHER vs baseline, conjunction, and SELF vs OTHER) are explicitly described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (the Social Detection Task) to probe perception/understanding of others (I3). It tested a healthy adult sample (N=38; ages 18–30) reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., Social > Non-social contrasts; FWE-corrected results, Table 1; Figures 2–4), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core results are clearly presented. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/highlights/metadata provided), preventing verification of key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task is clearly described). Inclusion criteria not confirmed: I4 (age range/sample details for healthy adults 18–65 not specified in provided content), I5 (no clear statement or evidence in the provided content that a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for healthy participants was reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be positively identified from the available excerpt. Recommend obtaining full article (methods/results) to confirm sample ages and whether whole-brain group analyses were reported.

This empirical study used task-based fMRI during two social-cognitive tasks (emotional perspective-taking and emotion attribution) that target social processing/mentalizing. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=121–129, ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholded contrasts (whole-brain FWE-corrected maps and voxelwise regressions with reported cluster coordinates), clearly attributed to the healthy participant sample. Reporting of whole-brain results in text, figures, and tables meets the reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports fMRI during an interactive mentalizing (prisoner’s dilemma) task in a sample of healthy adults (n=195; fMRI subgroup n=163), addressing social cognition/mentalizing (I3). Participants are healthy adults (I4). The abstract and highlights report task-evoked neural activations across multiple brain regions (bilateral temporal poles, precunei, frontal gyri) and voxel-based morphometry results, indicating whole-brain voxelwise analyses and group-level task effects for the healthy group (I5, I6). However, the provided full text appears to be truncated (highlights, abstract, references) rather than the complete article (missing full methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=true; confidence lowered for that reason. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. No exclusion criteria met.

This study is excluded because it does not use a task-based social fMRI paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports resting-state/structural/diffusion imaging without any healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (contains a healthy adult control group, ages appropriate). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task; the fMRI data are resting-state fALFF), I5 (does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group), and I6 (not applicable because qualifying whole-brain task results are absent). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used task-based fMRI with socially-relevant stimuli (dynamic fearful faces), meeting the social-related task requirement. It includes a separate healthy adult group (n=19, mean age 31.8) with results reported independently and used as the comparison benchmark. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation (face > place) with second-level one-sample t-tests and clusterwise FWE correction, and provides peak coordinates (Table S1) and group activation maps; healthy-control data are described and used in group comparisons, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain map. Results are presented in the main text, figures, and tables. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (round-robin face-viewing and person-judgment localizer, and MID), addressing perception/understanding of others and affiliative processing. Participants were healthy adults (n=26, mean age 28.7). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain random-effects parametric analyses (FWE-corrected clusters reported; Table S4, Fig. S1) demonstrating task-evoked activations in valuation and social-cognition systems; whole-brain results are clearly described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, SI).

This is an empirical fMRI study of motivated social cognition using a social-comparison task (close other vs. non-close other) performed in a sample of healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 18.7). The paper reports group-level, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (SPM{t} maps) and provides peak coordinates and statistical results for task-evoked activations (e.g., Target × Breadth, Valence, Target contrasts). Although multiple-comparison correction was applied within a priori ROIs, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and coordinates are reported in the main text (and figures), satisfying the requirement that qualifying whole-brain results be clearly described. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation/updating of others) using a task that presents faces with valenced behaviors (social perception/understanding of others). Sample: 24 healthy adults aged 18–45, which meets the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses (interaction and L2>F3 contrasts) with thresholding and cluster correction, and refers to whole-brain results in figures/tables/supplements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI data present). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study employing a social cognition paradigm (empathic and forgivability judgments), satisfying I3. It includes a healthy adult comparison group (N=14, mean age 30.5), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation results for the healthy/control group (within- and between-group activation maps, regions and coordinates reported in text and supplements), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, age-exclusion, or non-empirical issues).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract shows an fMRI study of empathy/forgiveness in ten volunteers and reports regional activations, satisfying that this is a social-related fMRI task (I3). However, the manuscript excerpt does not provide participant ages or full participant information to confirm a healthy adult sample within 18–65 (I4 not verifiable), nor does it provide the full methods/results to confirm that at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported (I5 not verifiable). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article (methods/results) to verify I4 and I5.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (false-belief/theory-of-mind; satisfies I3). It includes healthy adult control groups (Caltech n=18, MIT n=462; ages within 18–65) with results reported separately from the patient group (satisfies I4). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked contrasts (Belief > Photo) for healthy/control groups, including whole-brain maps and corrected cluster results (satisfies I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study investigates neural processing of self-construal (general vs contextual self-judgments), which falls squarely under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=24, ages ~21–24 and ~24), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise random-effects analyses (main effects, interaction contrasts, and whole-brain regression), with tables of coordinates and ROI/SVC supplemental analyses; results for the healthy group are clearly reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy group-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This study reports resting-state functional MRI connectivity in a mixed adolescent/young-adult sample (ages 12–23) comparing high-functioning ASD participants and typically developing controls. It does not include any task-based social fMRI paradigm or report a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation map. Therefore it fails the review’s requirement for task-evoked whole-brain healthy adult activation. Exclusion ID(s) met: E3 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity only, without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-based social fMRI), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 not reported separately — participants include minors and no separate adult-only healthy-group maps), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=25, age mean 24) that probes social-related processing (participants evaluated socially constituted meaning of artifacts; contrasts engage mPFC, TPJ, ACC, insula). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM8 random-effects, FDR/FWE-corrected results, tables of coordinates/figures). Tasks clearly target social cognition/understanding of others/self and affiliation-related modulation (relatedness). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a within-subject, double-blind fMRI study using the Cyberball social exclusion task (a social-related task). The sample comprises 21 healthy adults (age 20–37). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., “not receiving ESE > receiving INCL”) and provides uncorrected whole-brain results in Tables S3 and S4 as well as ROI SVC results, clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based fMRI study examining processing of vocal versus non-vocal sounds, which are social-communication relevant stimuli. It reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (vocal > non-vocal) with thresholding and activation maps, in healthy adult samples (Experiment 1: n=13, ages 21–41; Experiment 2: n=18, ages 18–33). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review requirements for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked results; no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only) apply.

The full text reports an fMRI study that used socially relevant stimuli (affiliation/romantic and power film clips) during task performance, meeting I3. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (17 males, mean age 23.6), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (affiliation>control; power>control) with cluster coordinates and significance thresholds reported in text, tables, and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly uses a social-related task—animacy perception (perception/understanding of others)—during task-based fMRI. The sample includes healthy adults (ages 19–36) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, whole-brain FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This study used a resting-state fMRI design and reports connectivity (network-level and node-node) differences arising from instructional manipulations. It does not report any task-evoked, group-level whole-brain activation maps from a social task. Sample consists of healthy adults (n=29, ages 18–22). Therefore it fails the requirement for a whole-brain task activation map and is excluded under E3 (resting-state/connectivity-only without whole-brain task activation). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task — no explicit task; resting state only), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map not reported), I6 (not applicable because no whole-brain task results provided). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study of social gaze processing (mutual vs. averted gaze), meeting the review objective. Sample: healthy adult participants (eight right-handed young adults) are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (across-subject t-statistic activation maps displayed on a standard brain with thresholds reported) in addition to ROI analyses, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within the target age range). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of joint action and social interaction using haptic contact (leading, following, mutual), involving healthy adult dancers (mean age 40.4, N=18), with whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (Talairach coordinates, FDR-corrected maps and tables). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. It meets the meta-analysis objective of social processing in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of moral reasoning, which is a social-related task (moral judgment, self/other understanding). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=28, ages 18–55) with results reported separately (one-sample analyses for HC are described). The manuscript reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group (one-sample analyses, FWE-corrected; Tables and Figures report HC activation), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain healthy-group task effects. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using live face-to-face interaction and a joint-attention task (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (ages 18–29) with group-level results reported for the healthy sample (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Live vs Recorded; Joint Attention vs Solo Attention) with correction for multiple comparisons and provides coordinates/tables/figures of significant clusters (meets I5 and I6). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (Frith–Happé animation ToM task) in adults. The paper includes a clearly-reported healthy/neurotypical control group (n=23, ages 19–56) with results reported separately. The authors conducted whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests for each group at whole-brain level are stated and presented in Supplementary Data 2) and report whole-brain ANOVA and between-group whole-brain contrasts (e.g., NT males > ASD males in right pSTS). Whole-brain results are described in the main text and supplement, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task effects. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) and a non-social control (I3); samples are healthy adults (Exp.1: 20 females, mean age ~20.8; Exp.2: 30 adults, mean age ~21.2) within 18–65 (I4); it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and statistical maps/tables (PD–Gamble contrasts, in-group vs out-group contrasts, connectivity/Granger analyses, Tables 2–5 and figures) clearly identified for the healthy group (I5); whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in text (I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, or between-group-only reporting).

Exclusion IDs met: E2 (study reports ROI-restricted task activation analyses with no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy/control group) and E4 (primary reported neuroimaging effects are group-by-condition interactions/ROI results and connectivity, without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related visual perspective-taking task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported). The methods explicitly state second-level task activation models were restricted to prefrontal ROIs (anterior cingulate, orbitofrontal, DLPFC) and results are presented as ROI analyses; exploratory whole-brain analyses reported are connectivity (seed-based), which do not satisfy the requirement for a whole-brain task activation map. Therefore the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an interactive mentalizing (Prisoner’s Dilemma) paradigm in adults and describes whole-brain task-associated activations (listing bilateral precuneus, cingulate cortices, temporal poles, IFG, TPJ, medial frontal regions, amygdala, etc.). The sample comprises 164 healthy adult subjects. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria for a social-related fMRI task (I3), a healthy adult sample (I4), and reporting of whole-brain group-level task-evoked activations (I5/I6). However, the provided full text appears truncated (only highlights, abstract, abbreviations, and metadata present) and lacks the full methods/results sections in the supplied content, so fulltext_incomplete is set to true; this reduces confidence that all reporting details (e.g., explicit whole-brain voxelwise maps/statistics) are present in the available text. If full article methods/results confirm voxelwise whole-brain group maps, the study is appropriate for inclusion.

This study is excluded because it is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity study in a pediatric sample (age 6.5–18.7), not a task-based fMRI investigation of social processing in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses) and E5 (includes only participants outside the 18–65 adult age range; no healthy adult subgroup reported). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use task-based fMRI of social-related processing), I4 (does not include a healthy adult group aged 18–65), I5 (does not report a whole-brain task-evoked group map for a healthy/control group), I6 (not applicable because no task-based healthy-group whole-brain results are provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (threatening faces) and includes a separately-reported healthy adult control group, the paper reports only region-of-interest (amygdala) analyses rather than any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy/control group. This violates the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group results (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social incentive delay task (social reward with smiling faces) addressing social reward processing (I3). The fMRI cohort comprises healthy adult participants (N=63; ages ~20–36), meeting the adult sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (e.g., whole-brain FWE-corrected activations across conditions; Tables/Figures with whole-brain contrasts and uncorrected whole-brain maps), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5). Results are reported in figures and tables (I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants played Cyberball (social exclusion/inclusion) and made social decisions in a modified Dictator Game while undergoing fMRI. Sample: 26 healthy adult participants (mean age 20.7), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., exclusion no ball > inclusion ball; Excluders > Includers; excluders equality > includers equality), with coordinates and tables of significant clusters. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral and whole-brain neuroimaging results), and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (dynamic social tie formation during a repeated public good game), using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (scanned N=25, ages 22–23). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and coordinates (MNI) with cluster-wise FWE correction; parametric contrasts and coordinates are presented in text/tables/figures. Thus it meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy adult group reported separately). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study examining empathy, Theory of Mind, and self–other differentiation (social cognition) using task fMRI. Sample: 15 healthy adult males aged 18–40 (within 18–65). Analyses: whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts and ANOVA reported with cluster and voxelwise thresholds, coordinate tables and figures; group-level task activation maps for the healthy group are described. The paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full article text provided). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social-related task (attribute framing/self and reflected perspectives), with a healthy adult sample (N=21, ages 19–41) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with coordinates and statistical thresholds (e.g., positive vs negative frame, frame-inconsistent vs frame-consistent). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The study includes a social cognition task from the HCP dataset and reports analyses on 493 healthy adult subjects (within the 18–65 range). The authors derived task-evoked activation patterns using GLM and report mean/group-level activation patterns (e.g., figures and supplementary material referenced, sensitivity analyses comparing model components to task-evoked maps). Thus the paper provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results for healthy participants (not ROI-only), and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI during an emotion discrimination task involving face processing (social perception of others); (I4) sample consists of 38 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 27.5); (I5) it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked SPM results for the contrast FACES>OBJECTS (with thresholds, cluster sizes, figures, and tables); (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures and tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical dataset). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore INCLUDE.

The abstract and metadata indicate an fMRI study of incidental fearful face processing (a social-related task) and the inclusion of a healthy adult control group (13 healthy volunteers), so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the provided full text is incomplete (only metadata/abstract present), so I cannot verify whether the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5). The methods described focus on multivariate connectivity/functional integration analyses, suggesting the possibility that only connectivity results (not unmasked whole-brain task activation maps) are reported. Because I5 cannot be confirmed from the supplied content, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively identified from the available abstract.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a passive viewing facial emotion perception task (social perception of others), includes a healthy adult control group (n=27; ages within 18–65), and reports whole-brain task-evoked analyses. The manuscript describes within-group whole-brain activation results for the groups (with full list of within-group activations noted in the Supplementary material) and presents whole-brain between-group contrasts and figures/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activations for the healthy/control group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported with supplementary material/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes unmasked healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI of Theory of Mind (affective and cognitive), which is a social-related process (meets I3). The sample comprises 23 healthy adult participants drawn from the general population with adult age covariates used (meets I4). The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FDR-corrected cluster results, tables and figures), including regressions of RFQ on BOLD and task contrasts for the healthy group (meets I5 and I6). Results are presented as whole-brain maps/tables and discussed for the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18-22) using a social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) during BOLD fMRI acquisition, satisfying the review focus on social processing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded Z-statistics and FWE cluster correction) and presents whole-brain results (text, figures, and tables) derived from the healthy sample (including analyses of treatment and methylation interactions as well as subgroup analyses). Core article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present in the supplied full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses task-based fMRI to investigate facial color processing, which pertains to social-related perception of others (social communication/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (n=25, mean age 25.24), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (natural-colored face vs. natural-colored scrambled image) and identifies face-selective regions (bilateral FFA and OFA) from group-level analyses, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical article) are met.

Full text is not provided (only abstract/metadata), so I cannot verify whether the paper reports a healthy-group, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map (I5). From the abstract, I3 (task-based fMRI of a social construct: theory of mind) and I4 (includes healthy younger and older adult groups) appear satisfied. However I5 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed from the available content. No exclusion criteria are explicitly met based on the abstract alone, but because a required inclusion criterion (I5) cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, I must exclude pending full-text verification.

This study reports task-based fMRI of live verbal social interaction (dyadic communication), using healthy adult participants (22 women, mean age ~27). Group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses are reported (second-level voxel-wise t-tests, cluster-correction, tables/figures referenced), showing task-evoked activations for listening, talking, and coupling analyses. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study of social/attachment-related processing (implicit attitudes toward adultery, regulation of interest in extra-pair relationships) using tasks tied to affiliation/attachment and perception of others. Sample: healthy adult participants (right-handed heterosexual males, ages 20–32) meeting the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, within-group whole-brain task activation analyses for the IAT (incongruent vs. congruent) with appropriate voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds; results are presented as whole-brain contrasts and tables of activations. Although the go/no-go contrast used an ROI constraint for VLPFC, the study nevertheless provides unmasked, whole-brain IAT task effects for the healthy group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (social reflection: self and other judgments) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 22 healthy adult participants (mean age 37.4), meeting the age and healthy-group requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results for the SR>AL contrast using cortical surface–based analyses with cluster-wise correction (Monte Carlo simulation) and presents cortical surface maps and tables of activations/peaks; thus it provides unmasked, within-healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps (figures/tables/coordinates). Resting-state connectivity analyses are secondary and do not negate the presence of task-based whole-brain results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is not accessible (site shows a privacy/cookie preference page), so core article content (methods, results) cannot be evaluated. I cannot confirm whether the study used task-based fMRI for social-related processing (I3), included a healthy adult group with results reported separately (I4), or reported whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria can be definitively identified from the available content. Recommendation: obtain the full article PDF or contact authors to reassess eligibility.

This fMRI study investigates affective theory-of-mind (a social cognitive task) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=22, 21 analyzed; mean age 23.7), reports behavioral and group-level whole-brain task contrasts (EFE > no EFE, interaction effects) with tables/figures and ROI as well as whole-brain results, and provides coordinates and statistical maps described in the text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full article reports task-based fMRI during social-related stimuli (social interaction, faces, erotica) in healthy control adults. A healthy control group (n=14, mean age 28.2) is reported separately and compared with depressed patients. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (voxel-by-voxel repeated-measures ANOVAs), with clusters and tables of regions reported (Tables 3–5) and figures illustrating activation patterns; simple-effects analyses describe within-group control responses. Results are presented as whole-brain group-level task-evoked effects in the control group. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an fMRI task study of perception/anticipation of others' actions, directly addressing social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Participants are healthy players (recreational, club/county, national/international) indicating adult healthy groups. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with thresholded voxelwise results and peak coordinates (experiment 1 and experiment 2 ROI selection based on whole-brain results), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Results are reported in-text and tables (coordinates). No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Caveat: participant ages are not explicitly listed in the provided text, but the sample description (competitive adult players) supports inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: []

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy/social cognition (perception and understanding of others), meeting the review objective. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (participants imagined and rated others' pain) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Pain > No Pain; No Pain: Dissimilar > Similar) with stereotactic coordinates, thresholds, tables, and figures. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=23, ages 19–34). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, experimental design, MRI acquisition and preprocessing, statistical analysis), Results (behavioral, fMRI localization, connectivity, eye tracking), and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=25, mean age 23.2) using an explicit social mentalizing task about friends and kin during task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (friend > kin contrast and parametric linear analyses across network layers) with cluster-thresholded statistical maps and tables of activation peaks. All required reporting formats (tables/figures/text) are present. Although the sample is female-only, it meets the healthy adult criterion and results are reported for that healthy group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related legal decision-making task that probes social cognition (inferences about others’ mental states and responsibility), satisfying the review’s social-processing scope. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=20 analyzed; ages 18–45), meeting the age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (multiple whole-brain main effects and contrasts described in the Results and reported as tables of peak coordinates), which fulfills the whole-brain evidence requirement; the manuscript explicitly describes whole-brain contrasts and provides tables of coordinates and corrected results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This study used fMRI during a social-evaluation task (I3 met). However, the sample comprises adolescents aged 13–19 (healthy control group 13–19) and the paper does not report a separate healthy adult (18–65) subgroup—so inclusion criterion I4 is not met. The manuscript also does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map reported specifically for a healthy adult/control group (I5 not met). Therefore exclusion criteria E5 (participants outside the 18–65 adult range without a separately analyzed healthy adult subgroup) and E4 (no accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text incomplete: the provided content contains only article metadata/metrics and navigation text, without core article sections (methods, participants, results). Cannot confirm inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task) cannot be verified; I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) cannot be verified; I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map from healthy/control group) cannot be verified; I6 (acceptable formats for whole-brain results) cannot be verified. Therefore the study cannot be confirmed as eligible and is excluded. No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are demonstrably met from the available information.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (imagined triadic interactions) in healthy adults. It meets inclusion criteria: I3 - uses task-based fMRI probing social cognition (triad/self/other conditions); I4 - sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 18–35) with results reported for the healthy group; I5 - reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., triad>iron, conjunction analyses) with whole-brain FWE correction and cluster reporting; I6 - whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and this is empirical data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task-based fMRI to examine observation of virtual social interactions (I3); participants are described as recruited on basis of age and health and results are reported for a healthy participant group (data from 15 participants), satisfying I4 (ages not explicitly listed but recruitment language and typical adult sample in JoVE imply healthy adults 18–65); the paper reports group-level whole-brain activation maps/contrast (Figure 1 activation maps, whole-brain coverage described), satisfying I5; results are presented as figures of activation maps and ROI time courses, consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and present unmasked group task activations. The provided full text includes methods, scanning parameters, data analysis, and representative results, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (modified Cyberball) explicitly addressing social evaluative exclusion/stress (relevant to affiliation/understanding of others and self). Sample: 40 healthy adults (mean age 27.8), meeting the 18–65 healthy adult requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses (random-effects GLM), with voxel-level FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures (multiple contrasts and a conjunction; Tables 1–2 and Online Resources). Full article contains introduction, methods, results and discussion.
