No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, ages within range, and empirical with original fMRI data). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This empirical fMRI study investigates political attitudes (a social cognition task involving perception/understanding of others) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (final N=24, ages 21–40) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts and whole-brain correction (FDR) and coordinate tables. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=178, mean age 40.9) using the EmpaToM paradigm assessing empathy and theory-of-mind (social-related constructs). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (one-sample t-tests for empathy and ToM contrasts) with reported activation peaks/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Although additional connectivity/DCM and resting-state analyses are included, the paper clearly provides unmasked, within-healthy-group task activation maps and coordinates. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This empirical study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=26 with usable fMRI data; behavioral n=58) who performed a social-sharing vs alone task, addressing affiliation-related processing. The sample age range (20–33) is within 18–65 and healthy volunteers were used. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (shared_emo > unshared_emo) including whole-brain analyses and cluster-level correction, and additionally reports ROI and whole-brain results (e.g., DLPFC and precuneus with whole-brain correction; Table 1, figures). Whole-brain results are clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports original fMRI data in healthy adult subjects (N=13, mean age 27.2) who passively watched video clips depicting social interactions, directly addressing social-related processing (I3). Methods and results present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (ANOVA; voxelwise P≤0.05 corrected across the whole brain) with tables and figures showing activations (DMPFC, precuneus, STS), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5, I6). The healthy adult sample meets the age and health criteria (I4). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range-age-only, or non-empirical paper. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (dishonesty/prosocial decision-making) and reports whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, and the participant is a healthy adult (age 22). However, the paper reports data from a single subject (n=1) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map derived from a group of healthy adults. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (group-level whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult participant present), I6 (whole-brain results acceptable in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain healthy-group map). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded.

This study uses fMRI during a social-evaluation task (meets I3), includes healthy adult participants in the sample (ages up to 22.9; meets I4), and reports whole-brain results/coordinates (meets I6). However, the authors analyze age as a continuous variable across a mixed-age sample (8–22.9 years) and report age-related effects (e.g., adolescent-emergent MPFC activation) rather than providing a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from a healthy adult subgroup (age 18–65). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social interaction task) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The methods and results report group-level, voxelwise analyses including whole-brain analyses (e.g., main effect CD>CC and complementary whole-brain analyses of drug effects), with activation tables and figures described in the text and supplements. The sample consists of healthy adult men and women with results reported for these healthy groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group maps or whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition/empathy using a dynamic multimodal social task (meets I3). It includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (n=24, mean age 35.25) separate from clinical groups (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (random-effects GLM, Monte-Carlo cluster correction) and within-group T-contrasts with coordinates and figures/tables that describe activations for each participant group, including controls (meets I5). Whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures (meets I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and within-group whole-brain healthy-control effects are reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (gaze-mediated social stimuli vs nonsocial stimuli) while participants performed a stimulus–response compatibility task. Participants were healthy adults (N=23, ages 21–37). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM second-level ANOVA), cluster- and voxel-thresholds, and tables/figures of activations (main effects and interactions), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 22–35) that examines social communication (co-speech gestures) during a naturalistic narrative. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., low_ID>high_ID, speech>gestures+speech, gestures+speech>speech) with coordinate tables, cluster extents, and thresholding procedures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group voxelwise activation maps clearly. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-attribution (People vs Bumper) task (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=17, ages 18–45) with results reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and group maps for the control group (one-sample t-tests and CON group maps are described and shown) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). Results are presented in figures and tables (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria are met: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy maps, participants are within age range, and it is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluations), using tasks directly relevant to perception/understanding of self (social cognition). The sample consists of healthy adults (final N=31, ages 19–24). The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts and regression analyses (e.g., SA vs. Fixation, SC vs. SA) with voxel-wise and cluster-level FWE correction, and provide tables of coordinates and figures. PPI connectivity analyses are supplementary but do not replace whole-brain task activations. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This fMRI study investigates explicit vs implicit processing of facial emotions (social communication/perception of others) in healthy adults using task-based fMRI. The sample includes 29 healthy adults aged 20–35. The paper reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps and whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected results are described and tabulated), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (minimal-group affiliation/group categorization) in healthy adults (N=20 analyzed, mean age 23.4), using simultaneous EEG-fMRI during a social task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (whole-brain fMRI results with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates reported in Table 1; clusters in mPFC and right STS/TPJ) tied to ERP measures. All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-reference and other-reference) in healthy adults. Sample: 110 healthy participants aged 19–31 (meets adult 18–65 requirement). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM results (contrasts SR+OR > baseline; SR > OR; OR > SR) with whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds and presents activation maps/tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction (gaze-based joint attention) in healthy adults (n=24; ages 20–34). It includes group-level, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., self>other; JA>NJA) with reported peak coordinates and statistical inference (SVC-corrected FWE) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for fMRI social-related task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level task results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of empathy for pain manipulating ingroup/outgroup membership (a social-related task addressing perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises 30 healthy adults (ages 18–35). The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 repeated-measures ANOVA) with tables of activations (main effects and interactions) and FWE-corrected results; whole-brain maps/coordinates are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical data present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only highlights, abstract, abbreviations, keywords, and references provided). Based on available content: Inclusion I3 is satisfied (fMRI study of social cognition—theory of mind during cooperation vs competition). I4 (healthy adult sample) cannot be confirmed because participant demographics and sample description are not present. I5 (reporting at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone; univariate and multivariate analyses are mentioned but no explicit whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinates are provided. Therefore I4 and I5 are not met/verified. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the provided text. Because key information (methods, participants, whole-brain results) is missing, the study cannot be confidently included. fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (joint attention/gaze perception) in healthy adults (ages 20–31). The methods describe fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, and the Results report group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (place>body and body>place contrasts) with maps and a summary table of activation peaks, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy group. The study explicitly addresses perception and understanding of others and reports group-level statistical maps and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI task of social gaze/joint attention (social-related task) and includes a healthy adult control group. The manuscript presents within-group (one-sample) activation results for controls (self-initiated JA > NJA), reporting significant activations in mOFC, mPFC, and PCC with coordinates/figures referenced (Table S4, Fig. S4) and describes whole-brain analysis procedures (one-sample t test thresholded at uncorrected P < 0.005, with ROI small-volume correction applied). Thus it meets: I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (group-level control task contrast reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=17 analyzed) using a task that probes understanding of others’ actions (why/how questions), i.e., social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (cluster-forming threshold p<0.001 with cluster-level FWE correction) and ROI and whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Age range of participants (21–46) falls within 18–65. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task activation maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group whole-brain task effects; participants within age range; empirical fMRI data present). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided.

The study is an fMRI investigation of social cognitive processing (causal attributions/mentalizing), uses a healthy adult sample (N=20; ages 18–41), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (ANOVA, contrasts, conjunctions) with whole-brain and small-volume FWE-corrected results and voxelwise thresholds described. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI of impression formation (social evaluation of others), meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample = 20 healthy adult males (ages 19–31), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper includes an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis (ANOVA) with reported threshold, clusters, tables and figures describing whole-brain activations from the healthy group, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are presented in text, table(s), and figures. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social task (modified cyber-ball and face viewing pre/post learning), satisfying I3. Sample comprises 15 healthy young adults (mean age 24.1), satisfying I4. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain searchlight analysis with corrected results (significant post-vs-pre changes in superior temporal sulcus reported at MNI coordinates), which constitutes whole-brain voxelwise task-related group results satisfying I5 (and I6 acceptable). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, and empirical fMRI data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (integration of speaker characteristics and sentence content — social communication/person perception). It includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=24, ages 18–39) and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the control group (within-group contrasts and whole-brain random-effects analyses, reported in text, tables and figures). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (the ultimatum game) in healthy adult participants (male, ages 23–28), meeting I3 and I4. The manuscript includes whole-brain, cross-subject offline classification analyses with voxelwise discriminating volumes reported as MNI coordinates, thresholding (p<0.05) and cluster sizes, and accompanying figures/tables (i.e., group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables), meeting I5 and the acceptable reporting format in I6. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (erotic and fearful social scenes and emotional faces) and a placebo-controlled intranasal oxytocin manipulation. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI with social/attachment-related stimuli), I4 (healthy adult sample, N=55, mean age 24.9), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and T-maps for main effects and substance effects, with FWE-corrected results), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of dynamic happy and fearful facial expression processing (a social perception/understanding of others task) in young adult participants. The paper includes at least one healthy adult group (matched control group, ages in early twenties) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the study groups (within-group activation/deactivation maps thresholded and displayed; Fig.2 and accompanying results). Whole-brain analyses were performed with FLAME and thresholding reported, and results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. The report also includes acceptable presentation of whole-brain results (figures/tables) and meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered (the study also includes ROI and PPI analyses but does not rely solely on them). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication: participants performed a referential communication (director–matcher) task and retrieved collaboratively vs. individually learned labels during fMRI, a clear social-related task. The sample includes healthy adult participants (directors and matchers; reported ages 18–33; n=70 reported), satisfying the age and healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts, cluster-level correction, tables and figures listing activated clusters), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements; results are reported in tables/figures as allowed. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext appears complete. Although an ROI analysis of the hippocampus was also performed, whole-brain analyses are present (so E2 is not met). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing/representation of others’ mental states) using a task that elicited thoughts about others’ mental states, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants (ages 18–27), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (searchlight representational similarity analysis and network-level random-effects one-sample t tests) with corrected statistical maps and tables (Figs. 2–4, Tables S2–S3), satisfying I5 and I6. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (behavioral ratings, PCA, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, GLM, searchlight and network analyses), so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical article) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social cooperation (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma), conducted in healthy adult participants (mean age 21). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (e.g., CC vs. other outcomes) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, within age range, empirical).

This is an fMRI study of gaze processing (a social perception task) that includes a typically developing control group and reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts for the healthy/control group (Direct > Averted gaze; Table 2) with coordinates and cluster statistics. The healthy group includes adults (ages 16.1–42.4, mean 24.2) and results for the typically developing group are reported separately. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses fMRI with a social cognitive task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes) and includes a healthy control group, but it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The presented results focus on between-group contrasts (control vs. high-risk) and small-volume-corrected findings; no clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task effect (main effect or within-group contrast for controls) is reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task) and I4 (contains a healthy adult control group). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no reported whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test) in healthy adult participants (16 right-handed women, mean age 20.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (emotion vs control) with cluster-forming threshold p<0.001 and FWE cluster-level correction; results are presented in figures and tables. Thus the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (I3), includes healthy adult participants within 18–65 (I4), reports whole-brain group-level task activation maps clearly from the healthy group (I5), and presents results in accepted formats (tables/figures) (I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of biological motion perception, which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age 28.2, n=13) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (canonical vs scrambled biological motion) with corrected statistics, coordinates, figures and tables of activation (whole-brain voxelwise results). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study used fMRI during a social-related (dynamic face) task (I3) and included a healthy adult control group aged 18–65 (I4). However, the paper only reports between-group (patient vs. control) whole-brain contrasts and group-difference maps; it does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

While the study uses fMRI with a social-related task (peer likeability/acceptance) and reports whole-brain results (I3 and I6 satisfied), it does not provide group-level whole-brain task activation maps that are clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control adult group. The sample (ages 18–21) includes healthy and clinical participants (e.g., current MDD) and all reported group-level whole-brain analyses are conducted across the mixed sample or are regression-based; no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group map or separately reported healthy-group results are presented. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. Full text appears complete.

Provided full text appears to be only an abstract/summary. The study clearly used fMRI with social-related tasks (viewing/imitating/producing facial expressions and social hand gestures), so I3 is satisfied. However the manuscript excerpt does not report participant details (age range and health status) so I4 cannot be confirmed. The provided content also does not include methods/results sections or explicit group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps or coordinates clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group, so I5 (and I6) cannot be verified. Because the full text is incomplete, key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed; therefore the study is excluded from the review at this stage pending the complete article. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available excerpt.

This is an fMRI study examining social processing during naturalistic movie viewing, focusing on DMPFC responses to social interactions (meets I3). The sample comprises 34 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.2), within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (a whole-brain reverse-correlation/χ2 voxelwise map shown in Figure 3 and described in the text), providing task-evoked whole-brain statistical results for the healthy group (meets I5). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (meets I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it used resting-state functional connectivity MRI rather than a task-based fMRI social paradigm (does not meet I3), the sample consists of adolescents aged 11–18 rather than healthy adults 18–65 (does not meet I4), and it does not report any whole-brain, task-evoked activation maps for a healthy adult control group (does not meet I5). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a task activation map) and E5 (participants are outside the 18–65 age range). No inclusion criteria are satisfied. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

The study used task-based fMRI of facial emotional processing (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I4). However, the reported results in the full text are presented as between-group contrasts (VCFS vs controls) and Table 1 lists between-group differences; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map or within-group (control) whole-brain activation map/coordinates clearly identified as from the healthy group. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). The provided full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition (Theory of Mind) task (animated interacting shapes) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activations for healthy adult controls (ages 22–56). The methods describe whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with corrected group results and within-group maps for healthy subjects, and results are reported in tables and figures. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The study uses an fMRI task of negative emotion processing (IAPS) rather than a social-related task probing affiliation, social communication, or perception/understanding of self/others. Thus it does not meet inclusion criterion I3. It does meet I4 (healthy adult sample, N=46, ages 18–45), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for HA− > neutral), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because I3 is not satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social evaluation (trustworthiness judgments of faces) in healthy adults (final N=14; ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level random-effects analyses and statistical parametric maps, provides coordinate tables and figures describing whole-brain task-evoked activations (with small-volume corrections reported where applicable). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses fMRI with a social-related task (Theory of Mind) and includes a healthy adult control group (mean age 55, range 35–75), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. Analyses were restricted to predefined ROIs with small-volume correction and the reported results focus on between-group contrasts (ALS>HC) rather than a healthy-group within-group activation map. Therefore it fails to meet I5 and meets exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI-restricted results/no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports primarily between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

The study uses task-based fMRI of a social-related process (eye-gaze/intention processing), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates for the neurologically normal (control) group (I3, I5, I6 satisfied). However, the reported healthy/control group includes participants with ages reported as 15.5–32.4 years (mean 23.4), so the control sample includes minors and the paper does not present a separate analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–65. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult group, age 18–65) is not met. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) directly apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded for failing I4.

This fMRI study examines face-emotion discrimination (a social cognitive task: perception/understanding of others), uses task-based fMRI, and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (one-sample t-tests and contrasts across participants and group comparisons) with tables of activations. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (two groups of community adults screened for Axis I disorders), and results for the healthy groups are reported. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The paper reports an fMRI study of a social-related task (Social motor response learning involving social inclusion/exclusion) in healthy adults, satisfying I3. The sample included 18 healthy subjects (mean age 42 ±12), meeting I4 (healthy adults within 18–65). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with FDR whole-brain correction (P<0.05) and present tables/figures of activations (ventral striatum, frontal operculum, dACC), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, age range appropriate, and is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/summary provided). Although the study uses fMRI of face perception/emotion (meets I3: social-related task), the available text does not report participant demographics/ages or clearly present group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for a healthy adult group. Therefore I cannot verify I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) or I5 (whole-brain evidence). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met based on the provided content, but because core full-text methods/results are missing, the study must be excluded pending full-text verification.

This study reports an fMRI task examining voice (socially relevant) versus non-voice sounds, addressing social perception (I3). It includes a separate healthy adult control group (8 age-matched adults, results reported separately) meeting the sample requirement (I4). The paper presents group-level whole-brain analyses for the control group (random-effects and fixed-effect analyses showing voice>non-voice activation along the STS, P<0.001 corrected), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (figures/tables/supplement) per I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplementary material noted but not required. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (third-party punishment/attribution of moral responsibility), meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample: 26 healthy adults (mean age 26, range within 18–65), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported (random-effects GLM; whole-brain FDR q<0.05) with reported activations and Talairach coordinates (R TPJ, R anterior insula), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results and maps are described in the text and figures. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects).

The study reports an fMRI task that probes social/moral behavior (charitable donation — affiliation/attachment and moral decision-making), uses a healthy adult sample (N=19, mean age 28.2, within 18–65), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (GLM, random-effects, contrasts; coordinates/tables in supporting information). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and participants are within the age range).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses task-based fMRI during a social perception task (passive viewing of biological motion) (I3); includes a healthy adult sample reported separately (n=48, ages 20–35) (I4); reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the healthy adult group (e.g., biological > scrambled; Sex×Condition ANOVA) with cluster correction and tables/figures of coordinates (I5); and whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-cognitive process: Perception and Understanding of Self), conducted in healthy adult participants (12 right-handed males, mean age ~19). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (e.g., unknown vs scrambled, familiar vs unknown, self vs familiar) analyzed in SPM2 with thresholding and cluster reporting; results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI of a social-related gaze-following paradigm (I3); includes a healthy adult sample (N=28; ages 18–36) reported separately (I4); reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (incongruent > congruent) with cluster correction and tables/figures (I5); and whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of empathy for pain (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=13; mean age 33 ± 9) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts and tables/figures of activations for the control group (e.g., Painful − Nonpainful and Painful − Baseline contrasts; Tables 2 and 4; Figure 1). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI task study of social cognition (Theory of Mind) using the REMICS task, directly assessing social-related processing and contextual adjustments (meets I3). Sample comprises 19 healthy adult participants aged 20–53 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (one-sample t-tests, voxelwise thresholding, cluster correction) with tables of peak coordinates and figures clearly attributed to the healthy group (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not solely connectivity or resting-state, and report healthy-group whole-brain task effects. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of a social cognitive task (false belief/theory-of-mind), meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample: 34 healthy adults (age 20–28), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (ROMS vs CTRL) with activation maps and coordinate tables, fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, behavioral and fMRI procedures, data analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults: participants (N=20 healthy males, age range 21–37) performed an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social decision-making task) while undergoing task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests, flexible factorial models) with FWE cluster-corrected maps and tables/figures of activations for task phases and treatment/opponent effects. Trust ratings, behavioral analyses, and whole-brain neuroimaging results for the healthy sample are clearly reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social processing: participants played a social (human confederate) vs computer resource-conflict task during fMRI. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (contrasts such as Human Conflict > No Conflict; conjunctions; tables and figures; thresholds reported). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task effects), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study directly manipulated social content (trustworthiness judgments) during an n-back task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with tables/coordinates of peak voxels and cluster corrections. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (final imaging N=14, mean age 22) within 18–65. The manuscript includes methods, results, and discussion (full experimental details and whole-brain activation maps/tables), meeting all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind; Why/How task) in healthy adult participants (Study 1 N=29, Study 3 N=21; ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Why>How, How>Why; Belief>Photo) with cluster- and voxel-level FWE correction and tables of peak coordinates. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, age-appropriate, and empirical). Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only metadata and cookie notice provided). Cannot confirm required inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none (insufficient information to apply E2-E6). Inclusion IDs met: none (cannot confirm I3, I4, I5). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (unable to verify that the study reports fMRI task results specifically from a healthy/control group — title implies affective theory of mind but full methods/results are missing), I4 (cannot confirm that at least one healthy adult group (18–65) is reported separately), I5 (cannot confirm that a whole-brain, group-level healthy-task activation map or corresponding coordinates are reported). Because core article content (methods/results) is missing, inclusion criteria cannot be verified and study must be excluded pending full text.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (race perception and trustworthiness evaluations) using a task involving face perception and trustworthiness—clearly a social-related task. Participants were 30 healthy adult (White) volunteers aged 18–29, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task contrasts (e.g., Black > White) and covariate analyses, with tables of peak coordinates and figures described in the text, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results include task-evoked activations and PPI connectivity, but are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From abstract, the study used dyadic fMRI during eye contact, so I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) is reasonably satisfied. However critical information is missing: participant details and healthy adult sample not reported (I4 not verifiable), and no clear report or access to a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for a healthy/control group (I5 not verifiable). Because core sections (methods, participants, whole-brain results) are not available in the provided content, I cannot confirm inclusion criteria I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied from the available text. Per screening rules, exclude when any inclusion criterion is not met or cannot be confirmed. Excluded due to incomplete full text preventing verification of I4 and I5.

This article reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants using a social cognition paradigm (EmpaToM) that manipulates empathy and Theory of Mind. Healthy adult samples are reported across experiments (N=25, N=65, N=178; mean ages within 18–65). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., emotionally negative > neutral videos; ToM > nonToM questions), thresholding and tables of peak coordinates (Tables 1–5, Supplementary tables) and figures illustrating whole-brain activation and contrasts. Behavioral and imaging results for the healthy groups are reported separately. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and supplementary references; core article content appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–25) using a social task (competitive matching-pennies game following social interactions with human/robot/computer agents). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects second-level one-sample t-tests, voxel-wise threshold and cluster FWE correction) with tables/figures of activated regions. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and is empirical).

This fMRI study addresses social processing (emotion recognition) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, although the paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (group effects and group × emotion interactions) and ROI results, it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (e.g., within-group healthy main effect or healthy-group contrasts reported with whole-brain coordinates). The reported whole-brain results are primarily between-group contrasts and interactions, and amygdala findings are largely from ROI analyses or patient-focused correlations. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates emotional sentence attribution (a social-cognition task involving perception/understanding of others’ emotions and ToM) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=25). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (FWE-corrected) for the main task effect and a Group and Task×Group interaction; the text and figures explicitly describe healthy-control activation (e.g., controls significantly activated mPFC during emotion attribution). Therefore it meets the social-processing task requirement (I3), includes a healthy adult sample (I4), and provides whole-brain healthy-group task-related results/maps (I5), with whole-brain results presented in figures/tables as described (I6). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of social cognition (empathic concern) in healthy adults (N=26, mean age 30.3). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts (FWE-corrected clusters, tables, and figures) alongside connectivity (DCM) analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during a social Theory-of-Mind task (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=25, ages reported 18–60) with results presented separately (meets I4). The authors conducted whole-brain voxelwise analyses (initial voxel threshold reported, whole-brain contrasts described) and report brain regions activated during ToM conditions in tables/figures and text, indicating group-level whole-brain task-evoked results that include/control-group findings (meets I5). Reporting of whole-brain results appears in tables and figures and is described in the text (meets I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and core data are reported; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI hyperscanning study using a social joint-attention task (sender/receiver paradigm) — satisfying I3. Samples are healthy adult volunteers (discovery n=26, replication n=50; ages ~23–24), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain spatial component maps derived from group ICA and statistical tests showing components’ task associations (repeated-measures ANOVA) and component spatial maps identifying rTPJ involvement; these constitute whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results reported in figures/tables/supplement, meeting I5 and I6. The study also includes replication and behavioral validation. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, includes within-group whole-brain results, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This article reports task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (face-based trustworthiness judgments with feedback), meeting I3. The sample includes a younger healthy adult group aged 20–33, satisfying the 18–65 requirement in I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA within a combined mask and a whole-brain ANOVA reproducing effects) and presents significant task and group effects at the whole-brain level (I5); results are clearly described in text/tables/figures (I6). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts without unmasked healthy-group task maps, out-of-range-only samples, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social-related task (viewing dynamic facial expressions), included a healthy adult sample (n=40, mean age ~30), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (dynamic > static) with coordinates and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From available content: study uses fMRI during a social-related face-perception task (meets I3). However, participant ages/health status are not reported in the provided text (cannot confirm I4). The paper’s abstract mentions amygdala BOLD and an ROI-based analysis, but the provided content does not clearly report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group (I5 not confirmed). Because core methodological/results details are missing, I cannot verify required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively confirmed from the truncated text. Recommend obtaining the full article to reassess.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N≈36, ages ~21) that used a social-related task (viewing others in pain; empathy/perception of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts (painful vs non-painful) with FDR-corrected voxelwise results and tables/figures of activations, and also describes methods, results, and discussion in full. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and supplementary analyses described, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures) in a sample of healthy young adults (mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (TFCE with permutation testing) with results described in text, figures, and tables. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group reported), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps/contrasts), and I6 (results reported as maps/tables/figures). None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants include adults within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used whole-brain voxelwise analyses of BOLD responses to natural movies and explicitly models responses to social communication (a social-related construct). Subjects were healthy adults (N=6; mean age 26.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results and maps (aggregated across subjects and hemispheres) and presents group-level analyses and visualizations, satisfying reporting of whole-brain task-evoked effects. Although the task involved passive viewing, the authors explicitly analyzed and reported neural responses to social communication categories, which fits the review’s definition of social-related processing. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used face viewing (social perception) and includes healthy adult participants (ages 18–37), but the reported whole-brain analyses focus on developmental (age) regression across a mixed-age sample rather than providing a group-level, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from a healthy adult group alone. Inclusion met: I3 (social-related fMRI task — face perception) and I4 (healthy adult participants present). Inclusion not met: I5 — no clearly identified whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map for the healthy adult group is reported (analyses are across the full age range or age-related contrasts). Exclusion applied: E4 (reports only age-related/between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study addresses social processing (dynamic emotional facial expressions) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, although the paper reports whole-brain searchlight results (combined sample) and ROI-based within-group results, it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone in the provided full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Per the review exclusion rules, this fits exclusion criterion E4 (no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on missing required healthy-group whole-brain map; other inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining mirror neuron system responses and the modulation by emotional (social-cognitive) stimuli in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: emotion processing and perception/understanding of others via mirror system paradigms), I4 (healthy adult sample, n=19, mean age ~27.7 within 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, including whole-brain corrected analyses and activation maps/tables), and I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described and presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, reports healthy-group task effects, empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating perception of others’ emotions (facial expressions and prosody), which falls under social-related processing (social communication / perception and understanding of others). Participants are healthy adults (university students aged 19–24). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level task analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA and simple-effects paired t-tests) with FWE-corrected results and tables/figures of activated clusters, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study investigating social processing (gaze following and observed eye contact), satisfying the social-task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=21, mean age 24.6), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (multiple contrasts, thresholding, and tables/figures with coordinates), providing whole-brain evidence for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (audiovisual integration of nonverbal emotional signals from voice and face) in healthy adult participants (N=24, mean age 26.6). It reports group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., conjunction (AV > A) AND (AV > V)), random-effects analyses, voxelwise correlation analyses, and tables/figures of whole-brain results (with small-volume corrections noted). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social tasks in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task-evoked maps.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social decision-making (modified prisoner’s dilemma) task assessing Theory of Mind processes (satisfies I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (N=20, ages 23–45) reported separately (satisfies I4). The paper provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group (e.g., conjunction and HC (Task > CONT) contrasts; cluster-level corrected maps and tables are reported), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, figures/tables, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (emotion/face matching) and includes a healthy adult comparison group (n=12, ages ~32) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and within-group (Emotion Match > Shape Match) contrasts for the healthy group (Table 1; whole-brain random effects analyses described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). From the abstract, the study used fMRI during a face-processing task (meets I3). The abstract mentions comparisons to control subjects, but it does not provide sufficient evidence to confirm there is a healthy adult group (ages 18–65) with results reported separately (I4 not verifiable). It is also unclear whether the paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group (I5/I6 not verifiable). Because the full article (methods, detailed results, and figures/tables) is missing, I cannot confirm whole-brain task activation reporting and therefore cannot include the study. Recommend retrieving the complete full text to reassess inclusion.

This fMRI study examines social processing (eye contact and mimicry), using a task explicitly probing social communication and affiliation-related mimicry (meets I3). Sample: 20 healthy adults (mean age 23) with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Congruent>Catch, Direct> Averted, interaction contrasts) with thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates in Table 1 (meets I5 and I6). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results (GLM and DCM), and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state results, and reports unmasked healthy-group whole-brain activations. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (empathy/familiarity) in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 23.6). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (threat vs safe) with conjunction analyses and voxelwise covariate analyses, provides coordinates, figures, cluster thresholds and tables, and describes methods and results in full. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented via figures/tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (emotion processing and theory of mind) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, age 28.4±8.3) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy controls (within-group contrasts, thresholding and figures/tables shown). Whole-brain results for controls are described separately (figures and supplementary tables), and reporting meets acceptable formats (figures/tables/text). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 21–32) that used task-based paradigms probing social-related processing (personal prayer vs controls) and explicitly interprets activations as social-cognitive/theory-of-mind processing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM, second-level, thresholds P<0.05 FDR corrected) with tables of coordinates and contrasts (individual contrasts and interaction effects) clearly derived from the healthy participant group. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for task-based whole-brain activation maps in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception using naturalistic videos of cooperation vs non-cooperation (meets I3). The sample includes 19 healthy adult controls (matched to patient group) and reports healthy-group results separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps/contrasts for the healthy control group (e.g., C+ > C– within controls, FDR-corrected, coordinates and figures/tables provided), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (meets I5 and I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported, participants are adult, and this is original empirical work).

This is an fMRI study using a task that probes social-related processing (evaluative judgments of self-conscious moral emotions: guilt and embarrassment). The sample comprises 19 healthy adult participants (ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (contrasts G−N, E−N; thresholds and tables of coordinates and figures are provided). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of empathy/perspective-taking (social cognition) in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 21–31). It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (paired t-tests, conjunctions) with cluster- and peak-level FWE correction and reports coordinate tables and time-course analyses. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study investigates face processing (a social-related task) with fMRI and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map (e.g., faces>houses) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The paper presents a whole-brain faces>houses map for the combined sample (n=28) and reports group differences and ROI analyses for the control group, but no NT-only whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level map or table of coordinates for the healthy group is provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/ROI results for group-specific effects without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related face-processing task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately in behavioral/ROI analyses), and I6 (reporting format acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map).

The full text reports whole-brain results collapsed across all subjects and a between-group contrast (NT > ASD), but does not provide an explicit unmasked, voxelwise, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control (NT) group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult control group present). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map reported). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (study reports a between-group contrast without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-interaction task (an fMRI-adapted Taylor Aggression Paradigm presenting angry vs. neutral opponent videos) in healthy adult participants (32 analyzed males, mean age 23.3). The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (angry>neutral) with cluster-wise FWE control and lists whole-brain results (Tables, Figures) for decision and outcome phases. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, ages within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study of grey matter volume and proneness to moral sentiments in healthy adults. It does not conduct a functional MRI task within the reported study and does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI statistical maps from the healthy group. Although the authors reference and use SSC-BOLD responses from a previously published fMRI study (subgroup N=29) for secondary correlational analyses, the current paper does not report whole-brain fMRI activation results itself. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (uses functional MRI during a social-related task) and I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). It does meet I4 (healthy adult sample). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are directly met.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI of social-related processing — face/voice perception). Inclusion not met / cannot verify: I4 (cannot confirm participant ages 18–65 or explicit healthy adult reporting), I5 (no clear evidence in the provided text of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported for the healthy group), I6 (unable to confirm that whole-brain results are reported in coordinates/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly met based on the available content, but inability to verify required inclusion criteria due to incomplete full text prevents inclusion. Recommend obtaining full article (methods/results/tables) to reassess.

This fMRI study clearly probes social-related processing (images of group vs individual social interactions) using an fMRI task (meets I3) and includes and separately reports results for a healthy adult control group (meets I4). However, the reported control-group results are presented from analyses constrained to a predefined composite ROI mask (ROI-corrected statistics) rather than as unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps. The paper explicitly states effects are reported within ROIs and only voxels outside these regions would be reported if they reached whole-brain significance; no unmasked whole-brain control-group activation map or whole-brain-corrected control-group main effect is presented. Therefore the study effectively reports only ROI-based task results and does not provide the required whole-brain healthy-group task map (violates I5 and triggers exclusion E2). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (observation and classification of social interactions vs non-social point-light displays). Sample: 14 healthy adult participants (mean age 29.4), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SI vs NSI contrast) with FDR correction and lists significant activations (tables/figures of peak voxels and clusters), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Results are reported for the healthy group (no restrictive subgroup-only maps). Not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not a non-empirical paper. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates face processing (a social-related construct: perception/understanding of others) using a task of face identity discrimination, meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (CA group, N=17, mean age ~31) with results reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses and presents group-level statistical maps/images for the CA (healthy adult) group (e.g., mean z-score images and corrected maps), satisfying I5 and I6. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text, and supplementary material is not required for the core whole-brain results; therefore the full text is sufficiently complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines social communication/mentalizing during a task where healthy adult participants (interns and producers; mean ages ~20.5) performed socially relevant judgments and interactions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (whole-brain thresholding and MNI coordinates are provided and results are reported in tables/figures), linking activations in mentalizing and reward networks to message propagation (buzz, intention, salesperson effects). Core methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text. Therefore it satisfies social-related fMRI task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and whole-brain group-level reporting (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

The provided content is limited to metadata, abstract, and references; core full text (methods, full results, figures/tables) is not present. From the abstract, the study used an fMRI mentalizing paradigm with 18 high-functioning adults with ASC and 18 matched controls, so I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported) appear satisfied. However, I cannot verify whether the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5) or whether whole-brain results (e.g., coordinate tables) are provided (I6). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm these required items and must exclude the study pending full-text verification. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively applied based on the available content.

This paper reports an event-related functional MRI study of impression formation (perception and understanding of others) using photographs and political-view sentences—i.e., a social-related task. Sample: 18 healthy adult participants aged 19–30 (meets age and healthy sample requirement). The analyses include group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent), with results reported as FDR-corrected activations and a table of MNI coordinates; figures and ROI follow-up are present. Thus the study provides a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not out-of-range age, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This study reports an fMRI task in which participants (including a healthy control group) imagined performing body-checking actions depicted in others—an interpersonal/mentalizing paradigm relevant to social cognition. The paper provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy control group (figures and text describing HC group activations) using voxelwise analyses. Full article contains methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps for HC), and I6 (maps reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study in adults using a social-related task (observing socio-affective touch videos) and reports behavioral and neural results. The sample includes a clearly reported neurotypical healthy adult group (N=21) analyzed and described separately from the ASD group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (mean group effects for social vs. non-social touch), with whole-brain statistics and coordinate tables (Additional file 1: Figure S2 and Table S2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core article content appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of self-recognition (social-related processing: perception/understanding of self), using healthy adult participants aged 18–24 (n=35 after exclusions). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM5; voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction) with tables of coordinates and figures describing group-level task contrasts (self vs friend, familiarity contrasts). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures described).

Full text is not accessible (PDF-only; only abstract and metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.
