From the abstract, the study meets I3 (uses fMRI with dynamic social interaction videos) and I4 (sample of 20 normal adult volunteers within 18–65). However I5 cannot be confirmed because the available content does not provide the full methods/results or clear reporting of a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group — the abstract reports significant activations but does not suffice to verify voxelwise whole-brain maps or coordinate tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied based on the incomplete text. Exclude pending retrieval of the full text to confirm I5; if full text provides whole-brain healthy-group results, the study could be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/perception (laughter types) in healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 26). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., JOY > TIC, TIC > JOY) with tables of coordinates and conjunction analyses, and describes random-effects, whole-brain and ROI-corrected results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy, theory-of-mind) in healthy adults using task-based paradigms (n=41 healthy adults in the Narrative Experiment; localizers in a separate healthy group). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SnPM whole-brain contrasts, corrected p < 0.05) with peak coordinates provided in tables and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text. Therefore it meets the review objectives and all required inclusion criteria: task is social-related (empathy/ToM), sample includes healthy adults 18–65, and at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported (coordinates/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, out-of-range age, non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-referential task (self, mother, president) assessing perception/understanding of self and others, meeting the review focus. The paper reports a healthy control group (n=15, ages 31–58) analyzed separately. Whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps for the healthy/control group are described and shown (e.g., Fig. 1 A–C) with whole-brain correction (AlphaSim), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without unmasked healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of socio-emotional processing (empathy induction) using campaign videos (meets I3). Sample comprises 20 healthy adult males (mean age 22.1), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (CV>NV) with FWE-corrected results and cluster peaks in tables/figures, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirement (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROI-only, not connectivity/rest, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical primary data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore include.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in which healthy adult participants viewed dynamic social approach stimuli (angry vs. happy faces) in the scanner, directly addressing social perception/intent (affiliation/dominance). The sample comprises healthy young adults (reported demographics and screening), and results are reported as whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (Angry>Happy and Happy>Angry) with MNI coordinates, cluster extents, and figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore, include the study in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-affective mimicry task probing affiliation-related processing (happy/angry faces; in-/out-group), in healthy adult participants (n=41; mean age 22.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Incongruent>Congruent and masked contrasts) with cluster-level correction and tables of peak coordinates (Tables 2–4), clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), and I6 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a randomized, placebo-controlled, within-subject pharmaco-fMRI study in 40 healthy adult males (mean age 25.8) that used an explicit social touch task (perception/hedonic evaluation of interpersonal touch). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activations and contrasts for the healthy participant group (coordinates and cluster statistics are provided and discussed), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results presented in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Abstract indicates fMRI was used with a social attribution task in healthy young adults (meets I3 and I4). However the provided content appears to be only title/abstract/metadata (full text incomplete), so I cannot verify that the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5) or that acceptable whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures (I6). Because all inclusion criteria must be confirmed and I5/I6 cannot be verified from the available material, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are confirmed from the available content.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social-cognitive processing (self- and mother-reflection), in a healthy adult sample (college-aged participants; analyses reported for 17 s/s and 17 l/l carriers). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts such as self- vs celebrity and mother- vs celebrity) are reported and described (Tables, figures, and whole-brain regression/hierarchical analyses with corrected thresholds). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (team/in-group vs out-group action perception) in healthy adult volunteers, using task-based fMRI during a social action–judgment paradigm. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (reported as adult volunteers; age ranges given with means in the early 20s) and results are reported at the group level. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts with cluster-level family-wise error correction (PFWE < 0.05) and provides peak coordinates and statistical maps in text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task results), and I6 (coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-groups-only contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

I3 and I4 are satisfied: this is an fMRI study using a social trust game and includes a healthy adult control group (20 controls) with results reported separately. However I5 is not met: the paper does not report an unmasked, whole‑brain task activation map for the healthy/control group (within‑group main effect or within‑group voxelwise map). The only whole‑brain, voxelwise results presented are exploratory between‑group contrasts (control > patient) reported with coordinates. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies: the study reports only between‑group whole‑brain contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole‑brain healthy‑group task effect. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 26) investigating perception of different laughter types and attention to social information. Tasks include an explicit social-processing task (laughter type categorization) and an implicit counting task, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts and cluster-level FWE correction (tables/figures described), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study used task-based fMRI during an explicit facial emotion recognition task (social perception/communication). The sample consists entirely of healthy adult participants (ages ~25–26) with two healthy subgroups (HDA and LDA). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain contrasts and cluster results; Table 2 and whole-brain figures) for task-evoked activity and between-group comparisons derived from the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are described in the text and tables (coordinates and cluster sizes), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group whole-brain maps, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 — the paper reports seed-based/background functional connectivity (functional interaction) analyses and between-group connectivity contrasts but does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — the study used fMRI during a social-perception task (same dataset as prior social perception study); I4 — a healthy adult control group (n=22) is included and reported separately. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the paper does not report at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. I6 (format allowance) is inapplicable because the required task-evoked map itself is missing. Therefore the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis objective because it provides connectivity/background interaction results but lacks the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map.

This is an fMRI study of social reputation processing (social-related task: perception/understanding of others/self-reputation), with healthy adult participants (14 males, 14 females; ages 20–24). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., positive vs. neutral, negative vs. neutral) with thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction and includes a table of brain regions and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an fMRI experiment using socially-relevant stimuli (point-light dyadic displays) while participants performed a task unrelated to social judgment, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (10 right-handed males, age 22–32), satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (second-level GLM random-effects contrasts such as atypical vs. typical, cluster-size correction, and peak coordinates/tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an rt-fMRI+EEG neurofeedback study targeting social communication and right pSTS (meets I3). However, the manuscript does not report participant details or confirm a healthy adult group (I4 not met based on available text), nor does it present or describe a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for a healthy/control group (I5 not met). Cannot verify whether results are ROI-only (potential E2) due to missing full text. Therefore excluded because required inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not confirmed from the provided content.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social-related processing (animated social vignettes, biological motion) and reports whole-brain group-level activation maps and connectivity analyses for the typically-developing (control) group. However, the participant samples are adolescents (ages below 18) rather than healthy adults (18–65), and no healthy adult subgroup is reported separately. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (participants outside the 18–65 range with no adult subgroup reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65). Full text appears complete. Accordingly, exclude on the basis of E5.

The provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/highlights/metadata). Based on available information: I3 (fMRI during social-related task: viewing emotional faces) appears satisfied; I4 (sample of 40 healthy volunteers) appears satisfied as a healthy adult group is reported. However I5 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group) cannot be verified because methods/results and full statistical reporting are missing from the supplied content. Therefore the review inclusion criterion I5 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available excerpt. Because the full text is incomplete and I5 cannot be confirmed, the study must be excluded at this stage. Recommend obtaining the complete article (methods and results) to reassess inclusion if whole-brain group-level maps are documented.

The provided content appears to be stimulus materials (lists of ironic vs. literal short stories) and bibliographic metadata only; the core article (introduction, methods, participant details, neuroimaging methods, results, whole-brain statistical maps) is not present. Therefore I cannot verify key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none can be confirmed from the supplied full text. Inclusion criteria not met / could not be verified: I3 (use of task fMRI during a social-related task cannot be confirmed from the stimuli alone), I4 (sample of healthy adults 18–65 not reported in the provided content), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or results are present), I6 (no whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text here). Exclusion criteria met: none explicitly met given available material, but fulltext_incomplete prevents confident inclusion. Recommend obtaining the complete article (methods and results) to reassess.

Full text is not accessible (paywalled) and only the abstract/metadata/references are provided. From the abstract it is clear this is an fMRI study of a social-related task (approachability judgments of faces) so I3 is satisfied. However, I cannot verify key required inclusion items: participant details (whether a healthy adult group aged 18–65 is reported separately) are not provided in the accessible content (I4 not verifiable), and although the abstract describes activations and contrasts, the available content does not allow confirmation that a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported (I5 not verifiable). I6 (acceptability of reporting formats) also cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are evidently met based on the abstract. Because I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded at this stage. To include it, please provide the full article text or confirm that the paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps for a healthy adult sample (18–65).

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses fMRI during a social-cognitive task (action observation with why/how/what goals), fulfilling I3. The sample is healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32), fulfilling I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects SPM ANOVA) and indicates that whole-brain results are provided in the Supplemental Material, satisfying I5 and I6 (whole-brain results in supplement are explicitly referenced). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical limitations). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This peer-reviewed empirical fMRI study (N=20 healthy adult participants, mean ages ~35) used an event-related whole-brain fMRI task in which subjects viewed faces of presidential candidates—a social-related perception/understanding-of-others task. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps and thresholding procedures (Z maps, cluster correction) and provides tables/figures of significant coordinates and contrasts (e.g., candidate vs rest, opponent vs own candidate), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, non-healthy-only age groups, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of emotional facial expressions) using dynamic human and monkey faces — a social communication task. The sample includes 23 healthy adult human participants (ages 24–34), satisfying the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster-wise correction and provides group significance maps and stereotactic coordinates (figures and supplementary Table 1), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Reporting of whole-brain maps/coordinates is explicit in the methods and results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages, or only between-group contrasts) apply.

The available text (appears to be abstract-level) indicates the study used fMRI during a social task (gender judgments to faces with gaze) in healthy adult men (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the provided full text is incomplete and does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level (voxelwise) task-evoked map from a healthy/control group; results described focus on between-subgroup comparisons (low vs normal fear scorers) and connectivity differences. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not demonstrably met, and I6 (acceptable reporting formats for whole-brain results) cannot be confirmed. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/subgroup comparisons reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). fulltext_incomplete=true prevents verification of whole-brain maps in the paper.

This fMRI study investigates labeling of briefly presented emotional facial expressions (a social perception task) using task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI in healthy adults (n=50, ages 18–29). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts (HA>NE, AN>NE, FE>NE) analyzed in SPM with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of significant clusters and coordinates, clearly describing results from the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range age, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (facial emotion and age judgments), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (age 18–65) with results reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (within-group and between-group maps), with tables/figures and supplementary material describing control-group effects, meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study that used a social interaction simulation task probing friendship/affiliation (social-related processing). Sample comprised healthy adults (N=28, mean age 22.6, range 19–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (main effects and interaction effects) with familywise-error corrected thresholds and cluster results presented in figures and a table of significant clusters. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI task-based social processing in healthy adults.

The provided content appears to be an abstract/summary only; core article sections (detailed methods, participant characteristics, results, full statistical maps) are missing. I3 is met: the study used event-related fMRI to decode vocal emotional prosody, a social-communication task. I4 is not verifiable: no participant sample details are given to confirm a healthy adult (18–65) group. I5/I6 are not verifiable: the excerpt does not provide or describe group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or coordinate tables/figures for the healthy group. Because required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5/I6) cannot be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full-text inspection.

The provided full text appears to be an abstract-level summary lacking key methodological details. While the study uses fMRI in a social-related task (promotion/prevention goals; satisfies I3), the manuscript as provided does not report participant ages and therefore does not confirm the healthy adult age range 18–65 (I4 not verifiable). The excerpt also does not clearly present group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables identified as healthy-group effects (I5 not verifiable). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the available information, but the incomplete reporting prevents confirming all inclusion criteria. Per screening rules, I exclude due to incomplete full text and unmet/unknown inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an implicit Face Matching Task (perception of others’ emotional faces), which qualifies as a social-related task (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=10; mean age 25), satisfying the age and healthy-group requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked GLM analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests) and refers to whole-brain results presented in Supplementary Table S2 and Figures S1–S3, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and acceptable reporting in supplemental materials (I6). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, seed-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial/family-related decisions (a social-affiliation/attachment task) in healthy young adults (Mage=20.2). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects task contrasts and provides tables of coordinates and figures (Tables 1–3, whole-brain and ROI-corrected results). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present).

This is an fMRI study of social cognitive processing (causal attributions, self-responsibility, self-serving bias) in healthy adults. Methods report task-based fMRI with whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (fixed-effects and follow-up random-effects ROI tests), tables of peak coordinates, and figures of activations. Sample: 12 healthy adults aged 20–51 (within 18–65). Whole-brain, group-level task activation maps are reported and clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a virtual social-cognition task (perception/understanding of others) — satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (14 controls, ages 18–45) with results reported separately — satisfying I4. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group (within-group Emotion vs Control contrast) with tables of coordinates and figures, analysed with AFNI — satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results (within-group maps and tables), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly manipulated affiliative (kinship-based) versus nonaffiliative social scenarios and measured task-evoked BOLD responses (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adults (final N=27; ages reported, 18–65 range) with results reported for the healthy group separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., affiliative vs nonaffiliative; FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates; meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within the age range, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets I3 (used task-based fMRI with social stimuli—emotional facial expressions) and I4 (included a healthy adult TD group, ages within 18–65, reported separately). However, the reported fMRI results are presented as ROI-based analyses focused on the amygdala (small-volume correction within the amygdala) and no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group is provided. Therefore it fails I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (reports only ROI analyses without whole-brain results). Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (pseudo-interactive joke task) in healthy adults (N=38, ages 19–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (SPM analyses with cluster-level FWE correction, tables of coordinates and figures for SELF vs OTHER, listener response, and interaction effects in ventral striatum), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The task probes social action-outcome contingency and self/other processing, matching the review objective. The full-text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (open-access/full article). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age in range, empirical data present).

This paper reports an fMRI task probing social processing (direct vs averted gaze/mentalizing), includes a healthy adult control group (n=16) with results reported separately, and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and whole-brain analyses for the control group (main effects and within-group contrasts described; tables/figures referenced). Whole-brain results for controls are clearly reported in text and figures (supplementary tables noted), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements for task, sample, and whole-brain reporting. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (audiovisual integration of non-verbal emotional signals, voice/face sensitivity) in healthy adults (n=24, ages 18–41), so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the analysis is an individual STS region-of-interest approach: parameter estimates were extracted from 27 measuring points along the STS and one-sample t-tests were performed on these ROI-based values. The paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps or unmasked healthy-group whole-brain contrasts (only ROI results and peak-normalized contrast estimates are presented), so it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and must be excluded.

This study used an fMRI social-related task (PANSIT-MC) so inclusion criterion I3 is satisfied. However, it does not include any healthy adult control group or report results for a healthy adult group separately: inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) is not met. Consequently, there are no whole-brain task activation maps reported for a healthy/control group, so I5 (healthy-group whole-brain evidence) is not met. The full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are applicable. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet I4 and I5.

This is an fMRI study of social/emotional body-expression perception (social-related task) that includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (12 adult males, ages matched, IQ reported). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts for the control group (conjunctions, main effects and figures/tables showing control-specific activations and coordinates using SPM2), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for healthy controls are presented separately from the ASD group. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes task-evoked whole-brain activations; not resting-state/seed-only; includes adults within 18–65; empirical fMRI data present). Full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathic decision-making (a social-related task involving empathy/mentalizing). Participants: 32 healthy adult males (mean age 22.8), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLMs, conjunctions, whole-brain cluster-corrected results) and lists brain activation tables/figures (vmPFC, IPL, etc.), meeting the whole-brain evidence reporting criteria. Results for the healthy group are reported directly (not limited to a subgroup). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of face perception (social processing) in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the face task (angry vs neutral) from the healthy/control group. The reported activation result for the FFA is an ROI-based percent-signal-change analysis and the other reported whole-brain images are seed-based PPI (task-modulated connectivity) maps. Because the paper provides only ROI activation summaries and seed-based connectivity results without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group, it meets exclusion criterion E3 and thus must be excluded from the review. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an event-related fMRI study of evaluative judgments (self-referential/social cognition), meeting the review topic. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=7, mean age 26.4) reported separately. The paper provides group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts for the control group (figures and tables of Talairach coordinates and thresholded maps), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interactive task (competitive reaction-time Taylor paradigm) that probes social processes (retaliation, observing another’s pain, empathy). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (16 male subjects, mean age 28.6; two excluded for disbelief), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2; voxel-wise thresholding, FDR correction) and provides activation coordinates/tables and figures for main effects and parametric modulations (i.e., unmasked healthy-group task effects). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of perception of socially relevant facial expressions (social communication), using healthy adult participants (N=17, mean age 25.9). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random effects SPM, threshold p=.001 uncorrected, coordinates and tables of activations for the main effect of SOC and time-bin contrasts). The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (biological motion perception), includes a healthy adult control group (N=15, ages within 18–65), and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and tables explicitly for the control group (within-group contrasts and main effects). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI studies in healthy adults.

Full text appears to be incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). While the abstract indicates a social fMRI task involving live eye contact (meets I3), the manuscript does not provide participant details or reportable whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps. Therefore I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) and I5 (whole-brain group-level task map) cannot be confirmed; I6 (acceptable reporting format) is also not evident. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be positively identified from the available text. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending a complete article.

This study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related gaze task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, it reports only seed-based task-modulated connectivity (PPI) results and does not present an unambiguous whole-brain, task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (no standard voxelwise task activation/main-effect map for controls is reported in the main text; whole-brain results referenced are connectivity PPI analyses and within-group PPI results are in supplementary material). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=21) that uses an explicit social task (gaze-based joint attention) during fMRI, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The methods and results report group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation (e.g., MPFC, PCC, anterior temporal poles, ventral striatum, bilateral fronto-parietal network) with voxel-level correction mentioned, and neuroimaging analyses were performed using a GLM in SPM5. The sample comprises healthy adult participants and results are reported for that group. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical fMRI data).

This study uses task-based fMRI while subjects viewed and evaluated nonverbal cartoons (a social-communicative stimulus requiring perception/understanding of others and social situations) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates, cluster statistics) linking trait cheerfulness to BOLD. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (10 right-handed males) reported separately. Whole-brain SPM analyses and coordinates are presented in text/tables/figure. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of charitable donation decisions (a social decision-making task), reporting whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps and contrasts in a healthy adult sample. The methods and results include introduction, full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Participants: 22 healthy adult females (ages 19–38) — within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures (GLM contrasts, conjunctions, and whole-brain PPI analyses), clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI task probing processing of personally familiar others (partner, child, friend), which is clearly a social-related construct (affiliation/attachment; perception/understanding of others). A healthy control group (n=13; mean age 64.5) is reported and analyzed separately from the patient, providing group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the control group (coordinates and FWE-corrected cluster results are reported). Whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy/control group are presented (partner > unfamiliar and faces > baseline). The manuscript includes complete methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or age-only outside 18–65 with no qualifying subgroup) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 22) that used a social-communication related task (listening to communicative vs. noncommunicative vocal sounds). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (vocal > nonvocal and communicative > noncommunicative) thresholded (FDR q < .05) with peak coordinates and figures/tables, and additionally describes statistical control analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study presenting a social-perception task (observation of nonpainful touch to another's hand), matching the review's domain (perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (n=22, ages 23–39) satisfying the age and sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects analyses with FWE-corrected results and voxelwise contrasts (touch observation > control, masked with real touch), and provides coordinates/tables and figures, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of social-related face perception (eye gaze and identity), meeting the review objective. Sample: 9 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 24), so I4 satisfied. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (face vs control; identity vs gaze; averted vs direct gaze) and reports coordinates and figures from whole-brain analyses (z-thresholds, cluster selection, Talairach/SPM coordinates), satisfying I5 and I6. The task is clearly social (perception of others’ gaze/identity), satisfying I3. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating mirror-neuron-related processing (observation of goal-directed hand actions) which directly probes perception/understanding of others (social processing). It includes healthy adult participants (college students) with explicitly reported screening excluding neurological/psychiatric disorders; group-level analyses are reported separately for non-alexithymic (healthy) and alexithymic groups. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise one-sample group activation maps (for non-ALEX and ALEX groups) with corrected thresholds, tables of coordinates, figures, and conjunction analyses (i.e., clear healthy-group task effects). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state or connectivity-only, contains whole-brain healthy-group task maps, participants are adults, and it is original empirical work). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of social evaluation/impression formation (social-meaningful, social-irrelevant vs non-social), explicitly reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts and corrected cluster results, and includes a healthy young adult group (ages 20–29) reported separately. Full text (methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (undergraduate sample, age 18–21) performing a social-related task (viewing social vs non-social scenes; mentalizing/understanding others). It includes a group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrast (social > non-social) with FDR correction (p<0.05) and reports results in figures/tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The full text contains introduction, detailed methods (participants, fMRI acquisition and analysis, experience sampling), results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation map), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion reason: The study includes only children/adolescents (ages 8–17) and does not include or separately report a healthy adult group (age 18–65), therefore violating E5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task—the Social Analog Risk Task), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses/contrasts), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/NeuroVault). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy adult participant group 18–65 reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because the absence of a healthy adult sample is a disqualifying criterion for this adult-focused meta-analysis, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates perception/understanding of others (vitality forms), a social-related construct. It tested 19 healthy right-handed adults (ages 21–29) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts (what vs baseline, how vs baseline, and how vs what) with PFWE correction; coordinates and statistical maps/tables are provided. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion (not a review or connectivity-only study). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines perception/understanding of others by comparing goal-directed (sports-related) vs non-goal-directed biological motion, matching the review’s social-related constructs. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 29.4, right-handed, N=12) meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (BR minus BU) using random-effects SPM analysis, with whole-brain correction and/or a priori ROI thresholds and provides coordinate tables and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (complete core content). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-18–65 sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

Meets all inclusion criteria: fMRI task manipulates social processing (empathic vs. unempathic verbal responses) (I3); participants are healthy adults (mean age 26, n=20) (I4); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and tables/figures of activations with FWE correction (I5); results are reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (self-referential moral processing and intergroup competition) in healthy adult participants (final N=21, Mage=23.1), meeting the review topic. The paper reports both region-of-interest and whole-brain random-effects analyses with corrected thresholds and presents whole-brain results in tables/figures (e.g., Table 2, supplementary figures) and describes group-level voxelwise contrasts, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample, non-empirical) are met. Hence the study should be included for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation) in healthy adults (N=19; mean age 19.1). The task is social-related (impression formation/outcome dependency). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts: the functional localizer contrast (form impression > sequencing) is presented with Talairach coordinates and cluster-corrected results (Table 1), and main task results include cluster coordinates (Table 2) and cluster-correction details. The sample falls within the 18–65 range. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so content appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adults (12 participants aged 21–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; contrasts between cooperation, competition, and independent conditions) with tables/figures of activations and thresholding details. All inclusion criteria are met (task is social-related, sample is healthy adults within 18–65, whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps are reported, and results are presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of social interaction (live human–human vs human–robot conversation), addressing social communication/mentalizing (meets I3). Sample comprises 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.8; within 18–65) (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM, cluster-level FDR-corrected results) and presents whole-brain statistical maps (figures; NeuroVault link) (meets I5 and I6). Full text contains complete introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion: E2 met. The paper’s primary task-activation results are reported and tested within an amygdala ROI (significance corrected within that ROI) and the reported statistical inferences focus on ROI and seed-based connectivity. Inclusion: I3 and I4 are satisfied (task-based fMRI of social stimuli; healthy adult sample n=15, ages ~27). Inclusion not met: I5 is not met — the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task-evoked voxelwise statistical map or whole-brain-corrected results for the healthy group (results are ROI-restricted); I6 is not met because no whole-brain coordinate table or whole-brain map is provided. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (SI) recognition using point-light displays (social-related task). It includes a healthy adult group (ages 20–41) with results reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (SI > NM) for each age group including adults, with SPM analyses, thresholding, cluster/FWE corrections, and coordinate reporting. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is not available (only abstract/metadata and a note that PDF is required). Abstract confirms fMRI experiments on social interaction (so I3 is met), but critical details cannot be verified: participant characteristics/ages and whether a healthy adult group (I4) was used and reported separately, and whether the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy group (I5). I6 (format of whole-brain reporting) also cannot be confirmed. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria and therefore exclude the study pending full-text review. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met from the available information.

This paper reports an fMRI social-perception task including healthy control participants and whole-brain analyses, but the primary whole-brain results are between-group contrasts (HC vs SZ). Inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) are satisfied. However the paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map (main effect or within-group contrast) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; instead results are presented as between-group t-tests and follow-up ROI analyses. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 is met (only between-group contrasts without accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Only abstract/metadata were provided (full text incomplete). From the abstract the study uses fMRI during a social-related pleasant-touch task (I3) and includes a healthy control group of adult non-using participants (I4). However, the full text is not available to confirm whether the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5) or the exact form/location of whole-brain results (I6). Age range for participants (18–65) is not explicitly reported in the abstract. Because I5 (and I6) cannot be verified from the provided content, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is thus excluded pending access to the complete full text.

This study uses fMRI of a social imitate/observe task (meets I3) and includes healthy adult participants reported separately in sample descriptions (meets I4). However, the full text does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map that is explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not clearly met). The reported whole-brain maps appear to be across all participants or collapsed/clustered groups (mixed diagnoses), and no clear healthy-group whole-brain task effect is presented in the available text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group/collapsed maps without an explicit healthy-group whole-brain effect).

Exclusion criteria met: E4. The study does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The whole-brain results reported are for the combined sample (HC and SZ) and ROI analyses report HC and SZ separately, but no unmasked HC-only whole-brain task effect or coordinates/figures/tables explicitly labeled as HC-only are provided. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related simulation/empathy task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 18–65, with separate behavioral/ROI results). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). I6 (format allowance) is not applicable because the required HC whole-brain result is absent. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion processing, a social-related task (perception/understanding of others), with a healthy control group whose whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results are reported separately. Methods and results describe within-group one-sample and paired t-tests and whole-brain ANOVAs with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables of activation (e.g., Table 3, supplemental maps). Healthy controls (n=31, ages reported within 16–40) are analyzed and reported separately from the first-episode patient group. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-cognitive processing (Theory of Mind and empathy) in healthy adult participants. The sample comprises 13 healthy right-handed adult males (ages 19–36), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., ‘ToM − Physical1’, ‘Empathy − Physical2’) analyzed with SPM2 and thresholded maps; activations are reported in tables of coordinates and figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a naturalistic social-cognition task (MASC) that probes theory-of-mind and social perception, performed in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 20–45). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (GLM mixed-effects ToM vs PI; thresholded maps, cluster results, coordinate tables and figures) and model-free T-PICA group analyses. Thus it meets all required criteria for inclusion: fMRI social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and whole-brain group task-evoked results clearly reported (I5/I6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates an fMRI social-inference task, so I3 (fMRI during social-related task) is met. However, the manuscript as provided does not report participant ages or confirm a healthy adult group (I4 cannot be verified), nor does it provide full methods/results to verify that a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task map is reported (I5/I6 cannot be verified). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone. Given the incomplete full text, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria, so the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 25.9) using task-based fMRI while participants listened to affective vocalisations (a social-communication task: perception/understanding of others’ emotional vocalisations). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (species contrast human>chimpanzee>macaque) with coordinates, figures and tables (uncorrected threshold p<.001) clearly from the healthy participant group. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study includes an fMRI task using social phobia–related words (I3 met). However, the fMRI sample is a patient-only subsample (N=25 patients) and no group-level whole-brain task activation map for a healthy adult group is reported. The fMRI analyses focus on a region-of-interest (bilateral amygdala) with ROI-based cluster correction rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task map. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria I4 (healthy adult fMRI group reported) and I5 (healthy-group whole-brain evidence) are not met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (visual social judgment of dominance/trustworthiness) in a sample of healthy adults (N=23; ages 21–43). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment) analyzed in SPM8 and provides a table of whole-brain FWE-corrected cluster results (Table 1) and figures. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This empirical fMRI study used an event-related task of facial emotion processing (a social perception/communication task), includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (ages within 18–65), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation results (figures and tables of coordinates and detailed group maps and contrasts). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Abstract and metadata indicate an fMRI study using a social communication task (communicative vs. descriptive speech) in healthy adult L2 learners (n=30), reporting task-related activations (left pSMG, MTG, OFC). These elements satisfy I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). The abstract reports specific regional activations consistent with group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, satisfying I5 and I6 plausibly. However, only the abstract/metadata are provided here (no full methods/results sections), so I cannot fully verify the presence and exact nature of unmasked, voxelwise group-level whole-brain statistical maps as required. Therefore I mark fulltext_incomplete=true and give moderate confidence.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (third-party punishment; mentalizing/theory-of-mind) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 26 healthy right-handed adults (mean age 26), which falls within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Decision Phase: Experimental > Control) with correction (q(FDR)<0.05) and provides coordinates, tables, and figures describing activations and parametric modulation results. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). Although the paper also reports effective connectivity (GCA), it additionally provides whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self- vs other-referential processing) in healthy adults. Sample: 20 healthy women aged 18–52 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked BOLD contrasts and individual-differences whole-brain regression results (figures and tables of coordinates and cluster results are presented). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and reports unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effects. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Ultimatum Game (a social decision-making task) with a healthy adult group (n=15, ages 19–28) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and full-factorial ANOVA) and displays/maps/coordinates for contrasts (unfair vs fair offers) for the healthy groups. The task probes social processing (theory of mind, fairness, reward), satisfying the review objective. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material absence does not preclude inclusion.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports resting-state intrinsic connectivity and PET measures during viewing but does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI activation map for the healthy adult group. Inclusion I4 is satisfied (healthy adult sample, mothers age 21–42). Inclusion I3 is not met because although mothers watched infant films in the scanner, the paper does not report task-evoked whole-brain fMRI activation maps or task-based voxelwise results; fMRI analyses focus on task-independent (resting-state) intrinsic connectivity. Inclusion I5 is not met because no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (main effect or within-group contrast) is reported for the healthy group. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis targeting task-evoked whole-brain fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study examines audiovisual speech integration, which qualifies as social communication (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=15; I4). The paper reports whole-brain analyses for the main congruency effect across all participants and reports group-by-congruency interaction maps. However, it does not present an unambiguously labeled, whole-brain task activation map or within-group (healthy/control-only) voxelwise statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Because the report focuses on across-group main effects and interactions and lacks an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect, it meets exclusion criterion E4 (between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study examining neural responses to witnessing an emergency (a social situation). It uses task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants (N=17, ages 18–27) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (parametric and contrast maps) with results summarized in tables and figures. The paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=21, mean age 24) that used task-based fMRI during action observation and execution to probe mirror-system responses—constructs that map onto social perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses including whole-brain results (thresholds and peak coordinates reported; tables/figures described) in addition to ROI analyses. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (results described with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI pharmacological-genetics study of direct vs. averted gaze in 55 healthy adult males (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper reports only region-of-interest (amygdala and inferior occipital gyrus) ROI analyses (FWE corrected within ROI) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps or whole-brain results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Decision: EXCLUDED because of E2 (ROI-only), with I3 and I4 met and I5 not met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind) using task-based fMRI and multi-voxel pattern analysis on narratives about others' beliefs and emotions. Participants were healthy adult volunteers (ages reported within 18–65) and analyses focus on the healthy groups. The paper includes task-evoked contrasts used to define ROIs (Belief > Photo localizer, reported with thresholding and referenced figures/Supplementary Fig. S1), and reports group-level results in the main figures and supplementary materials. Therefore it meets the review objective and reports whole-brain task-evoked results (localizer/contrast maps reported in figures/supplement), not only ROI analyses. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided material.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (emotion identification and attribution) in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–32). It uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts reported (How>Why, Why>How) and tables/figures listing coordinates and cluster results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and whole-brain contrasts, PPI analyses), and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (perception of biological motion/point-light displays), addressing social perception/communication (I3). Sample included healthy adults (n=26 analyzed, ages 18–39), meeting the age and healthy-sample criterion (I4). The authors conducted and reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with multiple-comparison correction) and reported significant clusters (right pSTS/TPJ) relating task activation to social-network measures, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Whole-brain results are described in text and figures/supplemental materials, consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants made social/individuation (vegetable preference) and categorical (age) judgments about photographed social group members while undergoing fMRI. Sample: 18 healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 20). Analyses: whole-brain, random-effects GLM contrasts reported (task and social-group main effects and simple effects), with figures and Talairach coordinates and cluster sizes provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (person perception and person knowledge/ToM) in healthy adults (N=21, mean age 24.6). The task is social (bodies/names paired with trait or neutral statements) and engages social cognition networks. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked univariate contrasts (e.g., Bodies>Names, Traits>Neutral, interaction) with tables/coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of narrative processing with moral/protected values (social cognition). Participants are healthy adults (N=78 across 3 groups, ages within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (e.g., stories vs rest; protected vs nonprotected) with cluster correction and ROI-independent analyses. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. Whole text appears complete.

This article is a non-empirical review (Article in Japanese) summarizing social neuroscience and psychiatry and does not report original fMRI data or methods/results from healthy adult participants. It therefore meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper). No inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task) not met; I4 (reports healthy adult sample) not met; I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps) not met. Additionally, the provided full text appears incomplete (abstract/metadata/review label only), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study of supramodal emotional processing (social communication/perception) in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–34). The task is social-related (emotion classification of facial and vocal cues), satisfying I3. The sample is a healthy adult group reported separately, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., AV > A, CAV > ICAV) with correction and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (co-speech gesture and body orientation) using a behavioral addressment task during scanning. Sample: 37 healthy adult participants (ages 20–39), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (main effects and interactions) with Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) coordinates and cluster thresholds described, fulfilling whole-brain evidence reporting. Results and tables of coordinates are presented in the full text. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete (only metadata/title; body content missing). Cannot confirm whether the study used an fMRI social-related task (I3), included a healthy adult group with separate results (I4), or reported whole-brain healthy-group task maps (I5/I6). Therefore eligibility cannot be determined and the study is excluded pending full text. Inclusion criteria met: none confirmed. Inclusion criteria not met/uncertain: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: none (based on available metadata). Recommend obtaining the complete article to reassess.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 19–29) investigating self/other social cognition during episodic recollection. The task is explicitly social (conceptual and agentic self/other judgments), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. Methods describe fMRI acquisition and whole-brain preprocessing/analyses using SPM8, and results include whole-brain activations (with FWE-corrected clusters reported) and coordinate tables, meeting the requirement for group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy control group. The paper is empirical, includes methods, results, and discussion, and is therefore eligible for inclusion under I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults (Human Connectome Project n=787). It includes a social cognition task (TOM vs Random) and reports group-level voxelwise task activation results with cluster coordinates and maps (Table 1, figures, Cohen’s d and z maps derived from level-2/level-3 HCP data). The sample is healthy adults within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps and cluster coordinates are clearly reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (final N=41, ages 18–24) examining social-related processing (decisions to share/select news, invoking self- and other-related/social-cognitive processes). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (select > content, share > content, share > select) with family-wise error correction and tables/figures of significant activations, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (perception of social interactions) in healthy adults (14 participants, ages 20–32). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects activation maps and peak coordinates for task contrasts (e.g., social interaction > independent), contains full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (trust/honesty) using task-based fMRI (TAG and subsequent trust game). Inclusion criteria: I3 satisfied — the study uses functional MRI during social-related tasks (advice-taking and trust decisions probing perception and understanding of others). I4 satisfied — sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=31; mean age 24.3; ages within 18–65). I5 satisfied — the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain univariate contrasts with FWE cluster correction, searchlight MVPA, and LOSOCV classification/prediction results). I6 satisfied — whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and supplementary tables/coordinates. Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining social-related processing (perception and understanding of others via footsteps), with a healthy adult sample (n=12, ages 22–37). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., STEP1+STEP2 – REST; STEP2 – NOISE2) with Talairach coordinates and statistical maps/figures. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of communicative (social) speech production (communication vs description), i.e., social communication, satisfying the review topic. Participants were healthy adults (n=30, ages 19–31) meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ECOM–EOBJ, L2COM–L1COM, interaction contrasts) with tables and figures of cluster coordinates and corrected thresholds, satisfying whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, no out-of-range ages, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is included in the review.

The study is an fMRI investigation of mental state decoding (Reading the Mind in the Eyes), a social-perceptual social cognition task (meets I3). Participants were healthy adults aged 18–27 from two cultural groups with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (RME − GD) and conjunction/contrast analyses with tables of regional activations and thresholds (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so inclusion is justified. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-affective task (SoVT film clips depicting others in distress) applied to healthy adult participants (ages 45–62) who are long-term meditation practitioners. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative; Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) with cluster-level FWE correction and presents results in tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.
