Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the cyberball social interaction paradigm (social exclusion/inclusion/control), reporting task-evoked whole-brain analyses and peak coordinates. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (20 female HCs) with results reported separately and post hoc within-group contrasts (t-contrasts reported in Supplementary Data). Whole-brain main effects and interaction effects are reported and supplemented by t-contrasts/peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement that healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked results are available. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Included. This paper reports an fMRI study of social attribution (why/how task) targeting perception/understanding of others, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=19; ages 21–46) reported separately, meeting the sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (conjunction and interaction contrasts, cluster-level correction) with tables/figures of results, satisfying whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete for screening). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not out-of-range ages, and is empirical).

The paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of social working memory (a social cognitive task addressing perception/understanding of others). Sample: 16 healthy adults (mean age 20), within 18–65. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (parametric contrasts, coordinates, figures, and cluster thresholds) clearly from the healthy sample. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material presence is not required.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma), addressing social cooperation/interaction (meets I3). Sample is healthy adults aged 18–22 (both sexes) with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The manuscript includes group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (CC and CD contrasts) with cluster-wise FWE correction and reported coordinates/thresholds and functional ROIs derived from whole-brain maps (meets I5 and I6). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and core analyses are described; no exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of social processing (learning moral status of faces via a Prisoner’s Dilemma), meeting the review objective. Healthy adult participants (scanned N=11, ages 21–36) are reported separately. Imaging used SPM2 with one-sample random-effects group analyses and whole-brain voxelwise contrasts; results are reported as statistical maps, coordinate tables, and figures. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded: This study does not meet the review's requirements for inclusion. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: none. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 — the fMRI paradigm is a non-social cognitive-control task (Preparing to Overcome Prepotency), not a social-related task; I4 — sample comprises patients with schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder (no healthy adult group reported or analyzed separately); I5 — although whole-brain task maps are reported, they are for patient groups only; there is no whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map from a healthy/control group. Therefore the study does not provide healthy adult whole-brain fMRI data for social processing and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports task-based fMRI using social stimuli (photographs and behavior depictions of children), addressing social cognition/understanding of others, satisfying I3. Participants are adult mothers (scanned mothers, mother’s age used as covariate), consistent with a healthy adult sample (ages implied within 18–65), satisfying I4. The paper conducted voxel-by-voxel whole-brain analyses (group-level random-effects analyses, contrasts own>other and inappropriate>appropriate) and reports activations and coordinates and figures from those whole-brain maps, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Confidence is moderate-high due to absence of explicit participant age range reported in the excerpt but mother sample and covariate imply adult ages within the eligible range.

This task-based fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (explicit and implicit processing of emotional facial expressions). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=9, mean age 27±7) with results reported separately, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and activation coordinates/figures for the control group (tables, figures, Talairach coordinates). The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. It is not limited to ROI analyses, connectivity-only analyses, or only between-group contrasts. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (imagining encounters with neutral faces in goal-relevant vs. goal-irrelevant social situations). Sample consists of healthy adults aged 20–36 (n=17 analyzed). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8 random-effects ANOVAs, whole-brain thresholds with cluster correction, tables/figures of activation contrasts), and also reports coordinates and small-volume corrections. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of crowd emotion and social interactions), involving 16 healthy adult participants (ages 19–27). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random effects ANOVAs) with cluster results, tables, and figures described in the text, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adults, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — participants are adolescents (16–17 y), outside the required adult age range 18–65. 
(b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — study uses fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion).
(c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — no healthy adult (18–65) participant group is included or reported separately (sample is 16–17-year-old males); I5 — the paper emphasizes connectivity analyses and does not clearly report a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked activation map for a healthy adult group (voxelwise whole-brain task map for an eligible group is not clearly provided). 
Given the mandatory age requirement (I4) is not satisfied and E5 is triggered, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of theory-of-mind (social cognition) using a task manipulating types of intentions (social vs non-social). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=12, mean age 24.8) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts and provides tables of coordinates and figures for within-group activations in controls (e.g., contrasts PInt/PSInt/CInt vs Ph-C), with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 24.1) that investigates perception of two-body spatial relations (face-to-face vs back-to-back), a socially relevant visual processing question. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (dyads > single bodies; facing > nonfacing dyads) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction, and provides whole-brain results in figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group-level maps.

This fMRI study investigates emotional prosody (a social-communication task) using an event-related whole-brain design in healthy adult participants (n=15, mean age 24.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts and MNI coordinates and figures clearly from the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mental state inference/prediction) in healthy adults. It used task-based functional MRI during a mentalizing/social task (participants rated scenarios evoking mental states), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 18–22 with group results reported separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (searchlight representational similarity and repetition-suppression), with corrected statistical maps and peak MNI coordinates described in the text and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not a between-groups-only contrast, includes appropriate age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (emotional face recognition). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts and regression analyses with FWE-corrected peaks and MNI coordinates (e.g., left and right amygdala, right inferior frontal gyrus), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Sample: 116 healthy men (mean age 24.7), within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain results are described in the main text with coordinates and significance values; figures and supplemental results referenced. No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, resting-state, or between-group-only paper; not non-empirical; participants are within age range). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). While the study clearly uses fMRI during a social-related face-emotion perception task (I3) and includes a healthy adult sample (14 right-handed volunteers, mean age 29±6) meeting age/sample requirements (I4), I cannot verify that the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group (I5). The abstract states "Statistical parametric mapping showed..." which suggests voxelwise analysis, but the full article (methods/results/tables/figures) is not available here to confirm an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation map or coordinate tables/figures (I6). Because I5 (and confirmation for I6) cannot be verified from the provided content, the study cannot be included at this stage. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met based on available information.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants learned about others’ generosity while being scanned and analyses focus on social vs non-social learning. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: learning about others’ generosity), I4 (healthy adult sample — N=26 final analyzed, ages 19–37 within 18–65), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with cluster correction and tables/figures), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and shown). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, age appropriate, and empirical). Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study examines perception and understanding of others (emotion and identity recognition from voices), meeting the review's social-related task requirement (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group of sighted participants (n=15, mean age 32.2), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (random-effects GLM univariate results, searchlight MVPA) with tables/figures of clusters and coordinates, providing whole-brain healthy-group results (I5,I6). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references) is provided, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates social-emotional processing (viewing human emotional interactions in movie clips) and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results. Inclusion criteria: I3 met — task involves social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, empathy-related processes) via movie viewing. I4 met — sample of healthy adults (n=16, ages 25–49). I5 met — the paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise ISC and GLM results (FDR-corrected maps, figures, and tables of coordinates). I6 met — whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that directly investigates observation and understanding of another person’s actions (toolmaking) with tasks requiring simulation or evaluation of the actor’s success—constructs within ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’. The sample comprises three healthy adult groups (Naïve n=11, Trained n=10, Expert n=5) described as neurotypical adults. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8), thresholding, and coordinate-based results (conjunctions and contrasts across groups) consistent with I5/I6. Ages are not explicitly listed but participants are described as adults; given explicit reporting of healthy adult groups and group-level whole-brain maps, all inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment on humor processing, a social-cognition related task (humor as a social phenomenon). The participants are healthy adults (29 participants, mean age 27, range within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (e.g., Cartoons vs. Neutral, parametric modulation) with corrected results and conjunctions, and provides detailed whole-brain results in text/tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI with a social decision task (SCDT) and includes a healthy young-adult group (21–22 y), so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, although the paper reports whole-brain analyses for the full sample (n=60) and reports age-comparison contrasts (Young adults > Adolescents), it does not present an unmasked, within-group whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult group alone. The adult information is only provided via between-group contrasts rather than an adult-only whole-brain task effect. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded for meta-analytic pooling of healthy adult whole-brain task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study of healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 22–39) investigating how collective/social schemas influence memory, probing social-related constructs (collective memory, social knowledge, group-level narratives and mentalizing). The task involved recall of museum pictures to assess representation of collective schemas in mPFC, and analyses include both ROI RSA and a whole-brain surface-based searchlight with group-level inference and TFCE-corrected maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI during social-related processing), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise/searchlight results), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/figured). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/summary provided). Inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI task probing social-related processing/action perception) is met based on the abstract. However I4 (clear report of healthy adult sample, ages 18–65) and I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the provided text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met, but because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, study must be excluded. Recommend obtaining full article (methods and results) to reassess.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition: subjects predicted another person's choices (a social ‘Other’ task) and the paper investigates neural signals of simulating others. Sample: 36 healthy, normal subjects (group-level healthy adult sample reported). Whole-brain, voxelwise task-based analyses are reported (whole-brain regression analyses, cluster-level corrections, Tables 1 and 2, Talairach coordinates, figures). Results are reported for the healthy/control group (not limited to a subgroup). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. I assign moderate-high confidence because participant ages are not numerically specified in the provided excerpt, but participants are described as healthy adult subjects in fMRI sessions.

This fMRI study investigates neural representations of heard human actions (mirror system) using an unconscious semantic priming task — directly addressing Perception and Understanding of Others (social-related processing). The sample includes healthy adults (fMRI subgroup n=11, age range 21–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with cluster-level correction and presents statistical maps, tables, and figures describing task-evoked activations for the healthy participants. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants (healthy adult undergraduates, mean age 24.4) performed a mind-perception task during event-related fMRI and a subsequent behavioral gaze-cueing task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise parametric analyses with cluster-based correction (FWER p<.05) and tables/figures describing surviving clusters (e.g., vmPFC, TPJ, fusiform). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20 males, mean age 24.6) using a social-related task (viewing first-person video clips of reactive–aggressive, social-positive, and neutral interactions) that clearly probes social processing constructs (empathic/perceptual processing of social interactions). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses are reported (FDR-corrected maps, conjunctions, contrasts, tables of peak coordinates and figures). Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Thus I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task fMRI study examining empathy/social perception (observing human and robot pain/pleasure) using fMRI. Sample consists of healthy adults (n=26, ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses (cluster-corrected results, whole-brain maps, and NeuroVault/OSF deposits). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain results.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=14, mean age 25) that investigates observation and motor imagery of meaningful face and limb movements, including socially communicative gestures. It meets inclusion criteria: (I3) uses fMRI during social-related tasks (social communication/gesture perception and imagery); (I4) sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65 and results reported for that group; (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (conjunctions and contrasts) with FWE-corrected thresholds and anatomical coordinates; (I6) whole-brain results are reported via figures and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is primary empirical work). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced). Therefore, include the study in the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social perception (perception of others’ facial expressions) in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 25.2). It uses group-level mixed-effects fMRI analyses and generates parameter-estimate maps registered to MNI space; additionally, a group-level localiser (faces>scrambled faces, n=83 healthy participants) produced whole-brain statistical maps used to define ROIs. The paper therefore provides task-evoked, group-level whole-brain statistical mapping and clearly reports the behavioural social-perception task and healthy adult sample. All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (communicative vs private intentions) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=23, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt; interaction effects) with coordinates and figures/tables, and also reports PPI connectivity but not as the sole result. All required sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met.

The paper reports simultaneous fMRI in healthy adult communicative pairs performing an interactive social-communication task, with group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (random-effects, cluster-level correction) identifying BOLD effects (e.g., rSTG) linked to mutual understanding. Sample: 54 healthy right-handed adults (27 pairs), ages 18–27. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task, healthy adult sample, and reporting of whole-brain group results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (primiparous mothers, mean age 24.1) using a social-related task (listening to own vs. other infant cry) addressing attachment and social-affective processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (own cry > control sound; own cry > other cry) with whole-brain cluster correction and tables/figures of coordinates and activation maps. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, reports within-group whole-brain task effects in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task and matched age-judgement version) meeting the review objective. The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n≈25; age range 18–59) reported separately from the Tourette group. Group-level whole-brain task activation results for healthy controls are reported (Supplementary Tables S2/S3 and descriptive text) with voxelwise thresholding and FWE correction, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Task-related activations are reported as tables/figures in the full text. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete.

This full-text reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=60, mean age ~20) using a social-related task (explicit control of interpersonal trust/distrust). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., trust+distrust > age; trust > age; distrust > age) with FWE-corrected thresholds and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures. Methods, results, and discussion are all present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=33, ages 20–34) using social-related tasks (charitable donation task and EmpaToM measuring empathy and perspective taking). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses and searchlight MVPA results with reported clusters/coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study directly probes social-related processing: participants read literary passages manipulated for social content (Social vs Non-social) while undergoing task-based fMRI, satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants ages 19–26 (N=26), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task contrasts (Social>Non-social and Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-level correction and a Table of peak voxels/clusters and whole-brain figures, meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state analyses, reports within-group whole-brain task effects (not only between-group contrasts), includes adults within 18–65, and is empirical with original fMRI data. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of task-evoked fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study includes a social cognition task (explicitly analyzed among seven tasks) using task-based fMRI (I3). The samples are healthy adult participants from HCP (ages 22–35 mostly) and UCLA (mean age 31.1, range 21–50), meeting the 18–65 requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (voxel-wise GLM, figures showing activation maps, and Supplementary figures), clearly identified as healthy/control group results (I5). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and supplementary materials and described in the text (I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core article content is present (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing/inferring others’ preferences) in healthy adults (n=64; age range 18–26), satisfying sample criteria. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (parametric modulation by self–other discrepancy), with peak coordinates and cluster statistics described in the text/tables/figures. The task is social (perception/understanding of others). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full-text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=14, mean age 35.9) that manipulates social context (human vs. machine competitor) to probe Theory of Mind/social competition while performing a Stroop task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with contrasts and thresholding, and provides tables of activation coordinates and cluster statistics. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment of methods and whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI hyperscanning study of social interaction (mutual gaze and joint attention) in healthy adult participants (mean ages ≈21–23 years). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (SPM analyses with cluster-level FWE correction; tables of coordinates and figures are provided) and describes behavioral and neural results for the healthy/control sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria (functional MRI during social task; healthy adult sample; whole-brain group results are reported; whole-brain results acceptable as tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses fMRI during social-related tasks (social distance trials comparing friends vs acquaintances); (I4) Healthy adult sample (N=15, ages 20–28) with results reported for the healthy group; (I5) Reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight MVPA and RSA maps tested across participants with FDR-corrected results; figures and tables present significant clusters); (I6) Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognition task (viewing photographs of social groups and rating emotions), with healthy adult participants (Princeton undergraduates, mean age 19.5). The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects analyses, Talairach coordinates, t-statistics, voxel counts, and contrasts such as subtractive and 3-vs-1 contrasts) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Reporting includes coordinates/figures and full methods/results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used an auditory task involving perception of human footsteps (participants judged motion direction of walking persons), which constitutes perception/understanding of others (a social-perception construct). The sample comprises healthy adults (ages 20–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-related analyses (contrast ‘footstep minus rest’) used to define VOIs and references group maps and Table 1 (supplementary materials contain activation maps), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates generation of cognitive reappraisals for anger-eliciting interpersonal scenarios (RGT), which engages social-cognitive processes (theory of mind/empathy, perception/understanding of others). Sample: healthy adults (N=45, ages 18–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (conjunction analysis and RGT>AUT, AUT>RGT contrasts) with voxelwise FWE correction and cluster reporting; results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of theory-of-mind/false-belief processing (social cognition: perception/understanding of others) in healthy adults. The methods report fMRI acquisition and whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts (e.g., belief > photo/map) with reported SPMs and peak coordinates (right TPJ, left TPJ, precuneus, STS, etc.), and a whole-brain implicit false- > true-belief SPM. Participants were healthy adults (mean age 22.7; n=16 included in MRI analyses). Results include group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social cognition task (Theory of Mind visual jokes) relevant to perception/understanding of others (I3). It includes a clearly reported healthy control group (n=13) with results presented separately (I4). The manuscript provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (within-group activations and contrasts) for the control/healthy group (Tables and figures described; thresholding and random-effects SPM analysis reported), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (direct and reflected self-appraisals; social cognition/self-perception). It includes a healthy adult group (N=12; ages 22.6–30.4) with results reported separately and compares adults and adolescents. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked analyses (unmasked whole-brain contrasts, corrected and thresholded; conjunction analyses and maps described), with coordinates and figures. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is a narrative review summarizing prior fMRI studies rather than reporting original empirical fMRI data from a healthy adult sample. It does not present primary participant samples, methods, or group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for a healthy/control adult group. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical review without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria I3 (study uses fMRI during a social task), I4 (reports healthy adult sample), and I5 (reports whole-brain group-level healthy-control task maps) are not met by this article itself, although the review discusses such studies. Full text appears complete for a review article (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (compassion/empathy toward others’ suffering) using a task that contrasts images of human suffering versus neutral images and tests regulation strategies. Participants were healthy adults (aged 18–45; n=41 analyzed) meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction and whole-brain corrected results identifying IPC and DLPFC at p < .01) and references whole-brain results/tables in the Supplement (S3–S5). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied, no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed emotion versus age judgments on dynamic face stimuli (social perception). Sample consists of healthy adults (final N=25, ages 21–33), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: a whole-brain random-effects contrast (faces > objects) used to define ROIs, and whole-brain searchlight analyses with second-level statistics (SnPM corrections and cluster tables), with results presented in tables/figures. Thus it provides healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (pupil mimicry, trust; theory-of-mind network) using a task involving social stimuli (eye region) and trust decisions. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=40 behavioral; n=34 fMRI), ages within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM, whole-brain contrasts, FLAME mixed-effects) with coordinates, figures, and tables of activation (e.g., precuneus, TPJ, STS, mPFC), and uses appropriate reporting of voxelwise results and permutation/FWE corrections. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group healthy whole-brain effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and none of the exclusion criteria are met.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4. The paper reports only between-group contrasts (high-Mach > low-Mach) from two-sample t-tests and presents group differences; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for a healthy/control group (e.g., main effect of GAME>CONTROL for the full healthy sample or for either subgroup reported as an unmasked within-group map). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social task — Trust Game), I4 (sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 19–30), I6 (whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/tables/figures). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map from a healthy/control group separate from between-group contrasts). Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (cooperation/competition; self-other judgments) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 24 healthy participants aged 19–31. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and corrected results (family-wise error cluster correction; whole-brain contrasts and peak coordinates are provided in Table 1 and figures). Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (task-based fMRI of social constructs, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain healthy-group results reported).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (vitality forms) in healthy adults. The study uses task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (listening/observing/imaging speech and actions) and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts with voxelwise results and MNI coordinates (FWE-corrected), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Sample consists of 18 healthy adults (ages ~25), meeting the age and healthy-group requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within age range).

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social-related task (Multifaceted Empathy Test) assessing cognitive and emotional empathy (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group reported separately from the BPD patients (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task activation results for the healthy/control group (main effects and tables/figures for controls are described; meets I5 and I6). The study is empirical, presents methods, results, and discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and tables described. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social related processing in healthy adults.

All inclusion criteria are met: the study uses task-based fMRI of a social interaction paradigm (a modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) probing reactive aggression and social processing (I3). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 22.9; final N=15) and results for the healthy group are reported (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses with statistical maps and tables of coordinates for task contrasts (decision and outcome phases) (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (person knowledge retrieval), using healthy adult participants (24 and 26 subjects; ages in 20s) and describes group-level whole-brain univariate GLM contrasts (voxel-level FWE-corrected maps) as well as MVPA, PPI, and DCM. Whole-brain task activation maps and contrasts for the healthy groups are clearly reported in the text, figures, and tables. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 18–27) using tasks that probe understanding of others’ actions (Why-How) and object categorization (Categories-Exemplars), constructs within social cognition/understanding of others. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with corrected thresholds and tables/figures describing activations and conjunction contrasts. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social exclusion (Cyberball), a social-related task (affiliation/ostracism). The sample consists of healthy adults (n=20 after exclusions; ages ~25) within the 18–65 range. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (social exclusion > fair play), reports cluster-corrected thresholds, tables of coordinates, and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range, non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study using an explicit emotion-recognition task (social perception of others) in healthy adult participants (n=21 males, ages 21–33). The paper reports group-level whole-slab/whole-brain analyses (explicitly describes whole-slab analysis, presents activation maps and reports voxel coordinates for significant clusters) in the healthy sample. Hence it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported for the healthy group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 18–28) that examines action observation and representation of multiple observed actions—relevant to social perception/understanding of others. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Observation > Neutral; 2H DIFF > 2H SAME; Squeeze > No Squeeze) with thresholding and peak coordinates and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social-cognitive processing (perception/understanding of others; participants judged whether observed actions were ‘biological’ vs ‘artificial’), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=12, mean age 27.3±4.7), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and present voxelwise results with thresholding, tables of activated regions and coordinates (Tables 1 and 2), satisfying whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study uses a social-cognitive visual perspective-taking task (I3) and includes a separate healthy adult control group with reported results (n=37) (I4). However, the authors explicitly used a region-of-interest (ROI) approach and restricted analyzed voxels to a combined ROI mask rather than performing/reporting an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain, group-level healthy-task effect (I5 not met). Exclusion criterion E2 applies (only ROI-limited analyses reported). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of healthy young adults (ages 21–24) that includes an explicit social manipulation (peer observation vs alone) during the Stoplight task, satisfying the requirement for social-related task engagement. The sample is a healthy adult cohort (n=49) with exclusions for clinical alcohol disorders, meeting the sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., Go/No-Go: No-Go>Go; Stoplight: Risk>Safe) and provides thresholded/unthresholded whole-brain maps via NeuroVault, meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain task maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-fMRI study of social cognition (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task), meeting I3. It includes an age-matched healthy adult control group with results reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., mental state > age and group effects) with cluster-level FWE correction and references to tables/figures for controls (I5, I6). The full text supplied contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and include within-group healthy control whole-brain activations rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social attribution task (judging another’s awareness) in healthy adults (n=50; ages 18–49). It provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (H trials vs E trials) thresholded and corrected (P < 0.05, cluster correction) with Talairach coordinates and figures/tables reporting the activation map, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The sample and analyses meet the review’s inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI studies of social processing. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening purposes.

The study uses fMRI with a social-related task (cyberball) so I3 is satisfied. However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain within-group task activation map for the healthy control group; results are reported mainly as between-group contrasts (BPD>HC, NSSI>HC) and a conjunction of these contrasts. Therefore it fails to provide a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I4 and I5 not met). This meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study investigates emotional prosody comprehension (a social-communication task involving perception/understanding of others' emotions), meeting the review objective. Sample: 19 healthy adult males (age range 18–51) reported separately — satisfies healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (emotion vs neutral; complex vs simple) with statistical thresholds and corrected cluster results, with coordinates presented — satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (PDF-only); unable to verify presence of a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5). Based on the abstract, the study uses fMRI during social-related processing of emotional facial expressions (I3) and reports data from 12 healthy subjects (I4). However, because only the abstract/metadata are provided and the full article (methods/results/tables/figures) is not accessible, I cannot confirm that whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported (required by I5). No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are clearly met. Therefore I exclude due to incomplete full text and inability to confirm I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (face gender categorization), meeting the meta-analysis focus on social-related processing. It tested healthy adults (N=16, ages 19–42), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (random-effects GLM; contrast gender-different > gender-same) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and described activations in multiple whole-brain clusters (right CoS, left precuneus, right lateral occipital gyrus), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing), Results (ROI and whole-brain analyses), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This study uses fMRI with a social/attachment task (listening to attachment narratives) (I3 met) and reports results from a healthy adult sample (fMRI sample: 23 healthy males aged ~29) (I4 met). However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for the healthy group (no univariate task activation contrasts); instead analyses are post-task resting-state, seed-based (caudate nucleus) functional connectivity and ROI-seed FC maps. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (only seed-based/connectivity/resting-state analyses without healthy-group whole-brain task activation) and E2 (analyses centered on ROI/seed with no whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study of empathy for pain that manipulates social context (presence/agency of another person). It directly addresses social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises 26 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.4), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., (PCO+PCS)-(NPO+NPS), social-context contrasts, and interaction contrasts) with correction for multiple comparisons (FDR p<0.05) and tables of stereotactic coordinates, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results include whole-brain activation tables and figures and PPI connectivity analyses, and healthy-group effects are clearly reported. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, tables/figures, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/highlights/metadata provided). Based on available information: inclusion I3 is satisfied (fMRI during social-related task: dynamic facial expression processing). Cannot confirm inclusion I4 (healthy adult sample ages 18–65) — participant ages and sample details not reported in the provided content. Cannot confirm I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy/control group) — the abstract mentions ROI targeting and localizer but does not explicitly state whole-brain group maps. Cannot confirm I6 (location/format of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the available text. Because required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5, at minimum) cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an fMRI study with a healthy adult control group and reports whole-brain group activation maps, but the experimental task is a monetary-reward continuous performance task (sustained attention with monetary incentive), which is not a social-related task as defined by the review (e.g., social communication, perception/understanding of self/others, affiliation/attachment). Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered; the full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test), includes a healthy adult control group (18 healthy men, ages comparable to other adult groups), and presents whole-brain, group-level analyses. The Methods state that single-subject contrast images (mental state attribution > gender discrimination) were analyzed separately for all five groups using one-sample t tests, and the Results/figures/tables report whole-brain cluster-level findings and planned between-group contrasts; ROI analyses are supplementary. Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables (cluster PFWE < .05), meeting the review’s reporting format requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state only, or missing healthy adult group) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes social-related tasks (reasoning about others’ mental states) presented as both text and video. Sample: 45 healthy adult participants (ages 19–23), satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (fixed- and random-effects analyses), figures of activation/deactivation, and peak coordinates in Appendix A, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendices) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

Full text appears to be incomplete (only abstract/highlights provided). Primary reason for exclusion: E3 (study reports only resting-state fMRI analyses and does not include a task-evoked, whole-brain healthy-group activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes a healthy adult control group and results reported for both groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task; study used resting-state fMRI), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group). Given the lack of task-based whole-brain healthy-group results and incomplete full text, the study is excluded from this task-based social fMRI review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Trust Game) with healthy adult participants (N=18 analyzed; ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., defect>reciprocate, reciprocate>defect), provides MNI coordinates, statistical thresholds and cluster correction, and ROI analyses. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants engaged in an interactive rating task where another person’s communicated emotional arousal influenced responses. It meets I3 (task is social/interaction-based and uses task-based fMRI), I4 (healthy adult sample, students, mean age 23.95), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with clusterwise FWE correction and tabulated activations), and I6 (whole-brain results shown in tables/figures and described in text). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical issues). Thus the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (observation of mouth actions/oral communicative actions across human and non-human agents), in healthy adult participants (three groups age range 18–60). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses are performed and reported (thresholded at p<0.05 FWE) with results described in text, tables and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of self- and other-related social cognition in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and coordinate tables. The methods describe fMRI acquisition and whole-brain SPM analyses (thresholds, cluster sizes) and report contrasts (e.g., self>syllables, old/same>new) with peak coordinates and SPM figures. Participants are healthy adults (age range 19.4–31), and results for the healthy sample are reported. The task probes perception/understanding of self and others (trait judgments about self and close friend), meeting the review’s social processing domain. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, figures/tables description, and discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 29.4) that used a social-related task (judgments of social concepts) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts, coordinates, figures, and conjunction analyses) for the healthy sample. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study that directly contrasts social (stereotype) and non-social semantic processing, meeting the review objective. Participants: 19 healthy adults aged 19–28 (within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (e.g., ‘social’>‘non-social’ and ‘non-social’>‘social’) with corrected thresholds, figures and tables of peak coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=27, mean age 27) that examines processing of others' facial expressions (canonical disgust vs distaste), a social-cognitive task tapping perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (canonical disgust vs neutral; canonical disgust vs distaste; distaste vs neutral) with tables/figures of coordinates and random-effects analysis, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception), using a task involving perception/understanding of others. Sample: healthy adult participants (ages 18–32), reported separately and meeting the age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with coordinate tables, cluster thresholds, and contrasts (e.g., faces associated with behaviors vs. novel faces; disgusting vs. aggressive), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (mentalizing, empathy for pain, prosocial decision-making) in healthy adult participants (N=32, females, mean age 22.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (SPM12; cluster-level correction P=0.05 with voxelwise threshold P=0.001) and provides coordinates/tables for activation clusters (Tables and Supplementary Material referenced). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is an empirical paper). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=32, ages ~24) who performed a social task manipulating collaboration and competition. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked SPM results (parametric modulations, contrasts, clusterwise FWE correction) and provides tables/figures of activations and VBM results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion recognition (a social cognition task) with adult participants including a healthy control group. The paper reports within-subject, within-group and between-group fMRI analyses and includes an exploratory whole-brain analysis reporting clusters for the neurotypical (healthy) control group (e.g., inferior frontal gyrus and fusiform gyrus clusters). Full text contains introduction, methods, results (ROI and whole-brain), and discussion. Therefore it meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (speed-dating paradigm) in healthy adults scanned with fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (contrasts, tables of coordinates, thresholding, and figures) for the healthy scanned sample (N=38). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a naturalistic, social-related task (video-based theory-of-mind/naturalistic mentalising) and reports group-level whole-brain task activation for the healthy control group (ToM > physical inference; Fig.1a and Table 3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=22; age range 19–46) reported separately. Whole-brain voxelwise results for the control group are presented (cluster-corrected activations and coordinates), satisfying acceptable reporting formats. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (only citation/metadata presented). Cannot verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (uncertain if task is an fMRI social-related task), I4 (uncertain whether healthy adult control group is included and reported separately), and I5 (uncertain whether whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation maps are reported). No exclusion criteria from list (E2–E6) can be confirmed from available information. Recommend obtaining full text to reassess eligibility.

This paper reports an fMRI study using an empathy-for-pain paradigm (socially relevant processing) in healthy adult participants (male, age 18–40). The sample includes a healthy control group and a stress group (final N=67 for fMRI analyses). The authors report voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (family-wise error correction over the whole brain), conjunction analyses, and tables/figures with MNI coordinates for reported peaks; results are clearly described for the (healthy) groups. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but not required. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines action observation and mirror system responses, which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (social cognition). It reports data from healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 20–34). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and conjunctions are described and thresholded (P<0.05 corrected across the whole brain), with peak coordinates and tables/figures reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or out-of-range age issues).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-communication task (emotional speech prosody), uses a healthy adult sample (n=22, mean age 24.8, within 18–65), and presents group-level whole-brain task activation results (cluster-corrected emotional > neutral prosody; Table 2, Figures). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures in addition to ROI analyses. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). All relevant inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6.

This paper reports original task-based fMRI data in healthy adult participants (ages 21–33) who performed a social-related semantic retrieval task contrasting why (mentalizing/abstract social cognition) vs how (concrete/action) processing. The manuscript provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, whole-brain contrasts) with cluster-extent correction, tables/coordinates, and ROI follow-up; results are clearly reported for the healthy/control sample. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/contrasts), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E2 applies: the study reports primarily ROI-based analyses using small-volume correction (amygdala, insula, striatum, OFC) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — viewing dynamic facial expressions/social communication) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group). I6 is not applicable because qualifying whole-brain results are not provided. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; decision based on provided full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-cognitive (mentalizing) processing about groups and individuals using task-based fMRI. Participants were healthy adults (ages 18–27 in Experiment 1; 18–23 in Experiment 2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical) with tables and figures of results and multivariate searchlight analyses. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps), and I6 (results reported via tables/figures) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=19 analyzed, ages 18–30) that used the Trust Game, a social/reciprocity task, during task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, cluster-level correction via AFNI 3dClustSim) and presents univariate activation results (tables/figures) and ICA/network analyses. All required inclusion criteria are met: (I3) task-based fMRI during a social-related task (reciprocity/trust), (I4) healthy adult sample within age 18–65, (I5) group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps/contrasts reported, and (I6) whole-brain results presented in tables/figures described in text. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social processing (manipulation of social context of gaze shifts), with healthy adult participants (behavioral N=10, fMRI N=12; ages 18–40/41 within 18–65). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed in SPM2 and multiple whole-brain contrasts are reported (e.g., gaze-shift vs no-movement; incorrect vs correct; social vs unsocial) with thresholding and tables of activated loci described. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), results (behavioral, imaging contrasts), and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly probes social-related processing (attribution of intentions/mentalizing toward perceived human-created music vs computer-generated music), meeting the review objective. Participants were healthy adults (n=12 analyzed; ages 21–31), satisfying sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Composer > Computer) with coordinates and cluster-level correction and a second-level random-effects analysis; results are presented in tables and figures. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; includes healthy adult whole-brain task activations; empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of dynamic audio–visual emotional perception, which is social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Participants are healthy adults (Study 1: n=10, ages 18–33; Study 2: n=5, ages 18–23), meeting the sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (multiple whole-brain analyses, conjunctions, tables of coordinates, figures; Study 1 used random-effects group analysis and whole-brain thresholds are described), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group results. Results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining social competition during a task (social comparison/mentalizing) — satisfying I3. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (20 females, ages 18–35), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses and contrasts (competition > no competition; working memory and feedback phases), with cluster thresholds and coordinates provided in tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, acknowledgments) is present in the provided content. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, age range within 18–65, empirical data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social perception/social communication (perception and understanding of others) using a task where healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 23–33) rated naturalness of dyadic nonverbal interactions, satisfying sample requirements. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (multiple contrasts, cluster-corrected; tables/coordinates and figures provided) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examines neural representations of sentence meaning, including a clear social/people dimension. Methods report functional MRI during a sentence-reading task with stimuli including social interactions; factor analysis identified a ‘people/social interactions’ factor and associated whole-brain voxel clusters. Participants: seven healthy, right-handed, native English-speaking adults (age 20–35), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (factor analysis-derived voxel clusters and associated locations reported; Supporting Information referenced) and presents task-evoked activation results tied to semantic/social content. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-related construct: Perception and Understanding of Self), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=10, mean age 26.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME, Z-statistic images thresholded and cluster-corrected) and provides coordinates/tables and figures of activation maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age-appropriate, empirical fMRI task data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) in a sample of healthy adult males (ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., high > low provocation) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures with MNI coordinates, and describes these results in the text. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range, non-empirical) are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI of a social communication paradigm (charades) in healthy adult participants (n=18 analyzed, mean age 27.5), and reports group-level, whole-brain differential Granger-causality (bbGCM) maps that were taken to the second level and thresholded for multiple comparisons. The paper presents group-level whole-brain statistical maps (figures and described thresholds) identifying regions in the guesser that echo gesturer activity, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply.
