Study is an fMRI investigation of social processing (impression updating of others) in healthy adults (N=21, ages 18–31). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, imaging acquisition, preprocessing and GLM), Results (whole-brain contrasts, interaction effects, tables and figures), and Discussion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps and corrected cluster results (e.g., L2>F3 contrast, 3dANOVA3, AlphaSim correction) and presents coordinate tables and figures for these effects. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition (social expectancy violations along warmth and competence), satisfying the review objective. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=12, mean age 20.4, within 18–65) so I4 is met. The methods and results include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses with coordinates and corrected thresholds (reported random-effects analyses, Talairach coordinates, cluster-level correction), satisfying I5 and I6. The task is clearly social-related (person perception, warmth/competence), satisfying I3. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: the study reports whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), is not solely connectivity/resting-state, includes healthy adults, and is empirical original data. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating perception/recognition of self vs others' body parts (a social-related task: Perception and Understanding of Self/Others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain localization contrasts (e.g., body minus objects; objects minus body parts) with Talairach coordinates and cluster voxel counts used to identify EBA, LOC, and V1/2, satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (Experiments: N=12 and N=15 with exclusions noted). Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of pain empathy (social-related processing). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=21; ages 18–60) with results reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses for the control group (e.g., Self vs Other and Effectiveness contrasts), with results described in the main text and referenced Supplementary Table S1. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; healthy-group whole-brain maps are provided; participants within age range; empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Study includes an fMRI experiment (Study 2) with healthy adult participants (heterosexual men, n=21, ages within 18–65) performing a social-related task (passive viewing of sexualized and clothed human targets probing mentalizing/Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (voxelwise threshold p<.001, AlphaSim cluster correction), tables of activated regions, and figures, clearly derived from the healthy participant group. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly addresses social-related processing (impression formation about people vs objects), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (N=14; ages 18.3–23.7), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trials) with voxelwise thresholding and tables/coordinates (SPM analyses), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, participant ages are within range, and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study addresses social group processing (movie viewing of rival fans) and uses fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 20.9), so inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) are satisfied. However, the main experimental results for the social task (movie viewing/ISC analyses) are reported using region-of-interest / atlas-based summary measures (averaged time series across 55 Harvard–Oxford regions and ROI analyses) rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the movie task. The only voxelwise group maps described are from a category localizer used to define ROIs, not the primary social task contrasts. Therefore the paper does not provide a whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the social task (I5 not met), and effectively reports ROI/parcel-based results without an accompanying whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task map, meeting exclusion criterion E2. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2.

This paper is a review/non-empirical article (explicitly described as a review) summarizing theoretical and prior fMRI findings rather than reporting original task-based fMRI data in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical review without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not present original fMRI during a social task), I4 (no report of an analyzed healthy adult sample in an original empirical study), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported for a healthy group), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results presented). Additionally, the provided full text appears incomplete (only introduction and abstract present; methods/results absent), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26). The task manipulated social relationship (self, friend, antagonist) during a gambling task and examined neural responses at trial onset and outcome. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (repeated-measures ANOVAs) with tables/coordinates and figures, including whole-brain effects and SPM results; small-volume corrections were applied for a priori ROIs but whole-brain maps and coordinates are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines perception of faces and changeable social aspects (gaze, expression), i.e., social communication, using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants. Methods report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FEAT, Z statistic images, Talairach coordinates, Table 1), and results/figures show unmasked healthy-group task activations. The sample comprises eight healthy adult observers. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This fMRI study examines perception of others’ emotional eye-region cues (social-related processing) using a task with masked fearful and happy eyes and reports task-evoked group-level results. Sample comprises healthy adult males (final N=43, mean age ~24), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The paper includes exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses (reported clusters and Supplementary Tables) in addition to ROI analyses, and these whole-brain results are clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within 18–65). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making in healthy adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses; however, the paper primarily presents between-group contrasts comparing two healthy subgroups (proself vs prosocial). I could not find an unmasked, whole-brain within-group or overall healthy-control task activation map (e.g., main effect or within-group contrast for the full healthy sample or an explicit healthy-control group). According to exclusion criterion E4, studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect must be excluded. Therefore the study is excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI task of action imitation/observation (a social-related paradigm tapping perception/understanding of others), includes a separate healthy adult control group (N=16) with results reported, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (within-group contrasts for healthy subjects reported via tables/figures and Talairach coordinates). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for healthy adult whole-brain task fMRI studies of social processing.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages ~21) that used a social perception task (passive viewing of in-group vs out-group facial expressions) addressing social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and interaction ((disgusted out-group–neutral out-group)–(disgusted in-group–neutral in-group)) with thresholding and corrected cluster results (tables/figures described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present, and healthy adult results are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-interaction task (virtual handshake) that manipulates social acceptance vs. rejection, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=16, mean age 27.4) reported separately from the clinical group. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts are reported for the control group (refusal vs. acceptance), with tables/figures and corrected cluster results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of social persuasion (celebrity expertise) in healthy adult participants (n=24, mean age 21.8). The task probes social-cognitive processes (perception/understanding of others, persuasion/trust). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (thresholding, cluster correction) with tables/figures of activation coordinates and ROI-SVC supplementary checks. All inclusion criteria are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and conclusions.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (n=30, mean age 21.2). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (thresholded maps, figures, and tables) as well as ROI and exploratory whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked results), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social cognition (theory-of-mind: cooperation, deception) using a task with cartoon social interactions, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises 13 healthy adult participants (ages 22–38), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses (exploratory second-level random-effects contrasts of ToM vs non-ToM and direct contrasts between conditions) with coordinates, figures, and tables, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, analyses), results (voxelwise contrasts, coordinates, figures), and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining social-related processing (perception of potential social involvement from biological motion) using a task in which healthy adult participants judged facing-toward vs away point-light and human-like walkers. Sample: 16 healthy adults (mean age 22.75), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation analyses with stereotaxic coordinates and FWE-corrected results (tables and figures), thus providing whole-brain evidence. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, GLM), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study of social-related processing (social preference task) in healthy adults (N=21, ages 23–51), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Preference > Gender) with statistical thresholds (p<0.05 FDR-corrected) and tables/figures of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain task activation). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 23–39) using a social-related task (judgments of ambiguous social interactions) with reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVA/t-tests, FDR-corrected; tables and statistical maps provided). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, statistical analysis), Results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging results), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social processing (monitoring outcomes of others' decisions) in healthy adults (n=12, mean age 21). The experiment used task-based fMRI with group-level, voxelwise GLM/random-effects analyses (SPM) and reports voxel coordinates and SPM results (with small-volume correction for ACC), satisfying whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level voxelwise task activation maps reported), I6 (coordinates/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of ASD (with and without ADHD) and typically developing controls using ICA/FNC; it does not report any task-based fMRI during social-related processing nor any healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (resting-state analyses only). Inclusion criteria satisfied: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-based social fMRI), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked map from healthy group), I4 (healthy adult group 18–65 not clearly reported/separated). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines neural correlates of vocal emotion recognition using fMRI (meets I3). It reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and tables/figures for the healthy sample (meets I5 and I6). However, the sample consists of children/adolescents aged 8–19 and does not include a separate healthy adult group (age 18–65) analyzed or reported separately. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Per exclusion criterion E5, because no healthy adult subgroup (18–65) is reported separately, the study is ineligible for this meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

EXCLUDED because the paper reports only ROI-based task analyses (and SVC ROI VBM results) and does not provide any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social processing — social closeness task with friends vs unfamiliar faces) and I4 (includes healthy adult participants aged 19–30). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain task activation map from the healthy/control group is reported). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — trustworthiness judgments) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, results reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain/voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group; analyses and reported results are ROI-based). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (study reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (gaze following and finger pointing) in healthy adult participants (n=17, ages 20–34). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (gaze vs baseline, finger vs baseline, and subtraction contrasts) analyzed with SPM2 and a random-effects second-level analysis, with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds described. The manuscript contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full article text present). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-related construct: Perception and Understanding of Self) in healthy adult participants (final sample N=16, ages 19–24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and presents coordinates and cluster-corrected activations (e.g., MPFC, PCC, precuneus) for contrasts comparing identifications of ambiguous faces, satisfying requirements for whole-brain evidence. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages) are met. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This paper reports an fMRI study using an explicit social attribution task (inferring situational causes of avatars’ emotional behaviors), includes a healthy adult control group (n=16) reported separately, and presents group-level whole-brain task activation results (between- and within-group contrasts, cluster-thresholded maps, and a Table of coordinates) with descriptions of % signal changes for the control group. Thus it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group reported), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and text). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study investigating judgments of pride (a self-conscious social emotion) vs joy, directly addressing social-cognition/Perception and Understanding of Self/Others. The sample is healthy adults (n=16, ages ~21), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (P−N, J−N, P−J) with tables of peak coordinates, statistical thresholds, and figures, meeting the whole-brain reporting requirement. Results for the healthy/control group are reported clearly. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of theory-of-mind (social) processing in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 25.7), using task-based fMRI during social and non-social story conditions. The paper reports whole-brain group-level random-effects contrasts (e.g., false-belief vs false-photograph localizer; unexpected vs expected outcomes) with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster peak coordinates reported in tables and text. Supplementary behavioral and ROI/MVPA analyses are present but whole-brain task activation maps/coordinates for the healthy sample are clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (maternal perception of own child’s facial emotions) using a task-based emotional face recognition paradigm (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group of mothers without early life maltreatment, reported separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task activation maps/results (e.g., familiarity effect in control mothers: medial frontal gyrus, whole-brain pFWE<0.001), satisfying the requirement for at least one healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5). Results are reported in ROI and whole-brain analyses and group-level contrasts are clearly described (I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study assesses processing of social stimuli (angry and happy faces) during task performance, satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample comprises N=30 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.2), meeting the age and healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM full-factorial, FWE-corrected results, whole-brain and ROI contrasts) and presents results in text, figures, and tables, fulfilling the whole-brain reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants in range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI social-related task and healthy adult participants (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the abstract does not report whether the paper contains at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5). The neuroimaging results described focus on functional connectivity, which raises the possibility the paper emphasizes connectivity/seed-based analyses (potential E3) rather than whole-brain task activation, but this cannot be confirmed from the provided text. Because I5 cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (face-emotion perception during a gender discrimination task), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=30 screened for psychiatric history). Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results are reported for the healthy sample (main effects across all subjects and genotype group comparisons; whole-brain comparisons at p < .001 uncorrected are mentioned and supplementary tables provided). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported for healthy subjects), and I6 (allowance of whole-brain results in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI of social processing (audiovisual integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions); (I4) Sample comprises 24 healthy adults (mean age 26) with results reported for this healthy group; (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain (RFX) voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected results and coordinates; (I6) Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper includes whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only), includes task-evoked activations (not only connectivity), reports within-group effects for healthy adults, and is an empirical fMRI study. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that used a social-related task (watching videos of violent dyadic interactions while attending to aggressor vs victim), fulfilling I3. Sample: 15 healthy adult males (mean age 23.6), within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (e.g., all conditions vs baseline; focus on aggressor vs victim), with figures/tables and cluster-level correction, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not limited to ROIs only, the study provides whole-brain task activation maps (E2 not met); it is not connectivity-only (E3 not met); it reports within-group whole-brain effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E4 not met); participants are adults within range (E5 not met); and it is empirical original research (E6 not met). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI to examine social-related processing (perception of others' pupil dynamics as social signals); (I4) sample consists of healthy adults (n=14, mean age 22 within 18–65); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (second-level random effects, whole-brain corrected clusters and voxelwise results with coordinates); (I6) whole-brain results are described in text, tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met; the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception/recognition (social processing: perception and understanding of others), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: 18 healthy adults aged 19–36, so the healthy adult sample criterion is satisfied. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain Random Effects task contrasts (differential activation for false recognition vs recognition/correct rejection) with Talairach coordinates, cluster correction, and statistical thresholds — i.e., whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (coordinates and figures/tables), satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, and is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the participant sample consists of adolescents (ages 11–17), not healthy adults; therefore exclusion criterion E5 is met. Inclusion criterion I3 is met (the study uses task-based fMRI of social/mentalizing processing). However inclusion criteria I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) and I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation map from a healthy adult group) are not met because the healthy/control group are adolescents, not adults, and no healthy adult whole-brain results are provided. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI during a clearly social-related task (agreement with music experts) and reports results for a healthy adult control group separately (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group; fMRI results are reported primarily as between-group contrasts and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses, with whole-brain results showing only group differences (controls > cocaine users). Thus it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of Theory of Mind using healthy adult control participants (I3 met). However, although healthy controls are included, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Analyses report group ICA component maps computed across all participants (ASD + controls) and report between-group contrasts (ASD vs control) for components. There is no standalone whole-brain healthy-group task effect map reported; thus exclusion criterion E4 is met. Inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied because results for the healthy group are not reported separately as a whole-brain task map and no control-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is provided.

This article reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~25–26 across experiments) using dynamic and static facial-expression stimuli, which are social-perception/social-communication tasks. The paper provides whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (ANOVA) with voxelwise results and cluster-corrected thresholds, presents stereotaxic coordinates and tables of activation foci, and describes methods, results, and discussion in full. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Accordingly, include the study in the review.

The paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition (prediction of others’ behavior framed as desires vs rules), using healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 18–44). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (second-level flexible factorial models) with cluster- and voxel-level corrections and reports coordinates/tables of activations. Behavioral task and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present (full article content provided). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of explicit social trait judgments (trustworthiness, attractiveness) on vocal stimuli in healthy adults. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8; cluster-level FWE correction) with coordinates and figures, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 21–60 within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24 analyzed, ages 19–31) that investigates recognition of personally familiar versus famous faces, a social-cognitive process (perception/understanding of others, social attachment/affiliation). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., P1–Cp1, P1–F1) with standard SPM random-effects analyses, cluster correction across the whole brain, and tables/figures describing maps and peak coordinates. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants within 18–65, empirical data present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This paper reports an original task-based fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. It uses an ecologically-valid social task (watching partner video-vignettes with self vs other perspective instructions), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 23–40 with exclusions applied, satisfying I4. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., self positive > neutral, other negative > neutral), corrected for multiple comparisons and presented in tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating anticipatory neural processes during active interpersonal touch (a clearly social-related task). The sample comprises 16 healthy adults aged 20–34. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise random-effects analyses (multiple whole-brain contrasts, cluster correction, Talairach coordinates, figures and tables) and a tactile localizer; results for the healthy group are explicitly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because it reports resting-state fMRI network/ROI (seed-to-seed and graph-theory) analyses and a behavioral Theory-of-Mind task completed outside the scanner, rather than task-evoked fMRI during a social-related task. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI/seed/network-only analyses with no whole-brain task activation reported) and E3 (resting-state analyses only, no healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from healthy/control group), and I4 (sample requirement: at least one healthy adult group 18–65 is not clearly satisfied — the healthy sample spans ages 12–24 and no adult-only healthy-group task activation is reported). No inclusion criteria are fully satisfied. Full text appears complete for screening.

Full text provided is only the abstract and metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract, the study is an fMRI task on social communication (I3 satisfied). However, the abstract does not report sample demographics or ages, so I4 cannot be confirmed. Crucially, the abstract describes brain activations but does not confirm that group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for a healthy adult group are reported (I5 cannot be confirmed; I6 likewise cannot be verified). Because the complete article (methods, full results with whole-brain maps/tables/coordinates) is missing, I cannot verify required whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete full text and inability to confirm I4 and I5.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (sighted mean age 32±13; congenitally blind mean age 44±16), using task-based fMRI to probe perception/understanding of others' actions (mirror system)—a social-related construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., familiar action sounds vs environmental sounds; motor pantomime vs rest) with cluster-size correction and provides anatomical maps, coordinate-based results, and contrasts for the healthy sighted group and for the congenitally blind group separately. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This article is a non-empirical review/synthesis of model-based fMRI and dopamine studies rather than an original empirical fMRI study in healthy adults. Exclusion met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data in healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met: none (no original data). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not itself use fMRI during a social-related task as an empirical report), I4 (does not report an original healthy adult sample with separate results), I5 (does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map as original results), I6 (does not report original whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement for a healthy group). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of joint attention, a social-cognitive task (meets I3). It includes healthy adult control groups (two neurotypical groups; ages 18–39 reported) with results reported separately from the ASD group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the healthy/control groups (within-group RJA vs SA, IJA vs SA, JA vs SA), with whole-brain random-effects analyses, thresholding, coordinates, and tables/figures (meets I5). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in text (meets I6). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper primarily reports group-by-age interaction (ASD vs TDC) effects and between-group differences in covariation with age; the provided full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social/empathic processing) and I4 (contains a healthy control group that includes adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no explicit whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy/control group is presented in the provided full text). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded per E4.

The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task—effect of expert advice/social context on decision making) and I4 (includes a healthy adult group, ages 18–45). The paper also reports voxelwise coordinate results and supplementary tables (I6). However, the full-text presents primarily developmental (age-group) contrasts and ROI follow-up tests; it does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy adult group alone. Because there is no clearly reported whole-brain, within-group (adult) task map, this violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group/interaction effects without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an original, empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=51, ages 18–53) investigating social-related processing (affective speech comprehension; mentalizing/Theory-of-Mind strategies). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with voxelwise statistical maps, FWE-corrected results, activation coordinates, figures, and extensive methods/results/discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of whole-brain task-evoked activations relevant to the review objective.

This paper reports three empirical fMRI studies that examine persuasion (a social-cognitive/mentalizing process) during task performance, meeting the social-related task requirement. All participant samples are healthy adults (ages ~20, right-handed university samples), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and provides tables of coordinates and thresholding details (e.g., p < .001 uncorrected, 5-voxel extent) for persuasive > unpersuasive contrasts across studies, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present in the supplied content. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group task maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study (N=46 healthy adults, ages 18–31) investigating theory-of-mind/emotion/pain judgments—clear social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (univariate second-level analyses with SnPM cluster correction and MVPA results), with results described in text, figures, and tables. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (N=27, ages ~25), using task-based fMRI while participants viewed cooperative vs. affective social interactions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise statistics (FWE-corrected maps), tables of activation foci, figures, and ROI analyses. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (task fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets I3 (uses an fMRI task probing emotion processing/social cognition) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with reported results). It also provides whole-brain results in figures/tables (I6). However, the paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone; reported whole-brain maps are either a main effect across all subjects or between-group contrasts (siblings > controls). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Decision: EXCLUDED for E4; inclusion met: I3, I4, I6; inclusion not met: I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating animacy perception/social cognition using task-based fMRI. The sample comprises 15 healthy adults (mean age 26.6), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise coordinates and cluster-level inference (tables and figures), providing unmasked healthy-group task activation maps and coordinates. The methods, results and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social/identity-based task (rivalry fan memory task probing self-referential and social-cognitive processes such as perspective taking and mentalizing). Sample: 23 healthy adult males (mean ages ~20–22), within 18–65. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM random-effects contrasts; Tables and Figures show whole-brain activations and SVC/ROI follow-ups). Reporting of results includes whole-brain maps/tables consistent with inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not an only between-group contrast, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an fMRI study of emotional perspective taking (empathy) in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages ~24) using a task that explicitly probes social cognition (SELF- and OTHER-perspective on emotional faces). Group-level, whole-brain task contrasts are reported and thresholded (e.g., p<0.05 FWE-corrected for simple effects across the whole group; gender effects assessed within whole-group activated voxels with coordinates/tables provided). Results for the healthy adult sample are reported separately and include whole-brain voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinate/table reporting). No exclusion criteria are met.

The provided full text appears to be an abstract/summary lacking key methodological details. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used fMRI during a social-related task—self/other trait judgments and perspective taking). Inclusion criteria not confirmed (and therefore not met for purposes of inclusion): I4 (participant demographics/ages: healthy adult age range 18–65 not reported in the provided text), I5 (no explicit confirmation of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group in the provided content), I6 (reporting format cannot be verified from the excerpt). No exclusion criteria are clearly met (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Because all required inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete/fulltext provided, the study must be excluded from the review pending full-text verification.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (attachment/affiliation) using masked emotional faces, satisfying the review objective. Sample: 51 healthy adults (mean age 28.5), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (masked sad vs neutral; masked happy vs neutral) with statistical maps and coordinate tables and describes voxelwise regression analyses relating attachment avoidance to brain activation. Results are reported for a priori ROIs and whole-brain (FDR-corrected) findings in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age appropriate, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Experiments 1 and 2; ages within 19–32 and 20–30). It investigates social-action perception using task-based fMRI and representational similarity analyses. Group-level whole-brain searchlight RSA results and corrected cluster maps are reported (tables of coordinates and cluster-corrected maps), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social-related processing), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain results reported), and I6 (maps/coordinates clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of vocal emotion perception (a social-communication task), conducted in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–36). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., the voice localizer [vocal > non-vocal] producing TVA) and provides MNI coordinates from whole-brain analyses; results are presented as voxelwise contrasts (coordinates and statistical maps), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Although many main findings are reported with ROI small-volume correction, whole-brain contrasts (voice localizer) and voxelwise coordinates are provided and described. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical dfMRI fMRI study of face-to-face eye-contact (a social task) with healthy adult participants (19 pairs, ages 18–33 reported). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM group maps for tasks A and B, paired t-tests for exogenous/endogenous systems) with cluster results, probabilistic atlas labels, and coordinates (figures and Table 3). Tasks and contrasts are clearly described for the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (results reported via figures/tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study used an implicit emotional face discrimination task (social communication/perception), meeting I3. It includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=19, ages 18–51), meeting I4. The manuscript reports whole-brain, voxelwise task activation results (SPM2 analyses, FWE-corrected contrasts) and describes within-group t-maps/activations for control subjects (e.g., frontal and basal ganglia activations for fearful and neutral faces), satisfying I5. Results and maps are presented at the group level (tables/figures described), consistent with I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, healthy adults within range, and original empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study probing social processing (empathy and sympathy—perception and understanding of others) using a task-based paradigm. The sample includes healthy adult participants (ages up to 40) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (PCS–NPS and PCO–PCS) with thresholding and coordinate tables/figures and reports age-related whole-brain correlation analyses; results for the healthy participants are clearly presented. Reporting includes coordinates and figures (whole-brain maps) and statistical thresholds (FDR). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it is complete for screening purposes.

This study reports an fMRI task (multiround trust game) probing social interaction (benevolence/malevolence) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and analyses. A healthy adult control group (n=21, age range 18–47) is reported separately. The Methods and Results explicitly describe whole-brain, voxelwise thresholds and present group maps for the healthy group (e.g., Figure 2A) and second-level analyses. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group reported), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps for the healthy group), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self/other/reflected evaluations) using task-based fMRI (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult group (N=19 adults, ages 22–31) reported separately alongside adolescents (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task analyses (2×4×3 repeated-measures ANOVA) with voxel-wise and cluster correction and reports significant whole-brain effects and clusters (meets I5). Adult-specific analyses and results are described, and separate analyses for each age group are referenced in the Supplementary Materials, satisfying the allowance for results in supplements (meets I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplements referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses a social cognition task (mental simulation of personally familiar others), satisfying I3. Participants were healthy adults (n=25 recruited; 23 analyzed; ages 18–27), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight RSA, random-effects t tests, corrected maps; figures and Table 1 list peak voxels and clusters), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting only, not between-group-only contrasts, not outside age range, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study of socio-emotional conflict processing using naturalistic film stimuli (social-related task). Participants were healthy adults (n=25 analyzed; mean age 26.3), within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (mixed-effects group regressions, voxelwise z>2.3, cluster-corrected P<0.05) and conjunction/PPI results; results are reported in the text, tables and figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported for the healthy group), and I6 (results reported in standard formats). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective: (1) It uses functional MRI during a social-related task (an emotional face‑matching task targeting perception of others’ emotions). (2) The sample consists of healthy adults (n=98; ages 18–30). (3) The authors report group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory unmasked whole-brain activation results and whole-brain PPI results are reported with tables/figures referenced as Tables S1/S2 and corresponding figures). (4) Whole‑brain results are presented in figures/tables and clearly described as coming from the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core article content appears complete). The study also reports ROI and connectivity analyses, but these are accompanied by whole‑brain task activation maps, so no exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore I recommend INCLUDING this study.

The paper reports an fMRI face-processing task (fearful faces) addressing social cognition, includes a separate healthy adult control group (N=13, age 25.6 mean), and provides group-level, within-group whole-brain task activation results for the control group (main effect of faces and linear contrasts reported with tables/figures). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM99, random effects) with reported control-group activations (e.g., bilateral amygdala, IOG, MPFC), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group task map. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion so is complete. No exclusion criteria (only ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation (Social-Reg) using a psychotherapist-based task, meeting the review objective of social-related processing. Sample: healthy adults (n=22 females, ages 22–32) within 18–65. Whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts are reported (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures of activations. Thus I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI with a social-related task (implicit facial emotion processing) and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper focuses on PPI effective connectivity and between-group contrasts (patient vs control) and reports the connectivity differences; the amygdala seed was localized using a control-group peak within an amygdala mask (not a reported whole-brain control map). Therefore it meets I3 and I4 but does not meet I5, and it violates exclusion criteria E3 (only effective connectivity reported without healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of allocentric social hierarchy and social-alliance judgments (social-related tasks), conducted in healthy adults (n=22 males, mean age 24.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects SPM analyses (p<0.05 FWE corrected; extent threshold 30 voxels) with activation tables and SPM figures/coordinates described in the text and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study is an fMRI investigation but does not meet the review’s population or task criteria. It uses a non-social visual attention task (not a social-related task) and the samples are boys (children/adolescents), not healthy adults aged 18–65. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of social-affiliative/attachment processing: mothers viewed dynamic video vignettes of their own vs stranger infants (task is social/affiliative). Participants are healthy adult mothers (ages 22–37), with groups defined but healthy-group results reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (own infant > stranger infant) with figures and tables, and ROI/functional connectivity analyses supplementing whole-brain results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=21 for fMRI) that investigates episodic retrieval of socially encoded life events and bodily self-perception (social interaction and perception/understanding of self). The paper reports group-level task-evoked activations during retrieval (baseline contrasts and whole-brain activations in retrosplenial cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, temporal pole, left angular gyrus; see Fig. 3B and Table S1), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. Participants are healthy adults with no neurological/psychiatric history. The social-related task (encoding and retrieval of real-life social interactions and bodily self perspective) fits the review’s constructs. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 (and I6 as reporting format is acceptable) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of cross-modal person recognition in healthy adults (ages 20–31) using task-based scans, satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper reports results primarily from ROI-based analyses (FWE-corrected within ROIs) and explicitly notes no significant whole-brain (unmasked) results at P<0.05 FWE; no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy group is reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task map reported). Full text appears complete.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related cognitive empathy (emotional perspective-taking) task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=24; ages 18–50) reported separately (I4). It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but these are presented as between-group contrasts (schizophrenia vs control) and clusters derived from group-difference maps; the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map (main effect or within-group contrast) explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails I5. Exclusion criterion E4 is met: only between-group contrasts are reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used task-based fMRI during an interpersonal/social task (imaginary sentence completion with mother/father conditions), meeting the social-processing requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=15; mean age 28.2) with results reported separately. The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain, group-level one-sample t-tests for each group (FDR-corrected clusters) and provides coordinates/tables of activations for the control group (see Table 2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social cognition (judgments about self, close others, and strangers) using task-based functional MRI across four experiments. Sample: 98 healthy adults (mean age 20.7) — satisfies healthy adult sample. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and whole-brain maps (e.g., self > other, friends > strangers) thresholded at p<0.001 and described in text/figures, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of a social appraisal task (preference judgments of faces) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=21). The manuscript provides whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (PREF>GENDER) and maps/tables presented for each group (figures and tables show within-group activations and contrasts for controls), using random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly identified in the text, figures and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables and described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses a social-related task (dynamic investigator feedback) to probe processing of negative social evaluation. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=21 males, ages 21–39). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (negative social feedback > positive social feedback) with random-effects second-level analyses and corrected statistical thresholds; results are presented in tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of pgACC functional connectivity related to autistic traits in neurotypical adults. While the sample consists of healthy adults (I4 satisfied), the study does not use a task-based fMRI paradigm nor report task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Instead it reports seed-based resting-state connectivity analyses (group-level connectivity maps), which fall under exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only resting-state or seed-based connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Therefore it fails to meet I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) and I5 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates social-affective processing (compassion/empathy) using the Socio-Affective Video Task (SoVT), meeting the review objective. Sample: 94 healthy adult female participants aged 18–35, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (e.g., HE vs LE videos; parametric modulations) with results described in text, figures, and tables and corrected for whole-brain FWE (and SVC for ROIs), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present in the provided text and appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (face/emotion processing) and includes a healthy adult control group, but the provided full text does not clearly present an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map specifically from the healthy/control group. Results focus on PPI (seed-based) connectivity and group differences; task activation details are referenced as being in supplementary material but a clear healthy-group whole-brain map is not reported in the main text. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) is not met, triggering exclusion under E4 (between-group contrasts / connectivity reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This is an fMRI study of face perception/recognition, which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Experiment 1 uses fMRI in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~23–25 across experiments), meeting the sample criterion. The authors performed group-level voxelwise analyses (mixed effects FLAME) to derive group patterns and used an independent group localizer (n=83) to define whole-brain ROIs (faces vs scrambled faces), satisfying the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map. Results are reported across visual field regions and face-selective regions and behavioral tasks linking to neural data. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. I have moderate-high confidence because the paper emphasizes MVPA/ROI analyses, but it explicitly describes group-level whole-brain GLM (FLAME) maps and an independent whole-brain localizer used to define ROIs.

The study includes a social-related fMRI task (facial expression discrimination) and reports data from a healthy adult control group, but it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The manuscript reports between-group (patient vs. control) contrasts (showing patient amygdala hyperactivation) and focuses on connectivity and between-group differences; I cannot identify a standalone whole-brain healthy-group task effect map or coordinates. Therefore Exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study meets inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social rejection) (I3); includes a healthy adult participant group (16 adult females within the adult age range) (I4); reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (exclusion>inclusion and inclusion>exclusion) analyzed in SPM with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/coordinates/figures (I5, I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply. Note: some analyses focus on age comparisons and some adult-specific post-hoc tests used SVC, but whole-brain task-evoked maps from the healthy participant sample are reported, supporting inclusion in the meta-analysis of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI task study examining perception/understanding of self (detection of visual feedback ownership), which falls under social-related constructs (Perception and Understanding of Self). It used healthy adult participants (n=15 after exclusion; ages 20–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps and their comparisons) analyzed in SPM2 with reported cluster- and voxel-wise thresholds and tables/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates emotion recognition from dynamic avatars (a social perception task—perception/understanding of others), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age ~28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses and presents multi-subject activation maps and cluster-corrected contrasts (emotional > neutral, parametric maps), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task effects. Methods, results, and discussion are provided in full. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18–24) that investigates social-related processing (mentalizing/social cognition and self-related processing) during an article-reading/sharing task. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (exploratory whole-brain searches, maps, and tables; see SI Fig. S3 and Table S5) linking task-evoked activation to population-level virality, clearly derived from the healthy control participant samples. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related task/constructs), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/SI). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of joint attention (social cognition) with a task manipulating initiating and responding to joint attention, meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample comprises healthy adults (final N=13, Mage=24.85), satisfying the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (RJA−RJAc, IJA−IJAc, conjunctions, and contrasts), FDR-corrected statistical maps, tables of coordinates and figures, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy/control group are reported clearly and not limited to a subgroup. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The full text reports task-based fMRI during a social/empathic paradigm assessing emotional egocentricity (social-related processing). Samples are healthy adult participants (multiple independent samples of right-handed female undergraduates, ages consistent with 18–65). Group-level, whole-brain task contrasts and peak coordinates are reported (interaction contrasts, MNI coordinates, tables/figures); exploratory whole-brain analyses were performed in fMRI1 and group-level results from fMRI2 are reported with coordinate-based results and SVC. The paper includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (rapid fearful face processing), satisfying I3. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group (n=25) reported separately from the ASD group, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (see Supplementary Fig. S1 and Supplementary Table 1 and whole-brain FLAME analyses described in Methods/Results), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary whole-brain results, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy maps, participants are adults, and it is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not include a healthy adult sample (all participants are adolescents aged 12–18), violating inclusion criterion I4 and exclusion criterion E5. Additionally, the paper reports mainly between-group whole-brain contrasts (e.g., control > ASC, control > sibling) rather than an unmasked, within-group whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; thus it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing—the Eyes task). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 absent), I5 (no clear healthy-group whole-brain task map reported). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion rationale: This study reports only task-state functional connectivity and ROI/seed-based voxelwise connectivity analyses without presenting any unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (exclusion E3). It therefore fails to provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation evidence (I5 not met). Additionally, the fMRI task used is an episodic memory old/new recognition paradigm rather than an explicit social-related task (I3 not met). The sample comprises older adults with aMCI and age-matched controls drawn from an aging population; no clear evidence that the healthy/control group falls in the 18–65 age range is reported, so I4 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: none (inclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Exclusion criteria applied: ["E3"]. Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind) using Sally–Anne style movies, meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample comprises healthy adults (mean age 24.4, final N=22), meeting the age and health inclusion. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM for the explicit general-belief localizer (false-belief vs false-photograph) thresholded at q(FDR)<0.05 with Talairach peak coordinates and a whole-brain map (Figure 2A), satisfying the whole-brain task-evoked result requirement. Results are reported in text, figures and coordinate tables. Although ROI analyses were used for the implicit task, the presence of the whole-brain localizer map means the study is not limited to ROI-only reporting. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task fMRI study in healthy adult participants that investigates social communication/mentalizing. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=18, ages 19–28). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (univariate contrasts, searchlight MVPA and MVCA) with cluster-level inference; results are presented in figures and tables. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used an explicit facial emotion identification task (socially relevant: perception/understanding of others) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group maps and contrasts. A healthy control group of adults (n=22, mean age 31.7) is included and analyzed separately (HC one-sample ‘faces minus animals’ contrast; figures and tables present HC activation and coordinates; analyses FDR-corrected at whole-brain level). Full methods, results, and group-level maps/tables are provided in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participant ages within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is suitable for the review objective of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using natural interpersonal touch (social-related task) in healthy adults (n=8, ages 22–39). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise ICA spatial maps (group-average ICs thresholded at z=2.5) that are task-related and presented in figures and described in the text; they also report event-related averages of IC time courses tied to the task. Thus the paper provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps (presented as ICA component maps) and meets the review inclusion criteria. Although ICA was used, the components were identified as stimulus-related and accompanied by task-locked analyses, so exclusion E3 does not apply.

Full text appears incomplete: only metadata and references are provided (no Introduction, Methods, Results, or Discussion). Cannot verify key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none can be confirmed from the provided content. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I3 (uncertain whether a task-based fMRI social-related task is reported in the available text), I4 (sample details for healthy adults not provided in the provided content), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or coordinate tables are present in the provided content). Exclusion criteria met: none explicitly met based on available content. Recommendation: obtain full article PDF/full text to reassess.
