Although this fMRI study uses a social-related task (self/other evaluation with perspective-taking) and includes a healthy adult control group (TD adults reported separately), the full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Most reported voxelwise results are either between-group contrasts (ASD vs TD) or combined-group analyses, and ROI/seed-based follow-ups are presented for the TD group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 and I4 but does not meet I5; it thus falls under exclusion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interaction results without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This paper meets the meta-analysis criteria: it uses task-based fMRI probing social-related constructs (self-referential processing and perspective-taking), includes a healthy control group with reported within-group whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps (e.g., left VMPFC/MOFC and right lingual gyrus reported for HC), and provides whole-brain group-level statistical contrasts and thresholding information. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling verification of analyses and healthy-group effects. Therefore it satisfies I3, I5, and I6. The healthy control group is reported and appears to be adult (age distribution matched to UHR youth sample), satisfying I4 based on provided demographics and analyses reporting. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or absence of healthy-group whole-brain maps) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly examines neural responses to romantic (affiliation/attachment) and sexual stimuli. It satisfies I3: uses task-based fMRI for social-related (romantic/affiliation) processing; I4: sample includes healthy adults aged 22–50 (n=20); I5: reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task contrasts (within-group and between-group contrasts, random-effects FLAME, cluster correction) and presents tables/figures of whole-brain results; I6: results are reported in figures/tables and described in text. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects, ages within 18–65, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study using a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (e.g., CC vs CD contrasts; whole-brain maps thresholded and corrected, and comparisons across groups) that are clearly derived from the healthy/control sample. Results are reported in the main text and supplementary materials. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (results clearly described in text/figures/tables) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI probing social-emotional processing (fearful/calm faces) (I3); includes a healthy adult control group (mean age ~39.8) reported separately (I4); reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts for the control (healthy) group with tables and figures describing voxelwise activation (I5,I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results (within-group whole-brain maps for controls), and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study).

This empirical fMRI study used a social-evaluative task (E.Vids) presenting positive, negative, and neutral social-interaction videos and measured BOLD responses. The sample comprises 37 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.8), satisfying the healthy adult inclusion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (positive>neutral, negative>neutral, conjunction), with FWE-corrected results, tables of coordinates and figures, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study directly examines visual perspective-taking (theory-of-mind/social perception) using a task-based fMRI paradigm in healthy adult participants (N=16, mean age 22.4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other) with cluster-level FWE correction, tables/figures of activations and coordinates, and full methods/results/discussion sections. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete. Recommended for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using an approach-avoidance task with explicit social and nonsocial stimuli (social positive vs nonsocial positive, etc.), meeting the review focus on social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (N=76 final; males aged ~21), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports voxelwise neuroimaging results with MNI coordinates and describes exploratory whole-brain analyses (thresholds and cluster reporting), and presents group-level statistical maps/peak coordinates from healthy participants (including main effects and contrasts), so whole-brain task-evoked evidence is available. Reported analyses include anatomically defined ROIs with small-volume correction but also whole-brain exploratory results and reported peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (theory of mind / social-exchange vs precautionary reasoning) using the Wason selection task. Participants were healthy adults (20 recruited, 12 analyzed; mean age 24.6), satisfying the age and sample requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (story and card contrasts), thresholding, clusters, and MNI/coordinate data (e.g., x=62,y=-10,z=-22), with tables and figures of activations. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text, so the full text appears complete for screening. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial emotion discrimination (a social cognition task: perception/understanding of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=12) matched to the clinical group and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and maps identified for control subjects (within-group contrasts such as emotion>baseline and sad>neutral are described and illustrated). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adults and reports unmasked whole-brain healthy-group effects).

This study reports resting-state fMRI data (n=20 healthy adults) and uses meta-analytic coactivation mapping (MACM) for functional characterization, but it does not present original task-based fMRI data from healthy adults performing a social-related task nor report group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Exclusion ID met: E3 (reports resting-state analyses/MACM without original healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (healthy adult sample reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, but the study design does not meet task-activation requirements for this meta-analysis.

Exclusion met: E4. The paper reports between-group contrasts and conjunctions showing diagnosis effects (patient vs control) but does not present an unmasked, whole‑brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (no standalone healthy-group whole-brain task effect or table/figure of within-group healthy activations is reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (BOLD fMRI during social-related tasks: Theory of Mind and affective empathy), I4 (includes a healthy adult control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude under E4.

The study includes an fMRI task probing social cognition (RMET) and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps for healthy participants, but the healthy participant group is older adults aged 51–84 (M=68.40) and thus not within the meta-analysis age range of 18–65. No separate healthy adult subgroup within 18–65 is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample aged 18–65). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (group-level whole-brain healthy-group task activation map reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a theory-of-mind (social cognition) task (satisfies I3). The sample comprises 109 healthy adult participants (healthy volunteers; satisfies I4). The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain task contrast (ToM>control) across all healthy subjects with whole-brain correction (P<0.01 FWE) and presents tables/figures of these results (satisfies I5 and I6). The full text supplied includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete for core article content (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, age-out-of-range-only, or non-empirical issues).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (emotion recognition with eye-gaze) using a task that probes perception/understanding of others, satisfying I3. It includes a healthy younger adult group (reported ages 17–27, mean 20.65) that clearly represents healthy adults within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (PLS) with peak coordinates and figures/tables, satisfying I5 and acceptable reporting formats per I6. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and includes an analyzable healthy adult group). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of healthy adult fMRI studies of social processing.

This is a task-based fMRI study of face processing in healthy young adults (I3 met) drawn from a population cohort in their 20s (I4 met). However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. The analyses are ROI-based interregional correlation (task-evoked connectivity) and structural covariance rather than whole-brain voxelwise activation results. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Exclusion criteria E2 applies (only ROI/connectivity analyses with no whole-brain results) and E3 also applies (reports task-based interregional connectivity without accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Because a required inclusion criterion (I5) is not satisfied and exclusion criteria E2/E3 are met, the study must be excluded from the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (imitation/observation of communicative gestures), reporting whole-brain, group-level task contrasts and peak coordinates with cluster correction. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=20 analysed; mean age 24.6), within the 18–65 range. The paper presents full methods, results (whole-brain contrasts, tables/figures), and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult control participants (n=59 across three studies) performing social-related tasks (person knowledge; socially relevant concept words), satisfying the review topic. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (social > non-social; thresholds, cluster-correction, and peak coordinates are provided), and whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. The healthy-control groups are reported separately from any patient groups. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Note: the manuscript does not state explicit participant ages, so I assign moderate confidence that the sample falls within 18–65, but participants are described as healthy adult controls. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (inferring others’ social emotions/beliefs) and includes a healthy adult control group (matched typically developing males aged ~30), so I3 and I4 are met. However, the manuscript reports primarily between-group contrasts (typically developing > ASD) and ROI-based follow-up analyses; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., no standalone healthy-group whole-brain task effect is reported in the text/tables/figures provided). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it used task-based fMRI during a social joint-attention interaction (I3); it includes a healthy adult sample (HC-HC pairs; ages within 18–65) reported separately from clinical groups (I4); the manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task analyses and contrasts involving the healthy-control group (HC-HC [INT>NoINT]) with whole-brain inference (I5); whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/tables are indicated as available (I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.
